The bare source name `geomycin` cannot be assigned to oxytetracycline from its MeSH trade-name synonym alone. The current `data/ingredients/mapped/Geomycin.yaml` uses `mesh:D010118` / Oxytetracycline, with an OLS exact-synonym lookup as the promotion evidence. Its existing native mapping disposition is already WITHHOLD. Preserve that hold.

Primary literature establishes a competing historical sense: [Brockmann and Musso, 1954, Geomycin II](https://doi.org/10.1002/cber.19540871128), abstract, describes a Streptomyces xanthophaeus antibiotic preparation with separable A/B/C/D components. This is positive evidence of name ambiguity, not a reason to choose one component or identify the source with that preparation. [MeSH D010118](https://id.nlm.nih.gov/mesh/D010118) supplies the oxytetracycline sense. Both must be considered.

The frozen campaign contains two distinct cases for `kgmicrobe.compound:geomycin`, from metatraits and gtdb-metatraits. In `audit_campaign_accounting_v1.py`, the owner-conflict loop indexes both `defaultdict` objects for every path in their union. Those reads create empty entries in the other category. Later counts and serialized inventories therefore describe the union as both categories.

The frozen Worker 1 draft has 32 distinct referenced owner paths and 17 distinct proposed owner paths, with 8 shared paths (union 41). The current report incorrectly gives 41 for both counts. These are owner paths, not distinct chemical identities or accepted curation changes.

body:
Independent read-only review of the native EdgeMech adapter branch found an incomplete durability barrier in `scripts/adhoc/run_edge_adapter_canary_20261107.py`, lines 80–87.

The publisher fsyncs `assertions.jsonl` and `manifest.json`, then renames their parent directory into place. It does not fsync the staged directory or the final output's parent directory. File fsync alone does not guarantee durability of the directory entries created and renamed during publication. A crash after reported success can therefore lose the visible generation or its manifest entry.

Fsync the staged directory before publication and the destination parent after publication, or apply an equivalent durable manifest-last protocol. Add a focused fault-injection/order test that establishes the publication marker is created only after persisted payload verification and that the relevant directories are flushed before success is returned. Retain failures without overwriting user data.

This is in scope for the immutable native export publisher in CLAW #767. It does not change native review status or authorize any scientific claim.
title: Fsync native assertion directory entries before reporting publication success

body:
Independent read-only review of the native EdgeMech adapter branch found a publication race in `scripts/adhoc/run_edge_adapter_canary_20261107.py`, lines 83–85.

The publisher checks whether the output exists, then calls `stage.rename(args.output)`. On POSIX systems, renaming a directory can replace an existing empty destination directory. If another writer or user creates the destination after the check and before rename, this operation can replace that directory despite the documented refusal to replace existing output.

Use an exclusive publication protocol, such as atomically reserving the destination and publishing a verified manifest last with exclusive file creation. Do not rely on an existence check immediately before a replacing rename. Add a focused collision-injection test that creates the destination in the interval and verifies the original destination survives and the export is not reported as published.

This is in scope for the native publisher in CLAW #767. The reviewed mapping payload and inherited-review interpretation were otherwise preserved; this finding concerns publication, not scientific approval.

# Separate shared curation contracts from the full orchestration dependency

The native EdgeMech adapter for CLAW #767 needs only the canonical
`kg_microbe_curation` identity and native-assertion validators. A direct optional
dependency on the full `kg-microbe-orchestration` distribution cannot resolve:

- MediaIngredientMech `pyproject.toml` requires `linkml>=1.7.0,<1.10` and

- CLAW commit `1b5391d083ba85ac94e5279c3cba25ac4fde243c` requires

The bounds have no overlap, including when the dependency is placed in a
native optional extra, because uv resolves all extras into the shared lock.

In-scope mitigation: pin the exact CLAW source revision in native metadata,
verify its Git identity and import origin, and run a dedicated mandatory
integration tier using only that source path and the existing native runtime.
No native LinkML upgrade is included in the adapter PR.

Follow-up: expose the minimal shared identity/review/curation contracts as a
separately installable distribution with explicit small dependencies and
cross-package conformance tests. This requires coordinated CLAW packaging
work and should remain open after the native adapter's source-pin mitigation.

Primary source evidence identifies G6501 as an isomeric hydrate mixture; its record carries the structure of one water-free positional isomer. That chemistry assertion needs correction. Whether two existing source owners denote the same material remains a separate identity decision.

Fresh-main validation and live issue deduplication are complete: Step 7c merge `467aa319a06ef992035f509f66fe251082b44ae1`; main `467aa319a06ef992035f509f66fe251082b44ae1`, checked `2026-11-03T00:31:09.269512+00:00`; record/hash and mapping-status comparison `all 67 selected source hashes and the named mapping decisions unchanged`; live deduplication `All-state G6501, exact CAS and owner queries returned zero hits; all six glycerophosphate matches and their full discussions were reviewed, with no dedicated duplicate.`. No record, merge or approval change is included in this finding.

At C5 `9a8414ad88bbbb01c2a43995e3f0decb2e7f2a7e`, `data/ingredients/mapped/Glycerol_Phosphate_Disodium_Salt_Hydrate.yaml` had SHA256 `34a148f0b60690558fc0aa0970a93b619fd340e057a3e07e490000b94d3859bc`, primary `cas:55073-41-1`, type `SINGLE_INGREDIENT`, and formula/InChI/SMILES for one water-free positional isomer. Its original CultureBotHT row specifies Sigma G6501, glycerol phosphate disodium salt hydrate and CAS 55073-41-1. The source's mass 216.04 is the dry-compound basis, not evidence of whole-hydrate stoichiometry.

[GSRS RCS9EQ01V4](https://gsrs.ncats.nih.gov/api/v1/substances/RCS9EQ01V4?view=full) identifies CAS 55073-41-1 as a mixture with required sodium 2-glycerophosphate pentahydrate and sodium 1-glycerophosphate hexahydrate components. It links [NCIT:C120561 Sodium Glycerophosphate](https://api-evsrest.nci.nih.gov/api/v1/concept/ncit/C120561?include=full), whose synonyms include the disodium salt hydrate. The successful [Sigma-Aldrich depositor capture, PubChem SID24895257](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/rest/pug/substance/sid/24895257/JSON), version 6, source `G6501_SIGMA`, explicitly calls the product an isomeric mixture. Response SHA256: `229b66301e98e2ea1a4b8fc032121244c80376c398a9d31e45759c0be917937a`. The direct supplier HTML request timed out; that failure is preserved separately and is not supplier-page verification.

The single water-free positional structure is therefore unsupported as exact chemistry for this source material. This extends #321's missing-hydrate-number concern and #268's enrichment-mechanism concern. It does not establish fixed bulk water content or justify averaging component hydrates into a formula.

At the inspected snapshot, `Sodium_glycerophosphate.yaml` already owned NCIT:C120561 with a SUPPORTED mapping, CultureMech provenance and counts 25/25. G6501 had counts 0/0 and two WITHHOLD mappings. Shared CAS/ontology metadata warrants comparison of the source boundaries; it does not authorize merging, moving occurrences or inheriting support. Recommend a guarded correction that removes the unsupported whole-mixture structural assertion or scopes it accurately, preserving the record and historical chemistry in its audit trail. Resolve shared identity and supplied-form sufficiency separately. Preserve the provisional carbon-source role and native holds; leave #1053's raw pentahydrate objects and #1020's corrected 2-phosphate record unchanged.

Historical deduplication covered #901, #268, #669, #321, #459, #296, #1020, #1053 and #1005, plus structured and semantic holds. All-state searches for the owner name, glycerophosphate, CAS 55073-41-1 and G6501 found no dedicated catalogue-mixture chemistry issue. This was a bounded search; the fresh live result above likewise found no dedicated duplicate. Findings `SEM:d5e18debeee10a3a9cfe` and `SEM:e22f4ed68806ce354630` concerned the older narrative and provisional role and remained OPEN in the preflight.

Evidence SHA256 values: GSRS `930bfa931206f64225a94fa9aaeee12240f217f918b3f59551fb5dc531b2ff33`; NCIt `8f36309df9aae2aa5f10857cffce7184c0fb0632f536761fa8f619b7c44dd5e8`; catalogue CSV `76b70a1836b25de431c4f5cc27c72bb6b06a223ce33911e93b7681d4fcdb28f9`. The CSV was historically captured as an untracked source file from the CultureBotHT checkout at revision `1f27c43b1d5c7d15c08b45fc675d91b6ee938371`; it is not claimed to be a Git blob at that revision.

Completion requires a source-boundary ruling before identity edits, guarded provenance-preserving changes, synchronized source/SSSOM/export and receipt checks, preservation of the supported owner's authority unless explicitly superseded, and independent final-head review. The unified snapshot and its budget remain outside this finding.

body:
Independent review found a safety defect in the **uncommitted, standalone cleanup helper prepared for this thread**. It is outside PR #1106's tracked source. Neither its production verification nor cleanup mode was executed, and no real branch was affected. The user required stopping on any failure, so #1106 was removed from the merge queue and remains unmerged.

The helper constructs this transaction at `cleanup_owned_branch.py:268`:

```text
option no-deref
start
delete refs/heads/OWNED EXPECTED_HEAD
delete refs/remotes/origin/OWNED EXPECTED_HEAD
prepare
commit
```

The stdin `option no-deref` protects only the next command naming a ref. If the second tracking ref becomes a symbolic ref to an unrelated branch at the same expected OID after the earlier symbolic-ref check, its deletion follows that target. The intermediate inventory compares names and resolved OIDs, so it does not detect this substitution. The exact transaction returned zero in an isolated fixture and deleted the unrelated branch; the tracking symref remained dangling. The later inventory detects the damage only after deletion.

The reproduction deliberately injects a race outside the helper README's coordinator-exclusivity assumption. That limitation does not make the intended no-dereference guard effective. This is a confirmed unsafe property of the prepared helper, not evidence that any concurrent session changed a real ref.

Preserved evidence under `output/approved-plan-20261101T031134Z/step7b-exception-20261102/cleanup-preparation/`:

- Frozen helper SHA256: `5c013cd59968d4bac27e06442bb8affc8a2523e4c4cbc45f68d03f97758cc65f`.
- Independent review `independent-review/review.json`: `dc6b80de8c2634c5d198a5ed7ba5132ee7c547297a92b6bd4860357438a48ca6`.
- Reproduction `independent-review/symbolic-tracking-results.json`: `cb3a08abf4fc4dfd2bd1a9f9e531e1e820c6d5c0d44ef3d11e38de1872a2e388`.
- Actual fixture commands `independent-review/symbolic-tracking-commands.json`: `8cf0ca5c171701659624f3384a213684a5a482bb0f6dfe1746d67e49d61582f3`.

Before any reuse, protect every deletion against dereferencing and independently reproduce the symbolic-substitution case with all unrelated refs preserved. No repair has been applied, and the frozen helper must not be executed. Any repair and resumed closure need a new reviewed execution decision; this issue does not authorize changing #1106, its tests, gates, approved snapshot pair, or scientific holdings.

PR #1106's head remains `6372aca7eaa9d2863d01aef3a778334709a89aaf`. Its exact-pair review, local QC/full suite and all sixteen PR CI checks passed before this separate cleanup review. Queue completion, squash merge, branch deletion and Step 7c are not claimed.
title: Prepared PR #1106 cleanup helper can delete an unrelated branch through a symbolic tracking ref

body:
The user identified a substance distinction requiring a separate owner-assignment review: **Tryptone is not Casamino acids**, yet the unified row `Tryptone Peptone (Difco 0123-17)` currently inherits the Casamino-acids owner through `FOODON:03315719`.

This issue records that unresolved assignment. **Do not fix it in #1106.** The one-time two-file unified-snapshot exception for #1106 preserves this inherited owner/identity assignment; it does not approve the assignment scientifically or authorize a record merge or replacement identity.

### Verified current behavior

Read-only inspection and native owner-resolution replay used MIM `2ed2804b9f787e354188b69284097c6af03b3409`, isolated Claw `33be66ab1b993e2a47792c13daa3e4f39635f2cb`, and CultureMech `a74dd489720c9df96cc073ffd11568d407d3c06c`.

- `UNIFIED_INGREDIENT_MAPPING.tsv`, line 1696: ingredient label `Tryptone Peptone (Difco 0123-17)`, 3 occurrences, `mim_id=FOODON:03315719`, `culturemech_term_id=FOODON:03315719`, `cas_rn=65072-00-6`, and a Casamino-acids synonym payload. The CAS is reported as inherited output here, not independently validated for this catalog product.
- The actual C4 regenerated candidate (SHA256 `1edaba0f0f2d1afb84129a2ba185963a2cdf3e9b982690fdfd610df1fd78cc88`) retains that assignment. Its only change to this row is clearing the stale `kg_microbe_node_id=CHEBI:78020`.
- The native resolver selects **`data/ingredients/mapped/Casamino_Acids.yaml`**, preferred term `Casamino acids`. The exact catalog label has no entry in MIM's published label index and no name-index answer; the resolver falls back to the `FOODON:03315719` ontology index. That index uses the first loaded owner for a shared identifier.
- Both `Casamino_Acids.yaml` and `Casein_Peptone.yaml` hold `FOODON:03315719` with `CLOSE_MATCH` mappings to `mammalian milk protein (hydrolyzed)`. The former's existing curation evidence describes acid-hydrolyzed casein; the latter's evidence describes enzymatic/tryptic/pancreatic casein hydrolysate. A shared parent term is not evidence that these source owners or products are interchangeable.

The three CultureMech source records retain the exact catalog label and local `term.id=FOODON:03315719`:

| CultureMech ID | Normalized source path | Recorded source |
|---|---|---|
| `CultureMech:006494` | `data/normalized_yaml/bacterial/for_dsm_16260.yaml` | KOMODO Medium 78b.1; 0.15 g/L |
| `CultureMech:006495` | `data/normalized_yaml/bacterial/for_dsm_16369.yaml` | KOMODO Medium 78b.2; 0.15 g/L |
| `CultureMech:006496` | `data/normalized_yaml/bacterial/KOMODO_78b_medium_FOR_TREPONEMA_PARVUM.yaml` | KOMODO Medium 78b; 0.16 g/L |

CultureMech's current `output/ingredient_occurrences.tsv` records all three as `local_fallback`, with the explanation `label not found in pinned MIM index; retained local identity`. Its aggregate groups this label under `Casein peptone`, while the unified MIM fallback selects `Casamino acids`. This is a source-owner question, not a reason to silently choose either record.

### Required evidence-based follow-up

1. Verify the exact Difco `0123-17` product and source-recipe wording against primary manufacturer/catalog and recipe evidence; establish the supplied material and preparation distinction under `MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md` section 3.
2. Review the CultureMech local annotation, the two distinct MIM source owners sharing the broad FOODON term, and the identifier fallback behavior together. Determine whether this label has an adequately supported existing owner, needs a distinct record/identity, or should remain explicitly unresolved.
3. Recommend and independently review a bounded correction before applying it. Do not infer an exact identity from the shared FOODON parent, CAS, a similar commercial name, or loader order; do not merge records without the required evidence.
4. Any future change must preserve the raw catalog label and provenance, use guarded writers, synchronize maintained surfaces, regenerate affected products, and run the required tests/QC. It belongs in a separate change after the present #1106 scope.

### Prior decisions and duplicate check

# Strict OLS client accepts mixed Unicode digits in a ChEBI identifier

Severity: low. This is a public client input-validation inconsistency; no unsafe automatic record mutation was observed.

The frozen `src/mediaingredientmech/utils/chemical_properties_client.py` at SHA256 `1a17480273f9deb2cf28dac73137d3e5411987f93d0241843c2cbd1b5491dc75`, line 147, validates requested identifiers using `re.fullmatch(r"CHEBI:[1-9]\d*", ontology_id)`. Python's `\d` includes non-ASCII decimal digits. Thus the malformed identifier `CHEBI:1２` (ASCII 1 followed by full-width 2) passes this supposedly strict ChEBI boundary.

A mocked direct call makes one provider request for an encoded IRI ending `CHEBI_1%25EF%25BC%2592`. When the synthetic response consistently echoes this malformed identifier and IRI, the client returns an `OlsChemicalProperties` envelope. The exact response parsing, hash, and other identity fields are otherwise consistent; this does not assert that any such term exists at the actual provider. The expected behavior is refusal before a request for a non-ASCII ChEBI identifier, matching the canonical `[1-9][0-9]*` contract already used by the record-aware guard.

Containment was also executed: `chemistry_preflight` and `prepare_chemical_properties` return `OWN_IDENTITY_MISMATCH` for the same mapped single-ingredient fixture, with zero property-provider calls. Consequently, this finding does not establish a path to an automatic chemistry write through the maintained guard/callers.

Suggested bounded fix: change the strict client regex to ASCII digits and add a no-request regression covering a mixed full-width digit and another Unicode decimal digit. Preserve the existing exact-identity checks and legacy retrieval behavior.

The new explicit form-review consumer developed for #1070 accepts the wrong historical claim as a retained row’s prior evidence basis. This finding concerns the unmerged `fix/melezitose-form-review-901-20261101` branch; no scientific source correction or production form authority has been applied.

Reproduction: a valid native scientific three-claim fixture changes the parent decision’s `prior_basis.evidence_key` to the same owner’s CAS identity entry. `check_prior` accepts that entry because its owner, subject, row digest and some historical endpoint match, without requiring the correct parent claim slot. `tests/test_form_mapping_followup.py::test_prior_parent_basis_cannot_be_replaced_by_same_owner_cas_claim` fails with DID NOT RAISE. The native scientific pair remains valid; the demonstrated defect is incorrect historical evidence attribution.

Evidence: `output/approved-plan-20261101T031134Z/logs/melezitose-form-prior-slot-probe.log`, SHA-256 `26bae803193d62ffe3a5330d1d521ac803bc3338a873a4fe71e3470d547c571b`. Independent adversarial boundary review is also examining endpoint/owner correspondence.

Required repair: bind immutable prior evidence to the correct retained claim slot and its exact historical endpoint/owner context. Preserve native three-claim assessment, receipt carry safeguards and old exact-only follow-ups. Add negative regression tests, rerun focused tests and obtain independent re-review before production application. No approval is granted by a receipt or prior evidence copy.
title: Bind form-review prior evidence to its actual historical claim slot

body:
The approved #901 continuation needs three separately assessed mapping claims for a CAS-primary supplied form: its own CAS identity, a broad form-of parent, and the native B1 registry handle required by MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md section 3. The strict approval-free supersession path landed in #1068 (`e568dbf0e0f759431ed317b973675680f031dd1d`). The existing follow-up intentionally accepts only exact relations, and its added-row path accepts a local primary with an empty alias payload. Those safeguards must remain intact.

Add a bounded form-review input for the melezitose correction first, followed by a separately reviewed sodium-perchlorate correction from merged main. This is a missing review capability, not a claim that the existing refusal is unsafe. #901 owns the source corrections; #718 retains the broader scientific-review backlog.

Acceptance:
- Bind each supported claim to its complete row, exact owner bytes, every emitted token, primary-source captures and a validated native scientific assessment of that specific claim.
- Preserve immutable prior decisions and negative findings. Discharge only the separately settled form-relation hold; retain preparation, grade, foreign-owner and unrelated scientific safeguards in both retained-row and added-row paths.
- Bind the actual verified receipt endpoint and B1 addition. Allow unrelated later position movement while refusing subsequent changes to the reviewed owner or row, including change-and-restoration cycles.
- Capture regular repository-confined evidence once; reject conflicting hashes, duplicate or unused claims, stale evidence and mismatched native review pairs. Keep roles and whole-record status outside mapping approval.
- Prove old CAS support withdraws before the fresh review. Test real assembly/export behavior, legacy refusal, stale and wrong-form cases, and continuity after an unrelated receipt.
- Regenerate through the native chain, run QC and regression tests, and obtain independent final-head review before queue publication.

No mapping approval is supplied by this issue, a receipt, a passing validator or the triplet structure itself. No paid provider calls are required.
title: Support explicit CAS-primary form-triplet reviews in the mapping completion assembler

body:

Refresh code-bound review inputs, retain the original failed CI evidence, and obtain independent review of the final head before queue admission.

Scope: strict #764/#766 replacement PR #1068. No scientific approval, canonical mapping or ingredient changes are authorized by this repair.

Add or retain a negative control proving that removing required fixture fields is rejected. Do not relax verifier checks or change historical scientific evidence. Audit any analogous failures from this same full-suite run and document each before fixing.

body:
Independent review of the strict #764 port found a per-plan withdrawal defect in frozen `reports/semantic_review_20260921/resolution/build_review.py` (SHA256 `ed66627f1ffd10decf33ecd32384d37ac99ee49fbdf8d9728b67b79f312c2e6c`).

`identity_support` first indexes original correction plans by owner, then `.update()` replaces them with recovered plans for the same owner. Validation sees only the surviving pin. The historical finding branch then uses that surviving pin's freshness but can cite the original correction plan as its resolving evidence.

The independent reproduction executes the real frozen `builder.main`, native receipt replay and graph exporter in the existing isolated builder fixture:

- A changed owner with only its original archived identity pin correctly leaves `SEM:identity` OPEN.
- Add a recovered identity plan for the same owner that binds its current exact bytes, while keeping the original stale plan and finding.
- The finding becomes RESOLVED and cites `corrections/identity-plan.json`. No identity supersession is recorded, because the old pin was overwritten before validation.

The unrelated fixed Aromatic hold is omitted as in the maintained fixture; this is an actual builder/provenance counterexample, not a claimed full semantic-gate bypass. The durable corpus has 13 original and three recovered mapped destinations with no overlap, so no current production misclassification is alleged.

Required repair:

- Retain original and recovered plan identities and archived hashes separately, even for the same owner. Prove withdrawal from each stale plan's own pin.
- Associate a finding with its actual supporting plan. A current recovered pin must not silently close a finding using stale original-plan evidence.
- Preserve legitimate current, explicitly scoped approvals and final mapping-only review behavior; add no approval to unrelated roles/components.
- Add actual-main regressions for overlapping pins, mixed current/stale plans, and incomplete chains, then independently re-review. Keep existing current-corpus dispositions and protected source bytes unchanged.

Evidence: `output/approved-plan-20261101T031134Z/step6-independent/consumers-9d8948/overlapping-identity-pins.json`, SHA256 `bf1e30430c298ddda7d32219638c984e0ff824115bd8a471c38995816ee85d4a`, with executable probe, exact source capture and logs. Actual non-overlap is separately recorded under `step6-independent/preparation/identity-plan-overlap.json`.

Deduplication: three live targeted searches found no duplicate. #740 is the existing stale-plan blocker; closed #850 requires exact archived hashes, and #1063 validates receipt operations. This finding concerns retaining and selecting distinct plan pins before those checks. Search responses and the original issue comments are preserved under `github/`. No production records or scientific decisions were edited by the reproduction.

body:
Independent review found a missing owner-history guard in the new strict receipt utility for #764/#745. Source: `src/mediaingredientmech/validation/mapping_change_receipts.py`, SHA256 `525b9c2f6f406ce602c55384dd349551c56fff97dece274a0a63fd22fc472155`.

`hold_lineage` inspects every suffix row operation and rejects even a same-payload change to the resolved held row. It checks the owner's final bytes against the frozen resolution, but does not inspect non-noop owner links after the checkpoint. An owner can change and then return to the original hash while the helper still certifies the existing frozen resolution's continuation.

The independent fixture preserves the actual 19-receipt prefix from base `7a06935dceb6ffc4ccccc1a1693e01f2950a8601`, its 2,981 current rows, the maintained receipt-11 checkpoint and actual frozen assertion/edge IDs. The positive control passes. Append two explicitly synthetic, structurally valid owner-only receipts:

- receipt 20: `Aromatic_Compound.yaml`, approved hash A → different hash B;
- receipt 21: the same owner, B → A;
- both receipts leave the canonical digest, all row payloads and positions unchanged.

Fresh `verify_mapping_chain` accepts the contiguous owner chain. `hold_lineage` also accepts it and returns suffix 12–21. The final owner hash matches A, but the owner lineage was not unchanged after its frozen approval. No actual corpus receipt or owner was changed. This demonstrates the utility boundary; no full-consumer scientific-release bypass is claimed while consumer integration is still under review.

The approved blueprint permits positional movement only for this frozen resolution and requires changed owners to fail. The selected #817 policy requires fresh approval after every record-byte change: [decision](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/pull/817#issuecomment-6050033909), [merged policy](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/pull/817#issuecomment-6050687305). This finding is narrowly about checkpoint-to-current frozen-hold continuation; it does not establish a broader byte-restoration policy for unrelated approvals.

Required repair:

- Reject any non-noop owner link for this resolved hold after its maintained checkpoint, including A→B→A, using the independently verified owner chain.
- Retain final exact owner hashes, receipt-11 identity, all row-operation checks and native assertion/edge parity.
- Keep genuine no-op owner links, unrelated-owner changes and changes before the reviewed checkpoint valid; retain both moved and unmoved row positives.
- Add negative/positive regressions, a guard-removal control and independent re-review. The actual 19-receipt corpus must still pass without any receipt or scientific-data edits.

Evidence: `output/approved-plan-20261101T031134Z/step6-independent/utility-525b9c/real-lineage-observation.json`, SHA256 `0a69a47d2340c54a1f55759f7a8a12b579aa624c1879619b293eadc450dcdbf2`, with the executable probe and isolated fixture. All 66 existing utility tests passed independently before this additional control.

Deduplication: four live issue searches found no duplicate. #745 is the existing position-shift requirement; closed #850 added endpoint byte pins; closed #819 concerned receipt advancement; #1063 concerns ambiguous row operations. None addresses changed-and-restored owner history in the new checkpoint utility. Captured responses and governing comments are under the evidence directory's `github/`.

body:

The helper captures five baseline outputs, including the 51-claim companion review, but compares only mapping, semantic assertion and finding decisions. It records the companion's new file hash without examining its decisions or including them in `scientific_approval_added` and the overall verdict.

Reproduction with the exact unchanged helper and isolated copies of the five real baseline outputs:

1. The unchanged positive control passes.
2. Change the companion's sole WITHHOLD claim (`MIM.annotation:78c235a18311ff2ab4d17d683bbc0f963bc8fc98eb50f24ce3c00a7391bd77c6`) to SUPPORTED and replace its reason.
3. The helper still exits 0, reports `EXACT_DISPOSITION_AND_SOURCE_PRESERVATION`, and reports `scientific_approval_added: false`. The companion hash changes, but that does not affect the result.

The fixture reduces the protected-file set to one real immutable source file; it retains all five actual comparison payloads. No production input or review was modified. Six separate negative controls correctly detect mapping-reason, assertion-payload, finding-removal, duplicate-key, blocking-summary and protected-source changes.

Required repair:

- Require an explicitly selected current companion review, with no fallback to the old review after refresh.
- Compare complete claim membership and scientific decisions against the captured prior review, including owner bytes, claim/payload identities, dispositions and reasons. Permit only independently verified dependency/evidence-locator updates.

body:
P1 implementation finding for the approved strict #764/#766 port on #817's exact-byte approval model. Not a claim that current published receipts are malformed or that the full semantic gate has been bypassed.

At merged Step 5 / fresh Step 6 base `7a06935dceb6ffc4ccccc1a1693e01f2950a8601`, the real `walk_mapping_changes` in `reports/sssom_completion_20260921/assemble_review.py:41–115` accepts four malformed synthetic receipts:

| Input | Result | Required rejection |
|---|---|---|
| `position_map=[1,null,2]`, no removed operation | Silently drops the second original row | Each null entry must have exactly one matching removed operation |
| Changed `before_position=0` | Reads the last original row through negative indexing | Require a true integer within the 1-based range before indexing |
| Two contradictory changed operations for the same original/destination row | Last after-payload wins | Reject duplicate original positions and conflicting destination operations |
| Boolean `true` in the position map | Treated as integer one | Exclude booleans from integer position/count/sequence domains |

Each malformed input reaches its explicitly declared terminal fixture rows. Adding only a replay-equals-current comparison does not address these cases. Valid unchanged, reorder, declared-add and declared-remove controls all pass. The actual 19-receipt corpus replays exactly to the current 2,981 canonical rows; no actual receipt was edited by the probe.

The assembler separately pins canonical/owner bytes and terminal replay and applies scientific safeguards. The reviewed-SSSOM and semantic consumers have additional checks. These reproductions exercise the maintained helper only; full-consumer tests must be added before claiming the extracted utility is strict. The receipt-11 frozen-hold checkpoint, whole prefix/suffix and eleven-field mapping-edge parity must remain intact.

Acceptance:

- Reject all four malformed fixtures before an ambiguous replay can be used; preserve valid add/remove/reorder and sequential changes across receipts.
- Validate exact integer domains, 1-based ranges, unique original/destination operations and complete one-to-one agreement between map removals/additions and declared operations. Preserve digest chaining, owner-byte chaining, full endpoint replay and exact receipt inventory.
- Exercise the shared utility and actual assembler/semantic gate boundaries; demonstrate targeted guard-removal controls.
- Keep exact archived owner-byte approvals, audit-only section refreshes and all scientific safeguards. A verified chain justifies withdrawal only; it cannot approve changed bytes.
- Preserve all original receipts and ingredient/canonical bytes. Rebuild the native review chain with no new positive scientific dispositions.

Deduplication: #742 (closed) concerned sequential receipts, not conflicting entries within one receipt; #743 (closed) added initial tests and did not identify these four accepted inputs. #765 (open) is edge-ID parity; #766 (open) is mandatory code-input binding. This is one new structural-validation issue covering the four related cases.

Evidence: `output/approved-plan-20261101T031134Z/step6-entry-7a06935/receipt-reprobe/` (`probe_current.py`, `results.json` and the entry index); results SHA256 `16f3e8b00d089a97e37d04f0a3a31f45949f18b40fbcd6900d58b01b512e8651`. Live deduplication responses and full governing comments are under the sibling `github/` directory. Fresh entry deduplication screened all 543 current issue bodies/titles (113 open, 430 closed), compared the prior inventory, refreshed governing comments and repeated six comment-inclusive searches. The only inventory delta was 12 Step 5 closures; no duplicate was found. No source edits have begun; this finding is filed before implementing the strict utility.

The merged producer correctly refuses `kg_microbe_write.registry` because its imported origin differs from the declared producer graph. Preserved evidence: `output/approved-plan-20261101T031134Z/step5-native-test-isolation-finding/`; original test SHA256 `ad7ec2942a7a07e012b7a4ad3d1a4fdb3ee10f96c14a2f93c76e168f783a890d`; actual gate controller log SHA256 `d1a959c5f080fb79f36e810a21fd6cc5c81d1af9d9cd1d5fcfe2e307fe0333eb`. No subsequent QC/full-suite gate ran in that failed attempt.

Repair only the integration test to execute the merged producer in a fresh interpreter with explicit producer import roots. Preserve the actual full-row projection and legitimate-versus-rejected glycerol alias assertions. Add a regression with the real pinned modules already cached, and retain a control proving the native producer still refuses an in-process mixed-origin import. Do not bypass the origin guard or silently skip the configured integration case.

The completed source, canonical, receipt19 and companion products stay unchanged. Their original context, continuation seal and failed gate are immutable history. Resume gates only after independent review of an explicit append-only context/seal migration binding the exact old/new test hashes; all other inputs and preserved output hashes must remain fixed. body:
Independent review reproduced a diagnostic-classification defect in the proposed consumer acceptance helper before any accepted production invocation. Exact native replay of a captured generation can legitimately fall back to the stored MIM label when a free ontology-label lookup returns no result. The helper instead compares the emitted label with the missing captured result (`None`) and rejects it.

The actual retained generation demonstrates this for ENVO:00002149 on four rows: an earlier capture resolved “ocean water”; the later capture omitted that label and the native builder emitted the stored “sea water”. The exact producer replay succeeds, but `diagnostic_delta()` raises because `label_changes.after` is null. The bounded canonical projection does not promote these unrelated raw label changes.

Independent proof log SHA-256 991e5ec3e82f7b4d37c67c34d5ef00da1654ec3e44edc9f0e00890285c6cea09; original helper starts at SHA-256 73c29396 and its exact source/proof are retained for the consumer PR. This is a fail-closed helper classification defect, not a wrong canonical label or a reason to weaken label validation.

Required fix: distinguish newly resolved labels from lost-resolution/native stored-label fallback, bind the fallback to the actual captured source record and exact native replay, and classify all changed diagnostic rows explicitly. Add the actual fallback regression plus wrong/unbound fallback refusal controls. Keep canonical field allowlists, exact producer replay, native label/invariant checks and no-approval semantics unchanged; independently re-review before acceptance. Related #669, #1055.
title: Classify verified native label fallback in consumer candidate acceptance

body:
Two existing unified rows for `Na2glycerophosphate x 5 H2O` and `Na2Glycerophosphate x 5 H2O` (six and two source occurrences respectively) publish CHEBI:15978 as both their MIM identity and ChEBI ID. The captured ChEBI primary response describes the neutral free acid C3H9O6P. A sodium salt pentahydrate cannot have that exact identity under MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md §3.

This is separate from #1020's reviewed correction of the existing CAS-identified MIM record to the glycerol 2-phosphate parent. The eight captured CultureMech ingredient objects supply the x5H2O labels and the 15978 grounding but do not establish the isomer or catalogue/CAS identity. #296 does not record a specific exact-identity ruling for these eight source objects.

An independent probe against merged Claw 9bd09b2ba163212a65289b91313f98cb0937476f disproved a seemingly conservative workaround: adding one casefolded source_only rejection entry for the wrong source term makes both rows MAPPED to cas:13408-09-8 through an existing normalized name anchor. It does not leave them unmapped. Clearing the source term therefore makes a new positive identity assertion that the captured ingredient objects do not substantiate. An unrelated genuine free-acid control remains unchanged.

Options:
- Establish the actual supplied material for these source recipes using primary recipe/catalogue evidence, then make an explicit source/owner ruling and regenerate with tests.
- If identity remains unresolved, design and review an explicit nonidentity-source disposition in the producer that cannot fall through to an unverified normalized owner; retain the original source fields as provenance.

Recommendation: keep this issue open, obtain source-specific evidence first, and use the second option if the evidence remains inconclusive. Do not infer the glycerol isomer or CAS from the hydrate formula or normalized spelling. Do not merge records. The bounded #669/#1019/#1020 consumer batch may remove the three unsupported glycerol aliases from these two rows, but must preserve and explicitly report this unresolved preexisting identity exposure; it must not claim the identity is repaired.

Evidence retained for the consumer PR: `step5-unified-glycerophosphate-finding.json` SHA-256 4b8e7bc66fc3befab5b8d6400e2acc1b7480d199bd16e61a3e3df75cda22b440; primary ChEBI response SHA-256 a90d99807742daaa58d197735bf51dc3999f8a8f1ef72453470f045c6d0a0c93; independent actual-producer probe log SHA-256 cd674e77c73b8d1f2844284d3b7f6a2e81427cb909b538fbda1ccfb96283f1e8; independent review SHA-256 a01cd850ae02ff80eb1ebbee78b2aa93b50c105aae9fc9bf1a35229eae01bb04. No source records, ledger entries or canonical identities were changed by the probes. Related: #669, #1020, #296.
title: Resolve raw pentahydrate glycerophosphate identities without normalized CAS guessing

body:
The approved #669 rollout requires form review before merging `Nh42ni_So42` and `Nh42ni_So42_X_6_H2o`. Related: historical #334.

Both records currently use CHEBI:86149, the hexahydrate. The bare owner's CAS 56110-30-6 and structure were enriched from the selected mapping; the explicit owner uses 7785-20-8. The source claims need to be kept distinct:

- [PubChem's 56110-30-6 lookup](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/rest/pug/compound/name/56110-30-6/property/MolecularFormula,MolecularWeight,InChI,InChIKey,IUPACName/JSON) resolves to CID 182663, H20N2NiO14S2, a hexahydrate. Its depositor synonym list includes that CAS string.
- The [PubChem CAS annotation](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/rest/pug_view/data/compound/182663/JSON?heading=CAS) assigns 7785-20-8 through FDA GSRS Q5LM426K64. [ChEBI:86149](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols4/api/ontologies/chebi/terms?obo_id=CHEBI:86149) and [Sigma 574988](https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/US/en/product/aldrich/574988) explicitly identify the hexahydrate with 7785-20-8.
- CAS Common Chemistry API access returned 401, so there is no direct registry response verifying 56110-30-6. The old claim that it necessarily denotes anhydrous material remains unverified.

Archived MediaDive concentrations for some bare-label sources fit roughly 394.99 g/mol. [NBRC 1199](https://www.nite.go.jp/nbrc/catalogue/NBRCMediumDetailServlet?NO=1199), however, gives only the bare nickel formula, with no hydration, CAS or catalogue. Omitted water does not prove anhydrous identity. Supplier/NBRC evidence is inspected web extraction; the failed MediaDive compound endpoint responses provide no identity evidence.

For this rollout, SUPPRESS the explicit hexahydrate's preferred name from the bare owner's published `other`, with unchanged records and a sidecar. Preserve the explicit owner's existing rejected bare-formula alias; do not silently reverse it or invent a replacement CAS.

Options are an explicit evidence-backed convention that the generic-label cohort denotes the hexahydrate, permitting a guarded merge, or distinct forms if original preparation/product evidence supports them. Recommendation: retain suppression and leave this issue open until registry/depositor provenance and source scope are reconciled. A future merge must preserve history, negative decisions and union overlapping memberships; current shared IDs are not independent form evidence.
title: Resolve bare ammonium nickel sulfate form and conflicting CAS evidence before merging

body:
The approved #669 rollout requires form review before merging `Sodium_Succinate_Dibasic` with `Sodium_Succinate`. Related: #738, #263 and #320.

The current identifiers agree on anhydrous disodium succinate: CAS 150-90-3, PubChem CID 9020 and CHEBI:63675. That alone does not settle the original generic record's supplied form. Its history includes supplier-derived CAS 6106-21-4 before a target-xref selection. The captured CultureBotHT input (SHA-256 `76b70a1836b25de431c4f5cc27c72bb6b06a223ce33911e93b7681d4fcdb28f9`, line 414) associates sodium succinate with Sigma S2378, 6106-21-4 and 270.14 g/mol. [Sigma S2378](https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/US/en/product/sial/s2378) is the hexahydrate; [Sigma 14160](https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/US/en/product/sial/14160) is a separate anhydrous product. Supplier evidence here is an inspected web extraction, not archived origin HTML. Existing recipe IDs derive from MIM and therefore do not independently settle the conflict.

For the approved bounded rollout, SUPPRESS `Sodium succinate` only on `MIM:Sodium_Succinate_Dibasic / skos:broadMatch / CHEBI:63675`, with a sidecar and unchanged source YAML. The alias is not established as chemically false, so it must not become REJECTED_LABEL. Preserve the explicit CHEBI:63686 hexahydrate control.

Options for the scientific decision:

- Trace the original product/form evidence and explicitly adopt an anhydrous naming convention for the generic source cohort, then merge through guarded writers with complete history, membership union and fresh review.
- If the source scope supports distinct forms, retain distinct identities and the §3 mapping pattern.

Recommendation: retain suppression and leave this issue open until that source scope or explicit evidence-backed convention is settled. No merge, replacement CAS or hydration state is inferred from the current target IDs. The bounded preflight and exact input hashes will accompany the consumer PR; this issue does not approve broader curation.
title: Resolve sodium succinate source hydration before merging dibasic and generic records

body:
Independent review of the proposed Step 4 closure verifier found an additional changed-path coverage defect while re-reviewing #1045. This finding is filed before repair or any branch cleanup.

The corrected NUL/literal-path verifier still uses Git's default rename detection when enumerating changed paths. For a reviewed rename, `git diff --name-only -z BASE HEAD` lists only the destination. A simulated merge can retain that correct destination and resurrect the removed source, and the comparison accepts it because the source was not enumerated.

The reviewer reproduced this with real isolated Git trees and a Unicode owner rename. The exact proposed helper was `verify_mim_merge_nul.py`, SHA256 `869d6925c57402f7867e8ab8f1c6a2b472125b57faa945332472993cea3b080a`. Evidence: `output/approved-plan-20261101T031134Z/step4-independent/probe_merge_rename.py` and `merge-rename-proof.json`. No historical production merge mismatch or cleanup is claimed.

Severity: medium, incomplete verified merge-content scope. Enumerate changed files with `--no-renames` so both deleted source and added destination are checked, preserve NUL parsing and literal path handling, and add a regression that a renamed-source resurrection is rejected. Retain positive rename, deletion and previous non-ASCII/path controls. Re-review the exact repaired helper before using it for the approved merge/cleanup sequence.
title: Verify both sides of renames before owned-branch cleanup

body:
The first actual Step 4 dependency-chain dispatch for #1005 stopped before invoking any native build command because the run-owned inventory guard parsed Git filenames incorrectly.

`native_chain.py` uses `git ls-tree -r --name-only BASE data/ingredients`, splits on newlines, and retains strings ending in `.yaml`. Git quotes and escapes non-ASCII filenames by default, so five existing owners end in a closing quote and are dropped. The actual ignored-inclusive filesystem inventory contains the unchanged 2,955 owners; the parsed baseline contains only 2,950. This falsely reports changed membership.

Affected existing names include `L-α-phosphatidylinositol_From_Glycine_Max_Soybean.yaml`, `Α-lipoic_Acid.yaml`, `Α1-Acid_Glycoprotein_From_Bovine_Plasma.yaml`, `Poly-ß-hydroxybutyric_Acid.yaml`, and `Α-D-Glucose_Monohydrate.yaml`.

Evidence: driver SHA256 `75c29e50c75fd6ee4acfc5c2b8402da634ee286f7ae8054958e656b368a21a13`; base `838d0c2627552b0094545ebb580b5bb9b1a84d57`; failed native dispatch log `output/approved-plan-20261101T031134Z/logs/step4-dispatch-chain-build.log` SHA256 `3d4f1b110a70aaa4d37ee91a6267df49cfcbae1f3976cb23a91c64f32d3c0241`. The separate post-application comparison already verified one changed owner and 2,954 unchanged owners. No native chain output was produced by this failed dispatch.

Severity: low, false refusal in execution guard. Use Git's NUL-delimited filename output and parse exact filename bytes/text without quote interpretation. Add a regression using real Git entries with non-ASCII filenames, and retain rejection of actual added/removed owner paths. Independently re-review before rerunning the chain. This is a run-owned driver defect, not a request to rename ingredient files or weaken ignored-file inventory coverage.
title: Use NUL-delimited Git paths in the Step 4 owner inventory guard

body:
Independent adversarial review found two races in the run-owned unified rebuild wrapper prepared for #1004, before it was executed against production records. This is the unpublished orchestration at `output/approved-plan-20261101T031134Z/guarded_unified_carnitine.py`; the native repaired publisher itself is not implicated.

1. The wrapper parses and bounds the candidate, then re-reads it for publication. Replacing the candidate during that later read can publish an unrelated `occurrence_count` change from 1 to 999 while the completed receipt still declares only the approved Carnitine Hydrochloride delta.
2. The wrapper captures its input path set before generation but passes no re-enumeration callback to the native publisher. Adding a new CultureMech YAML during receipt reservation is therefore not detected; publication completes without that new input in the recorded snapshot.

Both were reproduced against the actual native publisher, output reservations and validated transaction. Producer/checker subprocesses, Git metadata and caller lock were isolated fixture stubs; the positive control succeeded. No production application occurred. Evidence: `step3-mim-independent/orchestration-preliminary/probe_unified.py`, `unified-probe-results.json`, and `v2/` within that run directory. The initial fixture import-path failure remains separate from the successful reproductions.

Fix the wrapper to publish the exact bytes that were checked and to re-enumerate paths plus hashes in native precommit validation. Capture the code dependencies before importing/executing them and bind them throughout. Re-run the positive control and both race probes, then independently re-review before the actual unified rebuild. Retain the guarded execution script and evidence with the eventual #1004 PR. This issue grants no scientific approval and does not describe a defect in the current canonical snapshot.
title: Bind unified rebuild publication to checked bytes and the complete input set

The record maps `NARROW_MATCH` to CHEBI:15978.

Fresh primary database checks on 2026-11-01:

- [PubChem CAS 17989-41-2 query](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/rest/pug/compound/name/17989-41-2/property/Title,MolecularFormula,InChI,InChIKey/JSON) returns CID 439162, sn-glycerol 3-phosphate, formula C3H9O6P.
- [ChEBI:15978](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols4/api/ontologies/chebi/terms?obo_id=CHEBI:15978) carries this same free-acid formula and CAS.
- The record attributes CAS to `CultureBotHT compounds_to_cas.csv` and structure to automated PubChem backfill. The current occurrence statistics are 0/0. Its carbon-source role is explicitly a provisional name-pattern prediction, not form identity evidence.

Earlier #232/#732 work retained two free-acid names as `REJECTED_LABEL`, explicitly leaving identity unadjudicated. The canonical `other` still contains `Glycerol 3-phosphate` under #669's baseline. Neither synonym retirement nor the existing broad parent mapping validates a lithium-salt identity. Any correction must also preserve or explicitly reassess the provisional role and its content-bound evidence; no role approval is implied here.


Recommendation: trace the original CultureBotHT source/catalogue entry and an independently verified supplied form before choosing a replacement identity. If the salt name is supported, curate the salt-specific stable identifier and chemistry, retain the asymmetric parent and required identity rows, and refresh content-bound review receipts. If the supplied material was actually the parent, document that source-backed decision and reconcile the name/identity without losing raw source provenance. The automated name-derived CAS/chemistry is not independent evidence for choosing between these alternatives. Do not guess a replacement CAS, stereochemistry or merge.

Acceptance requires guarded curation/history, synchronized record/aggregate/SSSOM/label-index surfaces, preserved negative review holds, and native validation. No record edits are included in this finding. Neither target record is in the complete current #912 or #914 file list; shared aggregates and generated surfaces still require coordination.

This contradiction was listed as untracked in #887 and is related to the source-lookup risk in #235. Exact record-name and CAS issue searches found no dedicated open issue for this record. Historical #114 treated the parent mapping as acceptable; that does not validate the primary CAS identity. Keep #669 open pending this identity decision.
title: Resolve sn-glycerol phosphate lithium-salt label versus free-acid CAS identity

This is a different functional group, not one of the seven deferred generic-name/stereochemistry policy cases in #669.

Bounded correction:

- Retain this one name and its original `chebi_synonym_review` source as `REJECTED_LABEL`; append a sourced curation-history event through the native guarded writer.
- Preserve the current record identifier, mapping, status, occurrences, and unresolved salt/CAS/stereochemistry questions.

- Check that the rejected name cannot resolve through the label index or appear in native regenerated `other`; validate the record and run the required data gates.

**Evidence:** export_lines() calls json.dumps(..., allow_nan=False) with no default=; a record whose YAML carries an unquoted timestamp or date (yaml.safe_load gives datetime/date) raises TypeError and fails the Pages deploy. Found in the review of draft PR #957 (website feature unification, minor).

**Where:** `src/mediaingredientmech/render_ingredient_pages.py` (line 231)

**Claim or area:** curation_notice: PR body 'Every curator in the corpus is a process or agent' and the comment 'curation events name processes and agents rather than people, so no record's history can show that a human reviewed it'

**Evidence:** Scan of all 2,953 records: 185 distinct curator values; 'manual' appears on 3 events (e.g. Carbon_dioxide_gas.yaml: curator: manual, action: CREATED, 'Created MIM record for gaseous CO2'), 'manual_review_foodon_pass' on 1 and 'user_approved_curator_synonym' on 2 (6 records: Angustmycin, Carbon_dioxide_gas, Hydrogen_gas, Dry_Cow-manure, Nitrogen_gas, Stallimycin). The rendered disclosure is still truthful (it never asserts human review; on the single MANUAL_CURATION record, Atrop_Abyssomicin_C, it reads 'MAPPED: Has valid ontology mapping. The curation history lists 8 events by 7 curators; 1 is marked LLM-assisted' and its curators are processes plus 'claude'), but the stated basis is inaccurate, and for the two withheld qualities the badge (e.g. MANUAL_CURATION) is shown with no explanation at all rather than an explained caveat.

**Suggested fix:** Reword the PR body and comment ('no curator is a named person; three records record a hand-made creation as curator: manual'), and for LLM_ASSISTED / MANUAL_CURATION print the schema text with a caveat (or an explicit 'the schema's description of this value asserts human review, which this record's history does not record') instead of silently omitting the line.
title: Curation disclosure assumes every curator is a process or agent; three events name a manual curator

Found in the review of draft PR #957 (website feature unification, minor).

**Where:** `tests/test_unified_site_features.py` (line 332)

**Claim or area:** curation_notice: test_status_explanation_never_claims_human_review (both values)

**Evidence:** The test parametrizes over render.HUMAN_REVIEW_QUALITIES itself. With that set emptied (mutation M5) pytest reports 'SKIPPED [1] ... got empty parameter set for (quality)' instead of a failure, so the guard it protects can be removed or renamed without any red test. The disclosure would then quote 'Mapping suggested by LLM, human-verified' / 'Manually curated by expert' for records whose history names only processes.

**Suggested fix:** Parametrize over the literal values ['LLM_ASSISTED', 'MANUAL_CURATION'] and assert each is in render.HUMAN_REVIEW_QUALITIES, so emptying the set fails rather than skips.
title: Human-review guard test skips instead of failing when its value set is emptied

## Summary

Adversarial review of PR #908 identified that the per-record review bundle generator fabricated **775 synthetic `ReviewFinding` entries** across **742 per-record review bundles** for records that have no structured defects on `HEAD` (`3751d80fbd916de878be918aa481371020cc75bb`), converting bounded legacy narrative assessment groups into structured `deferred` findings.

1. **Contract violation (`reconcile-review-records`):**
   - When a record had no structured findings from `20261011T024636Z-mim-reconcile-all-batch-01..13`, `20261011T045916Z-mim-token-scope-reassessment`, live role-support checks on `HEAD`, open semantic dispositions in `reports/semantic_review_20260921/resolution/finding-dispositions.tsv`, or unresolved `UNMAPPED`/`AMBIGUOUS` identity, the generator promoted bounded `needs_reassessment` assessment groups (`Historical review coverage and residual narrative` and `Legacy field-missing triage rows`) into synthetic `ReviewFinding` entries (`mim-reconciliation-historical-review-coverage-and-r-<thex>` and `mim-reconciliation-legacy-field-missing-triage-rows-<thex>`) with `field_paths: ["curation_history"]`.
   - This violates `.claude/skills/reconcile-review-records/SKILL.md` ("Historical prose has no structured occurrence identity. Do not fabricate one or automatically migrate reports to manufacture a resolved lineage"), `.claude/skills/reconcile-review-records/references/legacy-findings.md` (`legacy-disposition` values are assessment labels, not `ReviewFinding.status` values), and `reviews/reconciliation/20261011T023739Z-all-mim/README.md` ("These are **bounded assessment groups, not distinct historical allegations**").
2. **Inconsistent promotion across records:**

body:
Found while re-checking CultureBotAI/CultureMech#271 before closing it. Checked on `main` at `3751d80fbd`, which includes #881.

## What MIM says

`data/ingredients/mapped/L-cysteine_Hcl_X_H2o.yaml` is the record with preferred term `L-Cysteine HCl x H2O` and identifier CHEBI:91248, status MAPPED. It lists `Cysteine hydrochloride` at line 55 as an `EXACT_SYNONYM`, with source `merged_from_duplicate_mim_record`. No curation event explains why a name without a hydrate sits on the hydrate.

`UNIFIED_INGREDIENT_MAPPING.tsv` was built at `1742bfd450`, before #881, and #894 tracks its rebuild. In it, `Cysteine hydrochloride` is the only cysteine-HCl spelling that names no hydrate yet maps to CHEBI:91248, with `cas_rn` 7048-04-6. Every other such spelling maps to CHEBI:91247, with `cas_rn` 52-89-1:

| label | occurrences | identifier |
|---|---:|---|
| `L-Cysteine HCl` | 135 | CHEBI:91247 |
| `Cysteine-HCl` | 111 | CHEBI:91247 |
| `L-Cysteine . HCl` | 16 | CHEBI:91247 |
| **`Cysteine hydrochloride`** | **15** | **CHEBI:91248** |
| `L-cysteine hydrochloride` | 13 | CHEBI:91247, whose ontology label this is |
| `L-Cysteine HCL` | 7 | CHEBI:91247 |

## What the sources say

**ChEBI, via OLS:**
- CHEBI:91247 is "L-cysteine hydrochloride", formula C3H7NO2S.HCl.
- CHEBI:91248 is "L-cysteine hydrochloride hydrate", formula C3H7NO2S.H2O.HCl.

**MediaDive** (https://mediadive.dsmz.de/rest/ingredient/1114). Compound 1114 is named "Cysteine hydrochloride":

| field | value | describes |
|---|---|---|
| formula | C3H8ClNO2S | anhydrous salt |
| mass | 157.62 | anhydrous salt |
| CAS-RN | 10318-18-0 | anhydrous salt |
| PubChem | 25150 | anhydrous salt |
| ChEBI | 91248 | monohydrate |

Its synonym list also includes the hydrate's systematic name, `(1R)-1-carboxy-2-sulfanylethan-1-aminium chloride--water (1/1)`.

**PubChem:**
- CAS 10318-18-0 is CID 25150, "DL-Cysteine, hydrochloride", C3H8ClNO2S, 157.62.
- CAS 52-89-1 is CID 60960, C3H8ClNO2S, 157.62.
- The monohydrate, CAS 7048-04-6, is CID 23462, C3H10ClNO3S, 175.64.

So the only source field that names the hydrate is MediaDive's ChEBI cross-reference. MediaDive's own formula and mass contradict it.

## Why #878 missed it

#878's check needs the label to state an explicit hydrate count, and `Cysteine hydrochloride` states none. CultureMech's own hydrate-agreement test has the same blind spot (CultureBotAI/CultureMech#278).

## Downstream

**Publication.** CultureMech's packaged label index, pinned at MIM `6643131b`, has `Cysteine hydrochloride,synonym,CHEBI:91248` at line 3313. CultureMech therefore publishes these rows as the monohydrate.

**CultureMech's own records are split.** 18 rows carry this name:
- 13 rows are grounded to CHEBI:91248.
- 3 rows are MediaDive rows on `mediadive.compound:1114`, with `chebi_term` CHEBI:91248.
- 2 rows are grounded to CHEBI:91247, in `clostridium_estertheticum_medium.yaml` and `clostridium_longisporum_medium.yaml`.

## Suggested fix

1. Move `Cysteine hydrochloride` off the CHEBI:91248 record. Add a `curation_history` event that cites the formula, mass, CAS and PubChem identity above.
   - The likely target is the CHEBI:91247 record, alongside `Cysteine-HCl` and `Cysteine.HCl`.
   - The name gives no stereochemistry, and MediaDive's CAS and PubChem point at the DL salt. Mapping spellings with unspecified stereochemistry to CHEBI:91247 is the existing convention.
2. Rebuild the unified mapping (#894).
3. Consider widening the #878 check to catch a label with no hydrate on an identity whose ontology label or formula names one.

Once CultureMech refreshes its label index pin, re-grounding its 16 record-level CHEBI:91248 values is CultureMech curation.
title: `Cysteine hydrochloride` is a synonym of the monohydrate CHEBI:91248, but its name, formula, mass and CAS describe the anhydrous salt

Found in the second review of PR #881. This predates #881.

When a mapping-change receipt touches a row, the assembler marks it WITHHOLD with the receipt as its basis, which is correct. But two kinds of reason, keyed by the row's baseline position, replace the receipt's reason:
- concern-cohort reasons (`reports/sssom_completion_20260921/assemble_review.py`, around lines 391-397);
- explicit holds (around lines 495-498).

`build_review.py` copies that text into `assertion-dispositions.tsv`, and `reviewed_sssom.py` exports `review_reason` into the released `mapping-dispositions.tsv`. A row can therefore ship with a reason that describes a defect the receipt fixed.

**Examples on #881's head (54e09be6):**

| row | record | published reason says | actual state |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2021 | `Na2so4_X_10_H2o` | "final other has an anhydrous label" | #881 removed it |
| 1608 | `L-cysteine_Hcl_X_H2o` | "final SSSOM exports concentration/no-water tokens" | #881 removed the concentration token |
| 1869 | `Mgso4_X_7_H2o` | holds on the cross-record baseline | #881 deleted that baseline pair, and the token is gone from the row |
| 1256 (on main) | Furaltadone | "still emits it as a narrow match" | it is an exact match now |

Semantic-review finding SEM:ae352c84b5456ae95a4a stays OPEN with the same outdated text (`finding-dispositions.tsv`).

**Effect:** dispositions stay conservatively WITHHOLD, so nothing is wrongly released. But the published reasons misstate the current rows, and a reviewer reading them would chase defects that are already fixed.

**Fix:**
- When a receipt has touched a row, label the carried reason as recorded against the pre-receipt payload, or put the receipt's reason first.
- Reconcile the fixed findings with the reconcile-review-records skill.
title: Review reasons carried past a mapping-change receipt still describe defects the receipt fixed

Found while reviewing PR #881. #897 is one instance; this is the backlog.

`MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md` §3 step 2 requires the following for a hydrate with no exact ontology term:
- its own identity (`cas:` or `kgmicrobe.compound:`);
- a `skos:broadMatch` to the nearest parent;
- the Rule B1 registry row.

The #245 ruling rejected `closeMatch` here, and #664 moved four sulfate hydrates off it. Among MAPPED records whose preferred term states a hydrate, counted on #881's head:

| identity | mapping_quality → parent predicate | records |
|---|---|---:|
| `cas:` | CLOSE_MATCH → `skos:closeMatch` | 45 (one is `Mgso4h2o`, fixed by #881) |
| `kgmicrobe.compound:` | CLOSE_MATCH → `skos:closeMatch` | 28 |
| `cas:` | NARROW_MATCH → `skos:broadMatch` | 12 |
| `kgmicrobe.compound:` | NARROW_MATCH → `skos:broadMatch` | 7 |

Examples:
- `cas:` with closeMatch: `Sodium_Deoxycholate_Monohydrate`, `L-Glutamic_Acid_Monopotassium_Salt_Monohydrate`, `Fosmidomycin_Sodium_Salt_Hydrate`;
- `kgmicrobe.compound:` with closeMatch: `Cocl2_X_4_H2o`, `Na2hpo4_X_3_H2o`, `Fecl2_X_6_H2o`, `Fecl2_X_7_H2o`, `Cu_No32_X_3_H2o`.

**Why it matters:**
- kg-microbe's consolidator treats `closeMatch` as symmetric (`scripts/consolidate_chemical_mappings.py:1776`, 1829-1873 at 1acb8b61f). It merges the hydrate's label and `other` tokens into the anhydrous parent's record and force-sets the parent's `canonical_name` to the hydrate label; the last row written wins.
- This comes from reading the code. I did not run kg-microbe or check which of these parents it actually renames.

**Also:**
- `MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md` (§3 step 2) says 34 hydrate subjects carry the broadMatch pattern. The count above is lower, so the doc or the data has drifted.
- `Cu_No32_X_3_H2o` keeps a local identity although its own CAS, 10031-43-3 (copper(II) nitrate trihydrate), is on the record. §3 step 2 would make it `cas:10031-43-3`.

**Related:** #696 (BROAD_MATCH publishes closeMatch) and #884 (schema direction of NARROW/BROAD).

**Fix:** a reviewed batch moving these records to NARROW_MATCH, with broadMatch and registry rows through the receipt chain. Check first which of them are SUPPORTED, because changing the bytes cancels approvals (#898).

## History

**How the cohort got here:**
- #342 (`scripts/regrade_hydrate_to_close_match.py`, in #500 on 2026-08-28) regraded 72 hydrate→anhydrous rows from narrowMatch to closeMatch on purpose. Its reason: narrowMatch claims a subsumption that ChEBI contradicts.
- That script also took those records out of Rule B1's scope.
- 72 SSSOM rows still carry `MIM:curator=regrade_hydrate_to_close_match`.

**The later ruling:**
- The #245 ruling (#735, 2026-09-22) settled the subsumption concern differently. It keeps `skos:broadMatch`, reads it as "form of", and forbids projecting it as `subclass_of`.
- It also records that `closeMatch` was rejected because it carries no direction and drops Rule B1.
- §3 step 2 has required broadMatch plus the registry row since then.
- #664 moved four sulfate hydrates back to that shape.

**Decision for maintainers:** these 73 are the #342 cohort the ruling did not migrate, so whether to migrate them is a maintainer decision, not a data error introduced by one PR.
title: 73 hydrate records anchor their parent with closeMatch, which §3 step 2 rejects; kg-microbe folds them into the anhydrous parent

Found in the second review of PR #881 (head 54e09be6).

PR #881 adds one synonym, `Magnesium chloride anhydrous`, to `data/ingredients/mapped/Mgcl2.yaml` (CHEBI:6636). Approvals are bound to exact record bytes, so that change cancels two approvals the reviewed release currently carries.

**What is lost**
- **The mapping:** `MIM:Mgcl2 skos:exactMatch CHEBI:6636` goes from SUPPORTED to WITHHOLD in `reports/sssom_completion_20260921/review.json`. Supported rows go from 1,741 to 1,740; this is the PR's only SUPPORTED→WITHHOLD change.

**What is gained**
- The name has 0 CultureMech recipe rows.
- ChEBI already lists it on CHEBI:6636.

**Consequence**
- The supported KGX keeps only approved edges.
- On the next export, MgCl2 (291 occurrences) would lose its CHEBI:6636 grounding and its role.
- Neither the PR body nor the README named the loss.

body:
Found in the second review of PR #881 (head 54e09be6).

## 1. The parent anchor is `closeMatch`, which §3 step 2 rejects

`data/ingredients/mapped/Mgso4h2o.yaml` takes `cas:14168-73-1` as its identity and anchors to CHEBI:32599 (magnesium sulfate) with `mapping_quality: CLOSE_MATCH`. The SSSOM row is `MIM:Mgso4h2o skos:closeMatch CHEBI:32599`. There is no Rule B1 registry row.

- **The rule:** `MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md` §3 step 2 says a hydrate with its own CAS and no exact ontology term takes `cas:<CAS>`, a `skos:broadMatch` to the nearest parent, and the mandatory registry row. The #245 ruling rejected `closeMatch` for these rows: it carries no direction, and Rule B1 is keyed on the asymmetric predicates.
- **Precedent:** `Mgso4_X_6_H2o` (same parent) is NARROW_MATCH, with a `broadMatch CHEBI:32599` row and a `kgmicrobe.compound` registry row. `Na2-citrate` (#704) has the same three-row shape. #664 moved four sulfate hydrates off `closeMatch` for the same reason.
- **Consequence:** kg-microbe treats `exactMatch` and `closeMatch` as symmetric. This is from reading `scripts/consolidate_chemical_mappings.py` at 1acb8b61f (lines 1776 and 1829-1873); I did not run it. For such a row it:
  - merges `subject_label` and every `other` token into the object's record;
  - force-sets the object's `canonical_name` to `subject_label`.

  `MIM:Mgso4h2o` sorts after `MIM:Magnesium_Sulfate`, so CHEBI:32599, the anhydrous node that "Magnesium sulfate" recipes use, would be renamed "MgSO4·H2O" and gain `CAS:14168-73-1`. On main the same row did this to the heptahydrate CHEBI:31795, so #881 moves the defect rather than removing it. The row is WITHHOLD in the reviewed release, so it bites on the full-SSSOM path or once someone approves it.

**Fix:** `mapping_quality: NARROW_MATCH`, with three rows:
- `skos:broadMatch CHEBI:32599`, with no CAS token in `other`;
- `skos:exactMatch cas:14168-73-1`;
- `skos:exactMatch kgmicrobe.compound:mgso4h2o`.

## 2. `kieserite` cites a PubChem record that does not list it

The PR adds `kieserite` as an EXACT_SYNONYM with `source: PubChem CID 16211255`. PubChem PUG REST (queried 2026-10-14) gives:
- CID 16211255, "Magnesium sulfate monohydrate", which has 24 synonyms including 14168-73-1 but not kieserite;
- the name "kieserite", which resolves to a separate record, CID 73357781 "Kieserite".

No CultureMech recipe uses the name.

**Fix:** drop the synonym.

## Confirmed correct

- No ChEBI term exists for the monohydrate.
- CID 16211255's formula (H2MgO5S) and InChI match the record.
- TogoMedium M2312 (Castenholz TYE) lists the ingredient as "Magnesium sulfate monohydrate".

The `cas:` identity stands.
title: MgSO4·H2O's parent anchor is closeMatch, not the broadMatch and registry row §3 step 2 requires; kieserite cites the wrong PubChem record

Found in the review of PR #881.

**The problem:** `data/ingredients/mapped/Na2so3_X_5_H2o.yaml` (a sodium sulfite hydrate) has identifier and ontology mapping `CHEBI:86477`, sodium sulfite (anhydrous), at `SYNONYM_MATCH`, with an SSSOM `skos:exactMatch`.

**Why it's wrong:** `MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md` §3 forbids mapping a hydrate to its anhydrous parent as an exact identity.

**Consequence:** because `Na2so3` carries the same id, PR #881's move of the "anhydrous sodium sulfite" names from `Na2so3_X_5_H2o` to `Na2so3` changes nothing for CultureMech or the KG.

**Existing tracking:** the only trace is the `HYDRATE_FAMILY_UNREVIEWED` row in `mappings/duplicate_identifier_baseline.tsv`. #321 is closed, and I found no open issue for this record.

**Fix:** follow the §3 decision procedure.
- If ChEBI has a term for this hydrate, ground to it.
- Otherwise, preserve a distinct `cas:` or `kgmicrobe.compound:` identity with a CLOSE_MATCH parent of CHEBI:86477.

Then update the SSSOM rows, the duplicate baseline and a mapping-change receipt.



## Update 2026-10-14 (second review of #881)

- **Correction to the suggested fix above:** where no ChEBI term exists, §3 step 2 needs three rows (see #897 for why `closeMatch` is wrong):
  - the `cas:` or `kgmicrobe.compound:` identity;
  - a `skos:broadMatch` (NARROW_MATCH) to CHEBI:86477;
  - the Rule B1 registry row.
- **More of the same defect:** `MIM:Na2so3`'s SSSOM `other` carries `Na2SO3 x 5 H2O`.
  - It is not a YAML synonym of `Na2so3`, so it came in from kg-microbe labels.
  - It is baselined under Rule K.
  - It should leave when this record is split.

body:
## Problem

PR #879 rebuilds `mappings/culturemech_recipe_membership.tsv` and 463 records' `occurrence_statistics` from CultureMech 41d4d39. That occurrence table omits every ingredient nested in a recipe's `solutions[]` (CultureMech#604). CultureMech#577 moved 2,175 ingredients of 360 recipes into `solutions[]`, so #879 drops genuine memberships.

Verified this session: `scripts/build_culturemech_membership.py`, run on a fresh `aggregate-all-ingredients` output at 41d4d39, reproduces #879's edge file byte for byte. The per-identifier edge changes against `main` (CultureMech 8c79a66f) include:

| identifier | main | #879 | removed recipes | cause of removal |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| MICRO:0002393 (Proteose Peptone No. 2) | 7 | 5 | 2 | CultureMech:001513 (BSK) now has only nested solutions; 0 occurrence rows |
| CHEBI:16494 (lipoic acid) | 1,747 | 1,767 | 25 | vitamin solutions nested in recipes such as CultureMech:000295 |
| CHEBI:33403 (sulfur) | 477 | 494 | 3 | same |
| CHEBI:30769 (citric acid) | 110 | 110 | 1 | same |

The additions I checked look correct, because each comes from a label that names the substance: lipoic acid +45, sulfur +20, BSA +2, citric acid monohydrate +3, CaSO4·7H2O +1.

## Consequence for #879

The PR's failing checks (pytest, reviewed-sssom, supported-graph, qc-unified-freshness) require an approval-free receipt for the 463 changed records. That receipt would withhold 147 currently supported mappings (1,741 → 1,594) until they are reviewed again. It would also break the exact-byte approvals of three records in the scoped ingredient bundle (Bovine_Serum_Albumin, Proteose_Peptone_No_2, Rabbit_Serum), and a unified rebuild with claw would be needed as well. Paying that cost for counts that are partly wrong, and then paying it again after CultureMech#604, is wasteful. #879 is on hold.

## Plan

1. CultureMech#604 is fixed, and the occurrence table is regenerated there (also CultureMech#580).
2. Rebuild #879 from that revision.
3. Re-check the removed-recipe rows above.
4. Update the pinned count tests (test_hydrate_family_identity, test_lipoic_stereochemistry, test_malformed_hydrate_identities, test_micro_source, test_reviewed_ingredient_identities, test_sulfur_family_consolidation) against the new edges, after checking each edge.
5. Add the receipt, rebuild unified, and re-pin the review artifacts.

#886 (detecting when the edges fall behind) would not catch this. The edges match their CultureMech revision; it is the revision's aggregation that is incomplete.


## Update 2026-10-14

- **CultureMech#605** is open. It counts inline-stock components, adding 8,162 occurrence rows at 41d4d390.
- **Preview:** a MIM membership rebuild from its output, not committed, gives:
  - Proteose Peptone No. 2 (MICRO:0002393): 8 recipes, against 7 on main and 5 at #879;
  - BSA (NCIT:C85253): 17, against 7;
  - citric acid: no removals.
- **Still open, membership policy:** lipoic acid (CHEBI:16494) still drops 18 recipes. Those media reach it only through references to shared stocks, which CultureMech counts once, on the stock record (CultureMech#312). Whether MIM membership should follow those references transitively is a MIM decision; it isn't decided here.
- **Still open, curation:** 27 components in 12 media sit only in inline copies under references (CultureMech#607 and CultureMech#609).
- **Rebuild #879:** after CultureMech#605 merges and its occurrence table is regenerated.

body:
Priority ranking from a full sweep of the open-issue queue on 2026-10-12, against `main` at 1742bfd4. It covers all 93 issues that were open on 2026-10-13 before the eight closures below, including #877, #878 and #880, which were filed during the sweep. It also covers the five issues the sweep filed. Update this issue in place rather than opening a second tracker.

How the entries were checked:
- **Re-checked against `main` directly:** the P0 items, the new issues and the closures.
- **From read-only reviewer checks:** every other entry, each issue checked against `main`.

## P0: wrong or missing identities in files kg-microbe and CultureMech read

- #882: 33 unified rows (3,378 recipe occurrences) have had no identity since #754, because nine merge tombstones no longer resolve to their merge target. PR #881 did not add a tenth: 54e09be6 fixed it before the merge on 2026-10-15.
- #808: 31 hydrate rows (492 occurrences) still have the anhydrous form or a different compound as their identity. Examples:
  - the `(NH4)6Mo7O24·4H2O` family maps to ammonium molybdate, CHEBI:91249, instead of CHEBI:86244;
  - `MnSO4 x n H2O` (209 occurrences) maps to the anhydrous salt.
  No check catches this.
- #869: 42 rows publish an anhydrous ChEBI term next to the record's own identity. kg-microbe ranks ChEBI first, so the parent wins.
- #811, surfacing as #868: wrong label-index answers flow into the unified mapping (e.g. `DL-Tryptophan` → L-tryptophan), including 13 rows that regressed in #863.

## P1

**Wrong identities with a smaller reach**
