body:
This is the item #449 left open: "Nothing re-runs any of this when CultureMech changes."

`mappings/culturemech_recipe_membership.tsv` is built by `just build-membership` (`justfile:317-334`). Its input is `output/ingredient_occurrences.tsv` in a sibling CultureMech checkout. That file is gitignored, so CI cannot rebuild the edges.

Nothing notices when the edges go stale:
- **No workflow runs the producer** or compares the edges with CultureMech.
- **The test can't see CultureMech:** `tests/test_culturemech_membership.py` compares the committed edges only with the committed records.
- **The provenance is never checked:** the edge file's header records the CultureMech commit it was built from (`culturemech_rev=8c79a66fec`), plus scoped corrections dated 2026-09-21 and 2026-10-03. Nothing reads that header.

#877 is the current instance. The edges were last rebuilt on 2026-10-03 (bf101f85), and #877 reports that 3,753 occurrence rows have changed identity in CultureMech since then. #877 is a one-off rebuild; this issue is about noticing the next time without being told.

Options, cheapest first:
1. Record which CultureMech commit MIM's edges must match. Fail a check when the header's `culturemech_rev` differs from it.
2. Run a scheduled job that checks out CultureMech, rebuilds the edges and opens a PR when they change.
3. Check out CultureMech in CI on every PR. #449 already weighed this cost.

The same trigger has to refresh `media_count` and `total_occurrences`. The edges reproduce both counts (`build_culturemech_membership.py`, module docstring), so updating one without the others breaks that agreement (#877, step 4).

#449's other leftover item was `media_count` shared across records on one identifier. #878 now tracks the remaining case: the `MgSO4·H2O` record sits on the heptahydrate. With both tracked, nothing else keeps #449 open.
title: Nothing detects when the CultureMech membership edges fall behind CultureMech (#449 leftover)

body:
Ruleset 22994916 ("CLAW merge queue") is active on `main` with no bypass actors. It requires 13 status checks:

`check`, `history`, `id-label-gate / label-correspondence`, `instruction-refs`, `pytest`, `qc-component-partonomy`, `qc-duplicate-ids`, `qc-evidence`, `qc-flat-coverage`, `qc-sssom`, `roundtrip`, `validate-strict`, `vendored-sync`

Three more checks run on every PR and every merge-queue candidate, because their `pull_request` and `merge_group` triggers have no path filter. None of the three is required:

| check | workflow |
|---|---|
| `qc-unified-freshness` | `QC — unified snapshot freshness` (`qc-unified-freshness.yaml`) |
| `reviewed-sssom` | `QC — reviewed MIM SSSOM` (`qc-reviewed-sssom.yaml`) |
| `supported-graph` | `QC — supported MIM graph` (`qc-supported-kgx.yaml`) |

So the merge queue would admit a candidate on which any of them fails. These three check the unified snapshot, the reviewed SSSOM and the supported graph, which are the files kg-microbe and CultureMech read. Nothing has slipped through yet: all three passed on each of the last 25 commits on `main` (2026-09-28 to 2026-10-12).

**Fix:**
- Add the three contexts to the ruleset's required checks.
- Add their workflows to `REQUIRED_JOBS` in `tests/test_merge_queue_workflows.py`, which currently lists the same 13. That test then also asserts the three workflows can't be path-filtered or skipped.
title: Three checks on published artifacts are not required by the merge-queue ruleset

body:
The schema's `MappingQualityEnum` describes the two grades from the ontology term's side (`src/mediaingredientmech/schema/mediaingredientmech.yaml:1193-1199`, repeated in the generated `docs/MappingQualityEnum.md`):

> **NARROW_MATCH:** Ontology term is narrower than the ingredient (more specific). Used when the ingredient name covers a class and the chosen term covers one instance/subtype of that class.
>
> **BROAD_MATCH:** Ontology term is broader than the ingredient (less specific).

`MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md` describes them from the record's side. It outranks the schema on mapping semantics, and it says the reverse:

> **line 151:** a record graded `NARROW_MATCH` is narrower, therefore its ontology term is broader.
>
> **line 555:** A record graded `NARROW_MATCH` still means "this record is narrower"; its published predicate is `broadMatch` because the *ontology term* is broader.

The code and the data agree with `MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md`:
- **The builder:** `predicate_for` in `src/mediaingredientmech/sssom_grading.py` publishes NARROW_MATCH as `skos:broadMatch` (comment at lines 51-57). It publishes every other non-exact grade, BROAD_MATCH included, as `skos:closeMatch`.
- **The corpus:** 164 records are graded NARROW_MATCH (151 of them MAPPED), and 1 is graded BROAD_MATCH.

A curator who follows the schema text would grade a record that sits under a broader parent as BROAD_MATCH. That record would then publish `closeMatch` rather than the `broadMatch` parent anchor. #696 asks whether BROAD_MATCH → `closeMatch` is deliberate, and this mismatch is the root of that confusion.

**Fix:**
1. Rewrite both descriptions from the record's side, as `MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md` does:
   - NARROW_MATCH: this record is narrower than its ontology term, and it publishes as `skos:broadMatch`.
   - BROAD_MATCH: this record is broader than its ontology term.
2. Regenerate the docs.
3. Settle #696's predicate question in the same change.
title: The schema describes NARROW_MATCH and BROAD_MATCH the opposite way from MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md and the SSSOM builder

body:
`UNIFIED_INGREDIENT_MAPPING.tsv` on `main` (1742bfd4) has 33 rows that are REJECTED with an empty `chebi_id`, `kg_microbe_node_id` and `mim_id`. They cover 3,378 recipe occurrences, and all 33 were MAPPED at 48408270 (#731, 2026-09-22).

| snapshot | REJECTED rows with no identity | occurrences |
|---|---:|---:|
| 48408270 (#731, 2026-09-22) | 0 | 0 |
| a8b26f00 (#754, 2026-09-25) | 47 | 9,386 |
| 6643131b (#802, 2026-10-05) | 47 | 9,391 |
| 1742bfd4 (#863, 2026-10-12) | 33 | 3,378 |

kg-microbe's consolidator skips REJECTED rows (`scripts/consolidate_chemical_mappings.py:1604-1606` at kg-microbe 1408e7099). MIM therefore supplies no identity for these labels. I did not check what kg-microbe falls back to.

## Cause

claw's unified builder finds a merge tombstone's target in `_mim_merge_target` (`scripts/build_unified_ingredient_mapping.py:129-140` at the pinned claw a5d56296):

```python
for event in reversed(data.get('curation_history', []) or []):
    if event.get('action') in MIM_MERGE_ACTIONS:
        return (data.get('identifier') or '').strip()
    if event.get('new_status') == 'REJECTED':
        return ''
```

The builder walks the history backwards and stops at the first event with `new_status: REJECTED`. Nine tombstones later gained a bookkeeping event recorded as REJECTED → REJECTED, so the walk stops before it reaches the merge:

| tombstone | identifier | blocking event |
|---|---|---|
| `Cocl2_X_6_H2o` | CHEBI:53503 | REJECTED_WRONG_FORM_SYNONYMS (#757) |
| `Na2moo42h2o` | CHEBI:75213 | REJECTED_WRONG_FORM_SYNONYMS (#757) |
| `Calcium_Chloride` | CHEBI:3312 | REJECTED_WRONG_FORM_SYNONYMS (#757) |
| `Sodium_Citrate` | CHEBI:32142 | REJECTED_WRONG_FORM_SYNONYMS (#757) |
| `Trisodium_Citrate_X_2_H2o` | CHEBI:32142 | REJECTED_WRONG_FORM_SYNONYMS (#757) |
| `Na-glutamate` | CHEBI:64243 | REJECTED_WRONG_FORM_SYNONYMS (#757) |
| `Mgcl2x_6_H2o` | CHEBI:86345 | CORRECTED (#739) |
| `Nah2po4h2o` | CHEBI:114249 | CORRECTED (#755) |
| `Cinnamic_Acid` | CHEBI:35697 | CORRECTED (#755); none of the 33 rows |

The corpus has 81 REJECTED records. Of these, 13 set `representative:`, 51 resolve through their merge event, these 9 resolve to nothing, and 8 have no merge event. The #755 CORRECTED events were written "so the merged name is credited to the live record". In the unified build they have the opposite effect.

## Rows affected

| labels | occurrences | identity at 48408270 | answer the records support now |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `CoCl2 x 6 H2O` | 2,317 | CHEBI:53503 cobalt chloride hexahydrate | same |
| 7 other CoCl2·6H2O spellings | 358 | CHEBI:35696 cobalt dichloride (anhydrous) | CHEBI:53503 |
| 6 Na2MoO4·2H2O spellings | 412 | CHEBI:75213 sodium molybdate dihydrate | same |
| 5 Na2MoO4·H2O spellings | 8 | CHEBI:75215 sodium molybdate (anhydrous) | none: no monohydrate record |
| `Sodium citrate`, `Sodium Citrate`, `sodium citrate` | 94 | CHEBI:53258 sodium citrate | contested, see below |
| `Calcium chloride`, `calcium chloride` | 82 | CHEBI:86158 calcium chloride dihydrate | CHEBI:3312 (live `CaCl2` lists `Calcium chloride`) |
| `Calcium Chloride` | 15 | CHEBI:3312 calcium dichloride | same |
| `Trisodium citrate x 2 H2O`, `Trisodium citrate・2H2O` | 77 | CHEBI:53258 sodium citrate | CHEBI:32142 sodium citrate dihydrate |
| `Trisodium citrate・3H2O`, `Trisodium citrate x 3 H2O` | 3 | CHEBI:53258 | none: no record for that form |
| `NaH2PO4•H2O` | 4 | CHEBI:37585 sodium dihydrogenphosphate (anhydrous) | CHEBI:114249 monohydrate |
| `MgCl2x 6 H2O` | 4 | CHEBI:86345 magnesium dichloride hexahydrate | same |
| `MgCl2 x 7H2O` | 2 | CHEBI:6636 magnesium dichloride (anhydrous) | kgmicrobe.compound:mgcl2_x_7_h2o |
| `Na-glutamate` | 2 | CHEBI:64220 monosodium glutamate | CHEBI:64243 monosodium L-glutamate |

- **Rows that lost an identity the records still support:** 2,748 occurrences in the "same" rows, mostly `CoCl2 x 6 H2O` (2,317) and the sodium molybdate dihydrate spellings (412).
- **Rows that had a wrong form at 48408270:** 534 occurrences. These should have been corrected, not dropped.
- **Contested labels (94 occurrences):** for the sodium citrate names, live `Trisodium citrate` (CHEBI:53258) lists `Sodium citrate`, while live `Na3-citrate x 2 H2O` (CHEBI:32142, the dihydrate) lists `Sodium Citrate`.
- **`Na-glutamate` (2 occurrences):** it had generic monosodium glutamate, where MIM now holds the L-form.

## Fix

Setting `representative:` on the nine tombstones, as 13 others already do, would make claw resolve them again. That step alone is not safe. Several tombstones still carry names of other forms as publishable synonyms, and a restored merge target would publish those names under the wrong form:

- `Cocl2_X_6_H2o` (hexahydrate): `CoCl2 x 2 H2O` and `CoCl2 x 4 H2O` (HYDRATE_FORM). Both forms have had their own records since #863.
- `Na2moo42h2o` (dihydrate): four monohydrate spellings (HYDRATE_FORM): `Na2MoO4 . H2O`, `Na2MoO4 · H2O`, `Na2MoO4.H2O` and `Na2MoO4xH2O`.
- `Mgcl2x_6_H2o` (hexahydrate): five spellings, `MgCl2 x 7 H2O`, `MgCl2 x 7H2O`, `MgCl2x7H2O`, `MgCl2  x 7 H2O` and `MgCl2  x 76 H2O` (HYDRATE_FORM).
- `Trisodium_Citrate_X_2_H2o` (dihydrate): `Trisodium citrate·3H2O` (HYDRATE_FORM).
- `Calcium_Chloride` (anhydrous): `CaCl22H2O` (HYDRATE_FORM). #757 retyped two other dihydrate spellings but not this one.
- `Na-glutamate` (monosodium L-glutamate): `(2S)-2-aminopentanedioate` and `L-glutamic acid dianion` (EXACT_SYNONYM). Both are names of the anion.
- `Sodium_Citrate` (dihydrate CHEBI:32142): its preferred term `Sodium Citrate` is a generic name, and its synonym `Na2citrate` names disodium citrate.

Suggested order:

1. Retype those names as REJECTED_LABEL, or move each to the record for its form, with curation events.
2. Set `representative:` on the nine tombstones. If review pins (#740, #745) block these edits, change claw instead: when looking for the merge, skip events whose `previous_status` is already REJECTED.
3. Rebuild with `just rebuild-unified`. Check that the 33 rows come back, except the 11 occurrences whose form has no record.
4. Add a gate. `check-unified-freshness` and `check-unified-rejections` both pass on the current snapshot. Either of these checks would have caught this:
   - every merge tombstone carries `representative:`;
   - no REJECTED row without an identity has a tombstone's name as its label.

Related:
- #878 covers MAPPED labels that sit on a different hydrate.
- #877 is the membership rebuild. It reports that CultureMech#591 now refuses tombstone redirects across hydrates on CultureMech's side.

## Correction to #863

#863's description calls rows like these "merged-tombstone answers that the reviewed builder withholds (MIM #811, #816)". Nothing is withheld on purpose: the builder loses the merge target as described above, and neither #811 nor #816 covers that.
title: 33 unified rows (3,378 recipe occurrences) lost their identity: nine merge tombstones no longer resolve to their merge target

body:
Found from CultureBotAI/CultureMech#597, using CultureMech's `label_hydrate_count` (CultureMech#591) over the label index at `6643131b`. These are **MAPPED** rows, MIM's curated answers. CultureMech honours MAPPED answers and does not override them, so they can only be fixed here.

Each row's label states an explicit hydrate count. Its identifier's count comes from the index itself: the identity's `ontology_label` rows when they state one, otherwise its MAPPED preferred terms. Recipe rows are occurrences in CultureMech `41d4d39`.

## A. Wrong identity: label hydrate ≠ identity hydrate (12 rows)

| label | label states | identifier | identity states | recipe rows |
|---|---|---|---|---:|
| `NaH2PO4 x H2O` | 1 | kgmicrobe.compound:nah2po4_x_2_h2o | 2 | 34 |
| `NaH2PO4·H2O` | 1 | kgmicrobe.compound:nah2po4_x_2_h2o | 2 | 1 |
| `NaH2PO4・H2O` | 1 | kgmicrobe.compound:nah2po4_x_2_h2o | 2 | 1 |
| `MgSO4·H2O` | 1 | CHEBI:31795 | 7 (ontology label "magnesium sulfate heptahydrate") | 2 |
| `magnesium sulfate anhydrous` | 0 | CHEBI:31795 | 7 | 0 |
| `Magnesium chloride anhydrous` | 0 | CHEBI:86345 | 6 (ontology label "magnesium dichloride hexahydrate") | 0 |
| `sodium sulfate, anhydrous` | 0 | CHEBI:32586 | 10 | 0 |
| `Anhydrous sodium sulfite` | 0 | CHEBI:86477 | 5 | 0 |
| `Sodium sulfite anhydrous` | 0 | CHEBI:86477 | 5 | 0 |
| `copper(II) nitrate (anhydrous)` | 0 | kgmicrobe.compound:cu_no32_x_3_h2o | 3 | 0 |
| `Cystein-HCl x 2 H2O (5% (w/v))` | 2 | CHEBI:91248 | 1 | 0 |
| `sodium monohydrogen phosphate dihydrat` | 2 | kgmicrobe.ingredient:disodium_phosphate_heptahydrate_~28002_m_stock~29 | 7 | 0 |

The three NaH2PO4 rows are already #758. Rows with 0 recipe rows are latent: they do not affect CultureMech today, but any recipe that uses those spellings would get the wrong hydrate.

## B. One misnamed record: the `MgSO4·H2O` record sits on CHEBI:31795

A MIM record whose preferred term is `MgSO4·H2O` is grounded to CHEBI:31795 (ontology label "magnesium sulfate heptahydrate"). It owns 12 heptahydrate synonyms, so those identities are right and only the record's name contradicts them:
- `MgSO4.7H2O` (23 recipe rows)
- `magnesium sulphate heptahydrate` (1)
- `magnesium sulfate heptahydrate`, `magnesium sulfate (1:1) heptahydrate`, `sulfuric acid magnesium salt heptahydrate`, `.MgSO4 x 7 H2O`, `MgSO x 7 H2O`, `MgSO2 x 7 H2O`, `MgSO4x7H2O`, and three `MgSO4•7H2O (...)` product spellings (0 each)

Either the record is a heptahydrate record with a wrong name, or it is a monohydrate record with a wrong grounding that has collected heptahydrate synonyms. In the second case, the `MgSO4·H2O` label (section A) and these synonyms belong on different records. `build_culturemech_membership.py` already flags this record ("a monohydrate inherits the heptahydrate's memberships").

## Not a defect

`Ceftriaxone disodium salt hemiheptahydrate` → record `Ceftriaxone disodium salt hemi(heptahydrate)` showed up only as a CultureMech parser false positive: the parenthesised prefix is read as "heptahydrate".

## Related

- #811: tombstone cross-hydrate redirects. CultureMech#591 now refuses those on its side; this issue covers the MAPPED cases it cannot.
- #758: NaH2PO4 monohydrate
- #877: membership rebuild




## Resolution (2026-10-15)

- **Fixed:** PR #881 (merged as 3751d80f) handles rows 4-12 and regrounds `MgSO4·H2O` to `cas:14168-73-1`.
- **Rows 1-3 not fixed here:** the NaH2PO4 monohydrate spellings stay with #758.
- **Follow-ups:** #894, #896 and #900-#904.
title: 12 MAPPED labels resolve to an identity with a different hydrate; the MgSO4·H2O record sits on the heptahydrate

body:
## Why

`mappings/culturemech_recipe_membership.tsv` was last rebuilt on 2026-10-03 (bf101f8). Since then CultureMech has made two changes that alter which identity its occurrences resolve to:

- **CultureMech#537:** the vendored label index moved from MIM `9f09e4fb` to `6643131b`. Compared with CultureMech's 2026-10-04 occurrence file, 3,753 occurrence rows changed identity. The largest: Sulfur → CHEBI:33403 (352), CoCl2·6H2O spellings → CHEBI:53503 (313), NiCl2·6H2O spellings → CHEBI:53542 (290), Iron(III) chloride newly → CHEBI:30808 (75).
- **CultureMech#591:** merge tombstones that redirect across hydrates now fail closed. 21 rows lose their identity: `MgSO4 x H2O` (12), `NiCl2 x H2O` (4), `MgSO4 . H2O`, `NiCl2・H2O`, and three `Na2MoO4·H2O` spellings (1 each).

The current membership edges therefore still reflect MIM's pre-6643131b identity answers. Rebuilding MIM membership before the pin landed would have reverted MIM's curated corrections. The pin has now landed, and this is the rebuild that order was waiting for (CultureBotAI/CultureMech#580).

## Input

`CultureMech/output/ingredient_occurrences.tsv`, regenerated 2026-10-12 with `just aggregate-all-ingredients` at CultureMech `main` `41d4d39`:
- 201,090 occurrences: 197,256 mapped, 3,834 unmapped
- `ingredient_aggregation_errors.tsv` has no rows
- the file is gitignored, so it must be regenerated (or reused) in a sibling CultureMech checkout at that commit or later

## Steps

1. In a CultureMech checkout at `41d4d39` or later, confirm `output/ingredient_occurrences.tsv` exists and is current; otherwise run `just aggregate-all-ingredients`.
2. In MIM, run `just build-membership` (defaults to `../CultureMech/output/ingredient_occurrences.tsv`).
3. Review the diff to `mappings/culturemech_recipe_membership.tsv` and `reports/culturemech_membership_unknown_ids.tsv`. Expect edges to move between the identities listed above, and the 21 hydrate-conflict rows to drop out.
4. Check whether `media_count` / `total_occurrences` in the curated records must be refreshed to stay consistent with the new edges (the invariant in `build_culturemech_membership.py`), and do so with the existing tooling.
5. Open a PR with before/after edge, identifier and recipe counts.

## Related

- MediaIngredientMech#811: wrong label-index answers; #758: NaH2PO4 monohydrate spellings
- Hydrate contradictions in MAPPED rows (filed separately)
title: Rebuild CultureMech recipe membership from CultureMech 41d4d39 occurrences

Found in the second review of #863.

`data/ingredients/mapped/Na2hpo4_X_7_H2o.yaml` has the local identity `kgmicrobe.compound:na2hpo4_x_7_h2o`. It was minted on 2026-08-13 under MAPPING_SEMANTICS §3 step 3, which covers "no exact term and no CAS". The record now carries `cas_rn: 7782-85-6`, the heptahydrate's own CAS. The x3 and x6 sibling records that shared it in the #334 scramble no longer carry it, and #863's unified snapshot publishes it on the `Na2HPO4·7H2O` row.

§3 step 2 says that when there is no exact term but the substance has its own CAS, `identifier` should be `cas:<its own CAS>`, with a broadMatch to the nearest parent and the Rule B1 registry row. Open semantic-review finding SEM:cb9ec35166086d936f70 already asks for "exact CAS promotion" on this record.

**Coupling with #863.** #863 adds a rejection-ledger row keyed (`kgmicrobe.compound:na2hpo4_x_7_h2o`, CHEBI:34683). A promotion to `cas:7782-85-6` must update that row's `mim_id` in the same change. Otherwise claw's `load_mapping_rejections` fails closed with "rejection disagrees with MIM identity".

**To do:**
1. Verify 7782-85-6 against an authoritative source for disodium hydrogen phosphate heptahydrate.
2. If it is confirmed, promote the record under §3 step 2 through the SSSOM receipt chain, update the ledger row in the same commit, and rebuild the unified snapshot.

Found reviewing #863.

12 of the 35 local-hydrate records (a `kgmicrobe.compound` identity and a hydrate label) carry an InChI with no water, which is the anhydrous parent's structure:
- `Cocl2_X_2_H2o`, `Cocl2_X_4_H2o`, `K2hpo4_X_3_H2o`, `Nah2po4_X_2_H2o`, `Na2hpo4_X_7_H2o`, `Nicl2_X_2_H2o` (the six records #863 edits)

- four "salt hydrate" records with unspecified hydration (bathophenanthrolinedisulfonate, cefsulodin, chlorhexidine diacetate, DL-isocitrate)

For example, the CoCl2 hydrates' `inchi` and `smiles` equal CHEBI:35696's exactly, under `data_source: PubChem (via CHEBI:35696)`, while their `molecular_formula` states the hydrate. These values ship in the full KGX `record_json`. Open semantic-review findings SEM:058def08fac3452ea333 and SEM:a7481e9dc9fae5bece11 already name this for the CoCl2 pair.

Precedent: #646 (`Mgcl2_X_7_H2o`) and #321 (`Fe2_so43_X_N_H2o`) cleared the inherited `chemical_properties` entirely. Clearing everything would also discard values that are right for the hydrate. For example, `Na2hpo4_X_7_H2o` carries the heptahydrate CAS 7782-85-6.

**Proposal:** one reviewed batch that removes the water-free InChI and SMILES (and any parent-derived `data_source`), keeps verified hydrate-specific values, and records a curation event on each record. Decide separately whether the unspecified "salt hydrate" records should carry an anhydrous structure at all.

body:
Found reviewing #812 (head 75033543).

**1. Major: fails on correct, unstaged work.** `just qc-roundtrip` now ends with `scripts/check_record_filename_case.py` (`justfile:452`). That script also fails when a record file is on disk but untracked, or tracked but absent from disk (`scripts/check_record_filename_case.py:119-122`, `:154`). CI's checkout is pristine, so neither condition can occur there. Locally, both are the normal state of a new, promoted, merged or deleted record before `git add` or `git rm`.

Reproduced:
- Add one record file, then run `just sync-curated`, `just export-indexes` and `just qc-roundtrip`.
- Every check passes, then the recipe exits 1 with `on disk but untracked: 1`.
- The hint says to re-run with `--fix`, but `--fix` prints nothing for this case.

`just sync-individual` and `just qc` call this recipe, so they fail the same way. 35 of the 126 commits on main since 2026-08-01 that touch `data/ingredients` add, delete or rename record files.

**2. Minor: runs last, so case drift is misreported.** CI runs this check first (`qc-roundtrip.yaml:63-70`, #352) so that a case-only rename is reported as itself. The recipe runs it last, after `check_visualization_currency.py --strict`. Visualization ids keep the filename's case, so on macOS a case-only rename fails the visualization step first ("naming missing records … Regenerate: just generate-umap / just generate-graph") and the filename check never runs. Following that advice would regenerate both visualizations, whose layout is not reproducible, around the drifted name.

**Fix in #812:**
- Add `--case-only`: fail on case drift and collisions, and report absent and untracked files without failing.
- Run the check first in the recipe, with `--case-only`. CI keeps the strict mode.
- Name a remedy for each kind of failure.
title: qc-roundtrip's filename-case step fails on unstaged record adds and deletes, and runs after the step it should precede

body:
## Finding

Adversarial self-review of PR #860 identified a publication hazard in the new successor review. `reviews/structured/20261011T030852Z-mim-token-scope-reassessment/review.yaml` records the real inspected Git base `0cc2b4e3`, the PR's first commit.

`scripts/record_review.py:source_provenance` requires the recorded base commit to exist even for a working-tree attestation. The active `CLAW merge queue` ruleset uses `merge_method: SQUASH`. Squash landing followed by topic-branch deletion does not retain `0cc2b4e3` in main ancestry; a fresh consumer can therefore reject a valid immutable successor as unverifiable. A local green check is insufficient because the author's object database still contains the branch history.

## Acceptance

- Do not rewrite the saved review's source revision or hashes.
- Retain the exact Git base through a durable archival provenance tag, without preventing topic-branch deletion or changing branch-protection rules.
- Record the tag and exact commit in the round's navigation documentation and test their agreement with the saved source attestation.
- Verify source provenance from a separate checkout that fetched main and the provenance tag, not the topic branch.
- Add skill guidance to check base reachability under the actual merge strategy before publishing future rounds.

This is a publication/provenance defect in this PR, not a scientific finding or permission to change the shared CLAW review schema.
title: Preserve reconciliation Git bases across squash merge and branch deletion

## Finding

Adversarial self-review of the all-record reconciliation on branch `codex/reconcile-review-records-skill`, initial commit `0cc2b4e3`.

The 17 `exported-context-tokens` findings infer `status: open`, `certainty: confirmed`, and a major defect from a token containing a recipe cross-reference or unbalanced concentration parentheses and appearing somewhere in an old report. This proves the token is still exported, not that its source scope makes it an invalid resolving label.

Concrete example: `data/ingredients/mapped/Riboflavin.yaml` retains `Riboflavin (see below)` as a CultureMech `RAW_TEXT` source label. The original report recommends removal, but current mapping semantics preserve genuine raw source names; neither the source recipe nor a contradictory identity was reassessed in this run. A blanket mechanical check cannot choose between preserving a source-specific name and rejecting an instruction fragment.

This is a review-certainty defect, separate from existing ingredient curation (#718) and upstream synonym cleanup (#587). It is not evidence that every token is valid, nor permission to remove labels. Other allegations, such as the trace-mineral labels attached to 4-vinylphenol, still need their own scoped identity adjudication.

- Preserve all 13 original saved review pairs byte-for-byte.
- Append evidence-backed, explicitly provisional/deferred successors for all 17 heuristic-only token observations, retaining exact issue keys, predecessor identities, and affected targets.
- Add skill guidance separating candidate detection from claim-level adjudication.

```
ValueError: Stale review input: output/mim-kgx-710-full/manifest.json
```

Reproduction on the candidate:

```sh
uv run --frozen python -m mediaingredientmech.export.kgx --output output/mim-kgx-710-full
uv run --frozen python -m mediaingredientmech.export.supported_kgx --root . --report reports/semantic_review_20260921/resolution/current-review.json --output output/mim-kgx-710-supported
```

An independent rebuild using the exact base package/schema and the unchanged candidate corpus reproduces the receipt's expected manifest SHA-256 `4caac6fab0bb6330767b200338ffb672a59bf0cc641ed832678ee4c1257b9515`. Rebuilding with the candidate schema gives `afb2c143250c0cadf8e345b1a1fc434974b4cb084d8d6ea5f554c178d305228e`.

body: Found in the second review of culturebotai-claw#571. A merge tombstone can keep, as a resolving synonym, a label that its survivor marks `REJECTED_LABEL`. body:
## Source

Found while refreshing CultureMech's vendored MIM label index to `6643131b`. I replayed every recipe label in CultureMech's occurrence table through the old and new pins; the method is from CultureBotAI/CultureMech#417. The pin refresh is a large improvement overall (99% of rows unchanged, and the changes are mostly hydrate-specific corrections). These are the labels where MIM's **current** answer still looks wrong or missing. In each case the old answer was no better, so none of this blocks the pin.

## Wrong form

| CultureMech label | recipe rows | resolves to | problem |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `MnSO4・xH2O` (+ `MnSO4·nH2O`) | 61 | CHEBI:86364, `MnSO4 x 1 H2O` | A variable hydrate resolves to the monohydrate. The variable-sulfate precedent (#646 and others) gives these a local `x n H2O` identity. |
| `NiCl2 x H2O`, `NiCl2・H2O` | ~5 | CHEBI:53542, nickel(II) chloride hexahydrate | A monohydrate label resolves to the hexahydrate. |
| `Trisodium citrate x 3 H2O` | 2 | CHEBI:53258 | A trihydrate label resolves to a non-trihydrate term. |
| `Potassium phosphate` | 4 | CHEBI:63036 | A generic label resolves to one specific potassium phosphate salt. |

The NaH2PO4 monohydrate spellings that resolve to the dihydrate record (~36 rows) are already tracked as #758.

## Missing or ambiguous

- **`sodium nitrate`, 58 rows, unresolved:** ambiguous because the stock-solution record `Sodium nitrate (0.70 M stock)` (`kgmicrobe.ingredient:sodium_nitrate_~28070_m_stock~29`) carries the bare compound name as a synonym next to CHEBI:63005. A stock solution's record shouldn't claim the compound's name.
- **`α-Ketoglutarate`, 3 rows, now unresolved:** #232 correctly retired it from the disodium-salt record as `REJECTED_LABEL`, but no record now claims the anion or acid name.
- **`Sea Salt`, now unindexed:** the old pin had it ambiguous through two `ontology_label` rows. Either way it got no identity, but no record claims generic sea salt.

The full replay table is in the CultureMech pin-refresh PR description.

## More from the CultureMech#537 review (same replay)

- **`MgSO4 x H2O` (12 rows) and `MgSO4 . H2O` (1) → CHEBI:31795, magnesium sulfate *heptahydrate*.** These resolve as trusted `mim_exact` through a REJECTED tombstone row on `Mgso47h2o.yaml` that carries the monohydrate label. Under the old pin they were flagged ambiguous; now they're confidently wrong, and KGX emits the edge.
- **`Na2MoO4.H2O`, `Na2MoO4 . H2O`, `Na2MoO4 · H2O` (3 rows) → CHEBI:75213, the *dihydrate*,** by the same tombstone-row pattern.
- **`sodium glutarate` (1 row): a regression.** It used to resolve to `cas:13521-83-0` (disodium glutarate). MIM no longer indexes that `ontology_label`, so CultureMech falls back to the recipe's local CHEBI:24329, the glutarate anion: a salt collapsed onto its parent.
- **NaH2PO4 monohydrate spellings split:** `NaH2PO4•H2O` → CHEBI:114249 (the monohydrate), while `NaH2PO4 x H2O` / `·H2O` go to the dihydrate record (#758). Two spellings of one substance get different identities.

Root pattern for the first two: merge tombstones keep raw labels naming a *different hydrate* than their survivor, and the label index publishes them as REJECTED rows that consumers follow by contract.

## From the unified-mapping fix (culturebotai-claw#571)

- **`MgSO .7H O` (17 occurrences)** is a safe (`unique`) synonym on the *anhydrous* Magnesium sulfate record (CHEBI:32599), but it's a garbled heptahydrate label. Its recipes carry the correct heptahydrate CHEBI:31795. Now that the unified mapping follows MIM's label index, this MIM synonym placement decides the published identity.
- **`Na2HPO4·7H2O`** has no label-index row; only other spellings of the heptahydrate are indexed. So its recipes' anhydrous CHEBI:34683 still wins (MIM#808).

## From the claw#571 review: MIM record and synonym defects that now decide unified-mapping identities

| label (occurrences) | MIM's `unique` answer | problem |
|---|---|---|
| `DL-Tryptophan` (4) | record `DL-Tryptophan` on CHEBI:57912 | CHEBI:57912 is the L-tryptophan zwitterion, so the racemate is recorded as an enantiomer |
| `Na2-DL-malate`, `Sodium DL-malate`, `Na-DL-malate` and others (26) | `Sodium malate`, CHEBI:91261 | DL labels sit on a disodium (S)-malate identity |
| `Na2SiO3` (8) | synonym on `Na2SiO3 x 9 H2O` (CHEBI:132108) | an anhydrous formula label on the nonahydrate |
| `Magnesium Chloride` (5) | record `Magnesium chloride` = CHEBI:86345 | a generic name owns the hexahydrate identity |
| `MgSO .7H O` (17) | synonym on anhydrous `Magnesium sulfate` | a garbled heptahydrate label (noted above) |

## From the second claw#571 review

- **Sodium malate family** (`Sodium malate` 14, `Sodium DL-malate` 11, `Na2-DL-malate` 6, `Na-malate` 6, `Na malate` 4, `Na-DL-malate` 4, `DL-Na-malate` 3, `DL-Sodium malate` 2; 50 occurrences): MIM's `Sodium malate` record sits on CHEBI:91261, disodium **(S)**-malate, while the labels are racemic or stereo-unspecified. The recipes carry CHEBI:91260 (disodium malate).
- **`H3BO2`** (3): an unreviewed import record grounds this (likely a typo for H3BO3, boric acid) to boronic acid CHEBI:38267.


## Update 2026-10-14 (second review of #881)

**Fixed in #881:**
- `MgSO4 x H2O`, `MgSO4 . H2O` and `MgSO4・H2O` now resolve to the monohydrate `cas:14168-73-1` (#893).
- `MgSO .7H O` now resolves to the heptahydrate CHEBI:31795 (#899).

**Still open, same class, from the label index on #881's head:**

Damaged-subscript formula labels resolving to the anhydrous form or to a different compound:

| label | `label_index.csv` answer | CultureMech recipe rows |
|---|---|---:|
| `CaCl .6H O` | CHEBI:3312, anhydrous CaCl2 | 5 |
| `ZnCl .6H O` | CHEBI:49976, anhydrous ZnCl2 | 3 |
| `EDTA.Na .2H O` | CHEBI:64734 (`Na2-EDTA`) | 3 |
| `CoCl .6H O` | CHEBI:35696, anhydrous CoCl2 | 0 |
| `FeSO .7H O` | CHEBI:75832, anhydrous FeSO4 | 0 |
| `LiCl.H O` | CHEBI:48607, anhydrous LiCl | 0 |
| `NaH PO .2H O` | CHEBI:37585, anhydrous NaH2PO4 | 0 |
| `ZnSO .7H O` | CHEBI:86463 (`AlK(SO4)2`), a different compound | 0 |
| `Na SiO .9H O` | CHEBI:86463 (`AlK(SO4)2`), a different compound | 0 |

Water-ratio names resolving to a different hydrate:
- `cobalt(2+) sulfate--water (1/7)` → CHEBI:53470, anhydrous CoSO4;
- `Cobalt(II) chloride--water (1/7)` → CHEBI:53503, the hexahydrate.

**Consistency question, not an explicit contradiction:** `Mgso4_X_7_H2o` carries four names, all ChEBI related synonyms of CHEBI:32599:
- `magnesium sulphate`;
- `magnesium(II) sulfate`;

They resolve to the heptahydrate, while `Magnesium sulfate` resolves to the anhydrous form. Semantic-review finding SEM:f345b845583ac48792ef is open on this.

body:
## Problem

Four merge tombstones from the 2026-09-21 semantic review (#722) still carry their **old, rejected identity** as `identifier`, not their merge target:

| record | `identifier` (published) | merged into (per its `MERGED_INTO` event) |
|---|---|---|
| `Nano.yaml` (label `NaNO`) | `NCIT:C54713`, the *nano* unit prefix | `CHEBI:63005` (NaNO3) |
| `Atrazin.yaml` | `cas:1924-24-9` (an erroneous CAS) | `CHEBI:15930` (atrazine) |
| `Edta_Chelating_Agent.yaml` | `NCIT:C360` (chelating agents, a class) | `CHEBI:4735` (EDTA) |
| `Sodium_Phosphate_Dibasic.yaml` | `CHEBI:37583` (trisodium phosphate) | `CHEBI:34683` (Na2HPO4) |

`docs/LABEL_INDEX_CONTRACT.md` says: *"For a **merged** record the `identifier` already points at the merge target, so the row still resolves correctly and should be followed."* These four rows break that rule. A consumer that follows REJECTED rows, as the contract tells it to, resolves `NaNO` to the nano prefix and `Sodium phosphate dibasic` to trisodium phosphate. No live MAPPED row holds any of the four identifiers.

## How it surfaced

CultureMech's label-index reader refuses a pin with dangling tombstones. Once CultureBotAI/CultureMech#520 lets it read `AMBIGUOUS` rows, a preview refresh against MIM `7a65c4e9` fails with:

```
LabelIndexError: REJECTED merge tombstone identifier is not held by a live MAPPED row: CHEBI:37583, NCIT:C360, NCIT:C54713, cas:1924-24-9
```

So this now blocks CultureMech's MIM pin, which is 106 commits behind.

## Proposed fix

Point each tombstone's `identifier` at its merge target. Keep the original fields on the tombstone, as the merge events say they should be kept, and record the old identifier in the `curation_history` event. Every one of these record changes needs a `mapping_changes/` receipt through the review chain. Also add a MIM-side gate so a merge tombstone whose identifier no live record holds can't land (CultureMech already enforces this as a consumer).
title: Four 2026-09-21 merge tombstones keep their rejected identity instead of the merge target, breaking the label-index contract

They are the ones most within reach:

- [ ] **`site_contract`** — CLAW's reason: "Publishes a site built in CI, so no directory in the checkout is the output the check would judge; running it on the Jekyll or template sources reports missing .html files that the build creates. - [ ] **`source_catalogue`** — CLAW's reason: "Fetches ontologies through download_ontologies.py rather than a declared catalogue, so there is no download.yaml to validate. Adopting one would apply here; it has not been written."
- [ ] **`kgx_export`** — publish the corpus as a validated KGX node and edge set for kg-microbe. KGX and SSSOM export apply to every Mech in the fleet, whatever the current declaration says; CLAW's declaration for this Mech is to be updated to match (culturebotai-claw#359).

Each adoption also means flipping the declaration to `enabled` in claw's `fleet.yaml`; culturebotai-claw#359 tracks closing the disabled declarations fleet-wide. The capability matrix on https://culturebotai.github.io/mechs/ shows these states.

body:
## Finding

#310 normalized five zero-padded CAS identifiers, but the conclusion drawn from the padded form was never revisited. Each record's evidence note (at dfce1c9) still reads "CAS-RN 0124-09-4 present, but no CHEBI entry exists (checked OAK CHEBI sqlite + PubChem CID synonyms)". The same pattern appears for the other padded numbers.

ChEBI has exact, current (non-obsolete) terms for four of them. Each carries the unpadded CAS as a cross-reference and the ingredient's own name as a label or synonym:

| Record (`data/ingredients/mapped/`) | Primary now | ChEBI term |
|---|---|---|
| `16-Hexanediamine.yaml` | `cas:124-09-4` | CHEBI:39618 hexane-1,6-diamine (synonym "1,6-hexanediamine") |
| `2-6-dihydroxybenzoic_Acid.yaml` | `cas:303-07-1` | CHEBI:68465 2,6-dihydroxybenzoic acid |
| `Aesculetin.yaml` | `cas:305-01-1` | CHEBI:490095 esculetin (synonym "Aesculetin") |
| `Indole-3-pyruvic_Acid.yaml` | `cas:392-12-1` | CHEBI:29750 3-(indol-3-yl)pyruvic acid (synonym "indole-3-pyruvic acid") |

No MAPPED record holds any of these four terms. CHEBI:490095 appears only in `unmapped/Esculin_Hydrolysate.yaml`.

The fifth, `Methyl-beta-D-xylopyranoside.yaml` (`cas:612-05-5`), has CHEBI:74863. That term is already the EXACT_MATCH primary of `Methyl_Beta-D-xylopyranoside.yaml`, so the two records look like duplicates.

Separately, the CAS-fallback notes say only ChEBI was checked. About 18 of the 84 `cas:` primaries match a current MeSH record by registry number (for example C007297 1,6-diaminohexane, C007628 esculetin, C060525 leucrose). MeSH is already a primary vocabulary for 92 MAPPED records.

## Suggested fix

- Re-resolve the four records to their ChEBI terms through the usual identifier-change path and collision guard, with a `curation_history` entry each.
- Merge or reject the methyl-beta-D-xylopyranoside duplicate.
- Consider a MeSH pass over the remaining `cas:` fallbacks before treating them as having no term.

Found while checking how the CultureBotAI site describes MIM's mappings (CultureBotAI.github.io#215, #150).
title: Four cas:-primary records have exact ChEBI terms; their 'no CHEBI entry' check ran on the zero-padded CAS

body:
Found while auditing the CultureBotAI X-Mech page (https://culturebotai.github.io/mechs/), tracked in https://github.com/CultureBotAI/CultureBotAI.github.io/issues/147. Everything below was re-checked against `main` at `1848b0f` (2026-09-25).

## 1. Schema headers say MIT; the package and README say CC0-1.0

All three schema modules this repository owns declare MIT:

| file (at `1848b0f`) | line | declares |
|---|---|---|
| [`src/mediaingredientmech/schema/mediaingredientmech.yaml`](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/blob/1848b0f/src/mediaingredientmech/schema/mediaingredientmech.yaml#L8) | 8 | `license: MIT` |
| [`src/mediaingredientmech/schema/mapped_ingredients_schema.yaml`](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/blob/1848b0f/src/mediaingredientmech/schema/mapped_ingredients_schema.yaml#L9) | 9 | `license: MIT` |
| [`src/mediaingredientmech/schema/unmapped_ingredients_schema.yaml`](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/blob/1848b0f/src/mediaingredientmech/schema/unmapped_ingredients_schema.yaml#L8) | 8 | `license: MIT` |
| [`src/mediaingredientmech/schema/mapped_ingredients_schema.py`](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/blob/1848b0f/src/mediaingredientmech/schema/mapped_ingredients_schema.py#L7) (generated) | 7 | `# license: MIT` |

The rest of the repository says CC0-1.0:

```
pyproject.toml:9    license = {text = "CC0-1.0"}
pyproject.toml:23   "License :: CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication",
README.md:166-168   ## License
                    CC0-1.0 - Public Domain Dedication
```

The two modules vendored from claw into the same directory declare licences of their own: [`history.yaml:29`](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/blob/1848b0f/src/mediaingredientmech/schema/history.yaml#L29) has `license: BSD-3-Clause` and [`mech_shared.yaml:33`](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/blob/1848b0f/src/mediaingredientmech/schema/mech_shared.yaml#L33) has `license: https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/`. The main schema declares MIT but imports `mech_shared`, so the schema set as a whole names three licences.

### Why it matters

- MIT and CC0-1.0 grant different things. MIT requires the copyright and permission notice to be kept; CC0 waives all rights. A reader of the schema, or of anything LinkML generates from it (Python datamodel, JSON Schema, docs), sees MIT. A reader of the package metadata sees CC0. GitHub reports no licence at all (see section 2).
- With no LICENSE file in the tree, these metadata strings are the only licence statements the repository makes, so the conflict cannot be settled by pointing at an authoritative file.
- The public fleet page renders `CC0-1.0` for this repository (`CultureBotAI.github.io/_fleet/fleet_fragment.html`). That string only reflects the README and pyproject, not the schema.

### Suggested fix

1. Once #627 settles the licence split (the fleet rule in CultureBotAI/culturebotai-claw#394 is code BSD-3-Clause, data CC0-1.0), set `license:` in the three MIM-owned schema modules to match. Use the same spelling as the rest of the repository: an SPDX identifier or the licence URI, one or the other throughout.
2. Regenerate `mapped_ingredients_schema.py` (and any other generated artifacts) so the MIT header goes away.
3. Leave `history.yaml` and `mech_shared.yaml` alone locally. They are vendored and sha-pinned (culturebotai-claw#7), so any change to their `license:` belongs in claw and gets re-vendored from there.
4. Optionally, add a test asserting that every MIM-owned schema's `license:` matches `pyproject.toml` / `LICENSE`, so the two cannot drift apart again.

## 2. No LICENSE file (already tracked in #627)

Re-verified for context, not re-filed. The recursive tree at `1848b0f` (6,744 files, not truncated) has no `LICENSE*`, `LICENCE*`, `COPYING*` or `NOTICE*` file. `GET /repos/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/license` returns 404, and the repository's `license` field is `null`. #627 already proposes `LICENSE` (BSD-3-Clause, code) and `LICENSE-DATA` (CC0-1.0, records). Resolving section 1 in the same change would make the schema headers, pyproject, README and licence files agree in one step.
title: LinkML schemas declare `license: MIT` while pyproject.toml and README say CC0-1.0

During review of the #769/#770 bundle implementation, adversarial fixtures reproduced three gaps beyond ordinary checksum/evidence validation:

- A matching review proof could use an envelope claim ID that differs from the payload's stable mapping/annotation/product/occurrence ID.
- An active registry xref or supported occurrence could reference a product whose own review is WITHHOLD.
- Surrounding whitespace in a raw source status such as ` SUPERSEDED ` bypassed historical-status recognition.

Reproduction: seven failures and one passing inactive-history control in `tests/test_ingredient_bundle.py` (`claim_envelope`, `supported_facts`, `whitespace_cannot`). The synthetic fixtures intentionally update review proofs to exercise semantic invariants independently of payload hashes; no scientific source decisions were changed.

Acceptance:

- [ ] Bind envelope IDs to the kind-specific stable payload ID.
- [ ] Reject active xrefs and supported occurrence/product associations through withheld products; retain inactive history without activation.
- [ ] Recognize historical statuses after whitespace/case normalization while retaining original source text.
- [ ] Keep all original case, owner, evidence and artifact-reconstruction tests passing.

Related: #767, #769, #770; consumer activation in Knowledge-Graph-Hub/kg-microbe#1134 and #1135.

body:
Review round 1 of [#768](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/768) found two interoperability defects in the initial local scope-profile implementation, before publication or consumer activation.

- Extension definitions currently use full IRIs for `property`. The [SSSOM 1.0 TSV rules](https://mapping-commons.github.io/sssom/1.0/spec-formats-tsv/#non-standard-slots) require resolvable CURIEs for definition properties/type hints. Emit compact declared properties such as `mimprofile:subjectScope`.
- A row-level `mimprofile:ingredient-scope/v1` and its identical full-IRI mapping-set default are rejected as conflicting because the validator compares raw strings. Reproduction against the round-1 module returns `ValueError: Conflicting row and mapping-set scope profiles`. Normalize declarations through the CURIE map before comparing.

Acceptance: correct both forms without weakening scope/authorization checks; add compact/full-IRI equivalence, conflicting-prefix/property and standard-parser serialization/reload checks preserving every declared extension and value. Validate the published TSV syntax separately from the in-memory URI representation.

The installed third-party SSSOM parser (sssom 0.4.21 with sssom-schema 1.1.0a5) also has an inverted strict-metadata predicate: `_is_irregular_metadata` returns False for a valid standard-only header, while `_fail_in_strict_parsing_mode` treats False as invalid. Record this environment limitation precisely; it does not justify disabling our profile checks or claiming a strict parser pass. A real non-strict parser round-trip plus explicit standard/extension validation can test interoperability while the dependency issue is assessed.

Parent roadmap: [#767](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/767). Resolve before merging #768 or activating the consumer contract.
title: Review scope-profile CURIE declarations and SSSOM serialization before activation

body:
Generic ingredient mapping must not erase the product/preparation reported by a source. Existing supplied-form and recipe evidence preserves this distinction, but it needs a structured, versioned export for KG-Microbe.

Tracking: https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/767. Depends on https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/768; publish alongside the manifest/annotation contract in https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/769.

## Deliverables and acceptance

- [ ] Define stable source occurrence and supplied-form identifiers, with links to the generic ingredient, source recipe/observation, original label, evidence, supplier, catalog number and known preparation/grade. Preserve source detail and uncertainty without inventing lot identities.
- [ ] Model product alternatives explicitly. Preserve `CultureMech:015191`'s Sigma A9647 **or** A7409 as alternatives, not simultaneous confirmed ingredients, interchangeable identities or a pipe list with unspecified semantics.
- [ ] Retain all seven reviewed BSA recipe memberships and their own amounts/preparation notes. Sigma A7030 belongs only to its reporting source; do not propagate its heat-shock/low-fatty-acid/protease qualifiers to every BSA occurrence.
- [ ] Document when occurrence qualifiers suffice and when a separately identified product/material is required because its identity or associated facts differ. A catalog product, a generic ingredient, a stock solution and an individual lot must not be conflated.
- [ ] Keep supplier/catalog fields out of generic ingredient exact synonyms and identity xrefs. A CAS shared by products does not equate those products; a catalog number alone does not establish molecular identity.
- [ ] Export deterministic source-linked records with an explicit alternatives/unknown-value contract and schema version. Bind them into the common release manifest and existing evidence/review process, with owner and reference validation.
- [ ] Add fixtures for the seven BSA occurrences, A9647-or-A7409, distinct products sharing a CAS, missing product information, and unresolved Sorbitan material. Preserve original source payloads and stable recipe references.

Implementation starts from `supplied_form` in `src/mediaingredientmech/schema/mediaingredientmech.yaml` and the existing occurrence/source evidence; do not overwrite source-specific claims with the shared ingredient's attributes.

Evidence and boundaries: [BSA source review](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/tree/ea697252223774072a188ae3ec23a0e2adea0778/reports/sssom_completion_20260921/mapping_review/identity-review-20260924), [#762](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/762). [#449](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/449) owns the broader recipe-membership import defect; preserve/reuse that work. Sorbitan identity evidence remains under [#761](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/761).
title: Export occurrence-specific supplied forms and preserve product alternatives

CAS annotations currently reach KG-Microbe through reviewed case-specific policy, while source-qualified registry history is retained in curation evidence. Export a general identifier-annotation artifact so current xrefs, historical claims and their owners/provenance survive together without converting every registry link into identity.

Tracking: https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/767. Depends on the scope contract in https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/768; coordinate the occurrence artifact under the same bundle contract.

## Deliverables and acceptance

- [ ] Define and export `ingredient_identifier_annotations.tsv` (or a documented equivalent) with one identifiable claim per owner/identifier/source/status combination. Include annotation ID, owning entity ID, identifier, identifier scope, source status, source identifier, source version/retrieval date, evidence, curation review status and reviewed xref eligibility.
- [ ] Keep source status distinct from our review status. A well-supported FDA SUPERSEDED claim remains useful historical evidence without becoming an active xref. Preserve conflicting source claims separately; a source-specific status is not a global CAS withdrawal ruling.
- [ ] Populate evidence-backed examples: Acriflavine NCIT:C76253 has FDA PRIMARY cas:65589-70-0 and SUPERSEDED cas:8048-52-0; BSA NCIT:C85253 has FDA GENERIC (FAMILY) cas:9048-46-8; explicit SV CHEBI:29673 has cas:6998-60-3, while generic rifamycin CHEBI:26580 receives no single CAS.

- [ ] Publish a versioned manifest binding the profile, supported SSSOM, annotation artifact and declared occurrence artifact/schema by content digest. Record exporter/review provenance, required capabilities and explicit presence/absence of optional artifacts. Build deterministically and publish immutable releases.
- [ ] Bind annotation approvals to their complete content and owner; changes invalidate the relevant review. Check referential integrity and reject missing/mismatched required bundle members.
- [ ] Add exporter/validation fixtures proving current versus historical eligibility, conflicting-source retention, stable annotation IDs and exact reconstruction of each claim tuple. Parallel pipe-separated CAS/status/source lists are not an acceptable representation.

Use the existing semantic release and receipt infrastructure, not an independent approval mechanism. Migrate reviewed case-specific data from [#762](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/762) without reopening completed identity decisions or changing published historical files.

body:
The reviewed mappings distinguish generic rifamycin from SV and generic trait xanthine from MIM's ingredient, but the general contract still relies on comments and case-specific consumer policy. Define a machine-readable scope profile so consumers can determine whether a mapping authorizes ID replacement, a broader alignment, or neither.

Tracking: https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/767. Priority: foundation; coordinate with KG-Microbe before enabling the profile.

## Deliverables and acceptance

- [ ] Define controlled scope vocabulary and explicit unknown/missing behavior for chemical families, defined substances, mixtures, preparations and catalog products. Document overlapping axes; do not infer scope from identifier namespace, CAS presence or `subject_type=owl:Class`.
- [ ] Declare application extension slots such as `ext_subject_scope` and `ext_object_scope` through SSSOM `extension_definitions`, with property IRIs, datatypes, profile version and examples. These are application fields, not existing SSSOM standard slots.
- [ ] Specify which reviewed predicate/scope combinations may support canonical ID replacement. An exactMatch is not automatically sameAs; closeMatch, broadMatch, narrowMatch and annotation claims do not automatically authorize identity substitution. A CAS exact mapping is permitted only after independent same-scope review.
- [ ] Keep source occurrence resolution separate from concept alignment. Preserve distinct scoped source concepts for generic Xanthine/CHEBI:15318 and MIM:Xanthine/CHEBI:17712; comments or context columns must not make two conflicting exact mappings from the same subject conditionally true.

Implementation anchors: `src/mediaingredientmech/schema/mediaingredientmech.yaml`, `mappings/ingredient_mappings.sssom.tsv`, `MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md`, `src/mediaingredientmech/export/reviewed_sssom.py` and semantic-release validation.

Coordinate with existing [#478](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/478) on composition versus granularity and [#294](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/294) on source-material annotations. [#734](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/734) owns MIM's broad-match KGX projection correction.

body:
Ingredient scope, canonical identifier choice and source-specific supplied products need separate, machine-readable representations. A generic ingredient must remain queryable without making every catalog preparation equivalent to it, and verified CAS annotations must remain available without becoming automatic identity substitutions.

This tracks the general producer/consumer contract following the case-specific work in [MIM PR #754](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/pull/754), [KG-Microbe PR #1130](https://github.com/Knowledge-Graph-Hub/kg-microbe/pull/1130) and [NCIT CAS export PR #1131](https://github.com/Knowledge-Graph-Hub/kg-microbe/pull/1131). MIM #754 merged on 2026-09-25; KG-Microbe #1130 and #1131 are ready with passing CI and await independent approval. Production promotion remains under KG-Microbe #1123.

## Required behavior

| Source meaning | Canonical identity | Annotation/context |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unqualified rifamycin observation | CHEBI:26580 | Family scope; no single CAS; no inference of activity against every member. |
| Explicit rifamycin SV | CHEBI:29673 | Verified xref cas:6998-60-3. |
| Generic bovine serum albumin | NCIT:C85253 | Verified xref cas:9048-46-8; supplier/preparation remains source-specific. |
| Reviewed MIM xanthine ingredient | CHEBI:17712 | Verified xref cas:69-89-6; retain the reviewed ingredient scope. |
| Generic xanthine trait observation | CHEBI:15318 | Do not inherit 9H specificity or the ingredient's CAS annotation. |

A CAS RN denotes a registered substance/material; a supplier catalog number identifies a commercial product specification. Neither namespace alone establishes scope. SSSOM's logical type slots do not distinguish chemical families from specific chemical concepts. Our canonicalization policy must require reviewed matching scope; SKOS exactMatch is not OWL sameAs and broadMatch does not by itself entail subclass_of.

## Work packages

MIM implementation is merged in #772, #773 and #775, following case-specific #754. The KG-Microbe stack is implemented, fully tested and ready for independent GitHub approval; its default-branch protection remains the merge gate.

- [x] [MIM: scope profile and canonicalization contract](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/768)
- [x] [MIM: identifier annotations and versioned release manifest](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/769)
- [x] [MIM: occurrence-specific supplied forms and product alternatives](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/770)
- [ ] [KG-Microbe: identity predicate and scope guard](https://github.com/Knowledge-Graph-Hub/kg-microbe/issues/1133)
- [ ] [KG-Microbe: scope/registry bundle consumer](https://github.com/Knowledge-Graph-Hub/kg-microbe/issues/1134)
- [ ] [KG-Microbe: product/occurrence preservation through KGX merge](https://github.com/Knowledge-Graph-Hub/kg-microbe/issues/1135)
- [ ] [KG-Microbe: end-to-end acceptance and profile activation gate](https://github.com/Knowledge-Graph-Hub/kg-microbe/issues/1136)
- [ ] Existing classification work: [MIM #734](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/734) and [KG-Microbe PR #1120](https://github.com/Knowledge-Graph-Hub/kg-microbe/pull/1120). Reuse this work; broad parent anchors must remain broad mappings unless independently supported classification is asserted.

## Sequencing and closure

1. Start the identity-predicate guard and shared scope contract first. The guard can begin independently; its final scope policy follows the agreed profile.
2. Implement the MIM annotation and occurrence exports against that contract, then their KG-Microbe consumers.
3. Complete the existing broad-match projection work and run a producer-to-transform-to-merge fixture using immutable inputs.
4. Enable the new profile only after all required capabilities, bundle hashes, owner-bound reviews and round-trip checks agree. Keep legacy compatibility explicit and auditable.

Closure requires a published contract, reproducible linked artifacts, reviewed handling of conflicts/unknown scope, preserved source alternatives/history, and verified KGX output. Shared CAS must not merge distinct product IDs; parent mappings must not manufacture identity or classification; uncertain materials retain local identities.

Existing case curation remains in [MIM #760](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/760), [MIM #762](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/762) and [KG-Microbe #1132](https://github.com/Knowledge-Graph-Hub/kg-microbe/issues/1132). Lysozyme and Sorbitan evidence holds remain [#753](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/753) and [#761](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/761). Existing-release production promotion remains governed by [KG-Microbe #1123](https://github.com/Knowledge-Graph-Hub/kg-microbe/issues/1123); this roadmap does not silently add every future product feature to that existing gate.

Design basis: the 2026-09-24 representation review at `reports/kgmicrobe_sssom_feedback_20260922/ingredient-identities/REPRESENTATION.md` in the local MIM workspace. The requirements above and the linked issues are self-contained; that local report is not required to access the plan.

body:
Review finding on #764 (read-only pass), not fixed there.

`build_review.py` lists `src/mediaingredientmech/validation/semantic_release.py` and, since #764, `src/mediaingredientmech/validation/mapping_change_receipts.py` in `proof_files`, so `current-review.json` `inputs` pins both and `validate()` verifies every listed hash ("Stale review input"). But `validate()` only *requires* the mapping review (`mapping_review_path in inputs`), the receipts (`set(receipt_names) <= inputs.keys()`, #764) and each resolution's evidence. A report that simply omits the gate's own module or the receipts module from `inputs` still passes, so the code that decides supersession and hold lineage is not itself bound by the report it validates.

Suggested fix: `require` both module paths in `inputs` in `validate()`, and extend the `reviewed_bundle` fixture in `tests/test_semantic_release.py` to list them (it currently pins only the artifacts it creates), with an adversarial case that drops one.

Related: #764, #745, #718.
title: Semantic gate does not require its own code (semantic_release.py, mapping_change_receipts.py) among the hash-bound review inputs

body:
Review finding on #764 (read-only pass), fixed in that PR.

`mapping_change_receipts._edge_id_at` re-derived a mapping edge's `MIM.assertion:` id at its baseline SSSOM position by hashing the edge row as read from `mim_edges.tsv` (minus `id`). But `kgx.Graph.edge` hashes the row it *built*, which for the mapping kind carries only the base columns, while `_write_tsv` emits every `EDGE_COLUMNS` entry, so the TSV row has `publications`, `metabolic_context`, `reference_scope`, `concentration_value`, `concentration_unit`, `completeness` and `assertion_method` as empty strings. Recomputing from the TSV reproduced **0 of 3,026** mapping edge ids on the real bundle, so `hold_lineage` could never match a moved hold and the gate would keep failing on any row removal above position 437 — the failure #745 set out to remove — silently, since an empty lineage just falls back to the exact-id check.

The unit test caught nothing because it compared against an in-memory `Graph` edge, which has the same key set as the hashed row.

Fix (in #764): hash exactly `MAPPING_EDGE_KEYS` (the eleven base columns a mapping edge carries), and add a TSV-shaped case to `tests/test_mapping_change_receipts.py::test_recomputed_ids_match_the_gate_and_the_exporter`. Verified on the real bundle: 3,026 / 3,026 mapping edge ids reproduce at their own position.

Note for anyone extending the lineage to role or component edges: those kinds are created with explicit optional fields, some of them empty strings, so the same recomputation would need the exporter's per-kind field list rather than "drop empty".

Related: #745, #764.
title: hold_lineage recomputed KGX edge ids from the TSV row, which carries empty optional columns the exporter never hashed

body:
The kg-microbe #1123 name-disagreement review exposed an invalid Lysozyme CAS identifier. An arithmetic check of the current supported MIM candidate found three invalid CAS RNs:

| Subject | Published target | Calculated check digit | Stored digit |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| MIM:Izalpinin | cas:480-14-4 | 8 | 4 |
| MIM:Lysozyme | cas:2650-88-3 | 6 | 3 |
| MIM:Methyl-2-Hydroxy-Phenylproprionate | cas:89471-28-0 | 3 | 0 |

Checked against main `5019d6871fe0b0f47eccd50f9d0c169c98c40484` and the proposed #752 mapping-only follow-up. [CAS documents its check-digit method](https://www.cas.org/es-es/training/documentation/chemical-substances/checkdig): multiply the digits before the final check digit from right to left by 1, 2, ... and take the sum modulo 10. For Lysozyme, `8*1+8*2+0*3+5*4+6*5+2*6 = 86`, giving 6 rather than 3.

A valid checksum does not establish chemical identity. Do not repair these by substituting the calculated digit: a missing or substituted earlier digit is also possible. Lysozyme needs source/form review, not forced equivalence with FOODON:03413135 merely to clear a downstream disagreement.

Immediate containment: add exact row/owner-bound WITHHOLD decisions for these three CAS assertions while preserving the complete source payloads and unrelated local-identifier assertions. Historical/published release files stay immutable.

Remaining acceptance: inspect original source records, independently verify the intended compounds/materials and replacement identifiers, correct YAML/SSSOM via the existing mapping-change receipt chain, and explicitly re-review corrected rows. Add a supported-release CAS check-digit gate to prevent recurrence without confusing syntactic validity with identity approval. This issue remains open until source correction and the permanent gate are complete.

Related: #752 and https://github.com/Knowledge-Graph-Hub/kg-microbe/issues/1123.
title: Correct three supported CAS assertions with invalid check digits

Review findings on #746 (read-only pass).

1. **Stale `object_label` on a registry row.** `MIM:Anisodamine_Hydrobromide` had its `subject_label` corrected to `Anisodamine Hydrobromide` on all three rows, and the `cas:` row was rewritten, but the `kgmicrobe.compound:anisodamine_hydrobromide` row still carries `object_label = "Anisodamine Hydrobromide ()"`, the old label with the ingest artefact. Registry rows take the record's `preferred_term` as their object label; the finish step must rewrite it for a relabelled subject.

2. **Old-term synonyms still published through `other`.** When the own-identifier row's object moves to a different term (ammonium molybdate CHEBI:91249 → CHEBI:86244, acridine orange, 4-hydroxynonenal, aluminium sulfate, bisabolene, ferulate), `reconcile_sssom` rewrites the object but leaves `other` as the enrichment builder filled it for the *old* term. `MIM:Ammonium_Molybdate_Tetrahydrate → CHEBI:86244` therefore still lists `Diammonium molybdate`, a name of the orthomolybdate the row just left. Under Section 1 a synonym channel token must name the row's substance; the finish step should drop every `other` token that is a name of the old term and not of the new one (and not a resolving synonym on the record).

Both are `--finish-sssom` defects in `scripts/apply_312_batch2.py`; fix there and regenerate the receipt/chain.
title: Batch-2 finish step leaves the old identity's traces on sibling rows: stale object_label on a relabelled subject's registry row, old-term synonyms in other

body:
Found while applying #312 batch 2.

`src/mediaingredientmech/validation/semantic_release.py` computes every current assertion id as `sha256([source, kind, position, payload_sha])`, and `FROZEN_RELEASE_HOLD_RESOLUTIONS` pins the resolution of `MIM.hold:724-aromatic-trait-synonym` to one such id (`Aromatic_Compound`, SSSOM position 437 at the time). The gate then requires a current assertion with exactly that id:

```
ValueError: Resolved release hold has no matching current assertion
```

Any change that removes an SSSOM row before position 437 shifts every later row, changes the id, and fails the resolution build, even though the hold's row, owner and payload are untouched. Batch 2 hit this by dropping the three `kgmicrobe.compound` registry rows that Section 3 step 1 makes redundant when a `broadMatch` parent is promoted to the identity (the #326 precedent for 72-Dihydroxyflavone). The batch keeps those rows instead, which is a new shape (no other ontology-identified subject carries a registry `exactMatch` row).

Consequences:
- the three promoted records (34-Dihydroxyflavone, Anisodamine_Hydrobromide, Apramycin_Sulfate_Salt) carry a redundant `kgmicrobe.compound` row until this is fixed;
- the merge batch of #312 (6-deoxy-d-galactose → D-fucose at row 286, before the pinned position) cannot remove the merged record's rows at all;
- the completion lock already handles this: `mapping_changes/*.json` receipts carry a `position_map`, and `assemble_review.py` maps its pinned positions (437, 439) through the chain. The resolution gate needs the same: resolve a frozen hold's assertion by mapping its baseline position through the receipts (or bind holds to `(owner, payload_sha)` instead of position), without loosening what the hold asserts.

Related: #312, #724, #725, #740.
title: Frozen release-hold resolutions bind to SSSOM row positions, so no row can be removed above them (blocks dropping redundant registry rows and every merge)

Found on #739: every local gate in the CLAUDE.md validation sequence passed (`validate-all`, `qc-sssom`, `qc-roundtrip`, `qc-flat-coverage`, plus `validate-products`, `qc-evidence`, `qc-duplicate-ids`, `qc-component-partonomy`, `check-instruction-refs`, `check-curation-targets`), yet the required `roundtrip` check failed in CI.

`.github/workflows/qc-roundtrip.yaml` runs a step the justfile recipe does not:

```
- name: Published visualizations name records that exist
  run: uv run python scripts/check_visualization_currency.py --strict
```

`docs/data/ingredient_umap.json` and `ingredient_graph.json` embed each record's `ontology_id`, `ontology_label` and `mapping_quality`, so any mapping edit stales them, and only CI says so. `just qc-flat-coverage` covers the other `docs/data/` producers (`export-lists`, `export-browser`) but not these two (`generate-visualizations`, ~45 s, non-deterministic coordinates).

Fix: add the currency check to `just qc-roundtrip` (or to `qc-flat-coverage`, next to the other stale-artifact checks) so the local sequence in CLAUDE.md predicts CI, and mention `just generate-visualizations` in the CLAUDE.md validation step 4 remedy list.

**Second gap, same job.** The workflow also runs `just export-indexes` (`scripts/generate_index_files.py`) and fails if `data/curated/*_index.{csv,json}`, `ALL_INGREDIENTS.md` or `MAPPED_INGREDIENTS.md` change. Neither `qc-roundtrip` nor `sync-curated` regenerates them, so a per-record mapping edit that passes every local gate fails CI twice, on two different CI-only steps. Both belong in the local recipe (or `sync-curated` should regenerate the indexes it makes stale).

body:
Review finding on #739 (read-only pass).

`assemble_review.py` builds `mapping_changed_rows` keyed by the row's current position, keeping only the **last** receipt that touched it, and then in the disposition loop compares that receipt's `before` payload to the synonym-refresh `after` (or the baseline row):

```python
expected_before = correction.get("after", previous_mapping)
if mapping_change["before"] != expected_before:
    raise ValueError("Mapping-change receipt does not chain from the reviewed row")
```

For a row corrected in batch 1 and again in batch 2, batch 2's `before` is batch 1's `after`, not the baseline, so a perfectly chained second correction is rejected. Batch 1 (#739) touches no row twice, so it passes; the defect surfaces on the first later batch that revisits a subject.

Fix: verify chaining while walking the receipts in sequence — for each receipt, each `changed`/`added` row's `before` must equal the running state of that row (baseline → synonym refreshes → earlier receipts) — and keep only the final `after` for the loop's `after == mapping` check. That walk belongs in a function so it can be unit-tested with synthetic receipts.
title: assemble_review: a row touched by two mapping-change receipts fails the chain check (before compared to baseline, not to the previous receipt)

body:
From the #312 triage (DEMOTE proposal), re-verified against `chebi.db`; not applied because it is a curator call, not a mechanical fix.

`data/ingredients/mapped/Angustmycin.yaml`: identifier `CHEBI:8612 psicofuranin`, `SYNONYM_MATCH`, preferred_term `Angustmycin`. The authorizing evidence note says "angustmycin A is a historical/trade name for the antibiotic psicofuranin — same molecule". ChEBI disagrees:

- `CHEBI:8612 psicofuranin` (C11H15N5O5, cas 1874-54-0) carries the related synonyms `Angustmycin C`, `Psicofuranin`, `psicofuranine`. It carries **no** bare `Angustmycin` and no `Angustmycin A`.
- `CHEBI:191094 Decoyinine` (C11H13N5O4) is angustmycin A, a different compound.

So the bare label denotes either A or C. The record's `Psicofuranine` RAW_TEXT synonym (absorbed from UNMAPPED_0839 in #213) is legitimately CHEBI:8612; the trait phrase `produces: angustmycin` is already REJECTED_LABEL (#703).

Options, per MAPPING_SEMANTICS Section 3:
1. **Split** (the triage proposal): rename the record to `Psicofuranine` (its raw synonym), keep CHEBI:8612, add `Angustmycin C` as a synonym and move the bare `Angustmycin` off it — but "correct the label, keep the raw string" means a rename is an identity decision, and the source occurrences are 0/0, so there is nothing to disambiguate from.
2. **Step 5**: the label is under-specified and only specific terms exist → `mapping_status: AMBIGUOUS`, no mapping row; keep `Psicofuranine` as a RAW_TEXT synonym pointing readers at CHEBI:8612 in the note.

Either way the evidence note "angustmycin A ... same molecule" must be corrected: it is false.

Related: #312, #213.
title: Angustmycin: bare label is ambiguous between angustmycin A (decoyinine) and C (psicofuranine); record sits on CHEBI:8612 with a false authorizing note

body:
Found while applying #312 batch 1.

`reports/semantic_review_20260921/resolution/build_review.py` builds `identity_support` from `corrections/identity-plan.json` plus `resolution/identities/identity-plan.json` and, in `validate_explicit_plans`, requires `records.get(name) == item["after_record"]` for every plan entry. Any later edit to one of those records, however well verified, makes the build fail with

```
ValueError: Identity plan no longer describes current record: data/ingredients/mapped/Arabinoxylan_Rye_Flour.yaml
```

The record concerned: `Arabinoxylan_Rye_Flour` was given a `kgmicrobe.ingredient` identity on 2026-09-21 (FALLBACK_REGISTRY, no ontology parent). The verified #312 proposal adds the parent anchor `CHEBI:28427 arabinoxylan` (NARROW_MATCH, `skos:broadMatch`, the `Amylopectin_From_Maize` shape; CHEBI:28427 is held by `Wheat_Arabinoxylan` as an identifier so it can only be a parent here). The completion lock solved the same problem with chained receipts (`mapping_changes/`, PR for batch 1). The resolution side needs an equivalent: an identity plan entry must be supersedable by a later, explicit plan entry (or a receipt) rather than freezing the record forever. Until then, every record in `corrections/identity-plan.json` and `resolution/identities/identity-plan.json` is uneditable by any curation batch.

body:
The #245 ruling (recorded in MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md, PR to follow) is: keep `skos:broadMatch` as the parent anchor, no data change, but its meaning is **"form of / closest broader term"**, not strict subsumption. Consumers must emit it as `biolink:broad_match`, not `biolink:subclass_of`.

Measured on `mappings/ingredient_mappings.sssom.tsv` at `c5993f67` against `chebi.db`:

| broadMatch rows | 165 |
|---|---:|
| CHEBI parent | 95 |
| … parent is a fully specified molecule (has InChIKey) | 69 |
| … … salt-named subject | 31 |
| … … hydrate-named subject | 10 |
| … … solution-named subject | 3 |
| … … other (racemates, cation-named salts, polymers, concentrates) | 25 |
| … parent is a class (no InChIKey) | 26 |
| non-CHEBI parent (NCIT 29, mesh 25, FOODON 10, ENVO 4, MICRO 1, UBERON 1) | 70 |

ChEBI relates a salt to its parent acid and a hydrate to its anhydrous form with `has part`, not `is_a`, so a `subclass_of` edge is false in the source ontology for the 69 molecule-parent rows.

Two MIM-side consumers still project `subclass_of` and are **not** changed by the ruling PR, because they are inside the review lock (#729–#731) and the export contract:

- `src/mediaingredientmech/export/kgx.py` (`if pred == "skos:broadMatch": predicate = "biolink:subclass_of"`, plus the `hierarchy` list it feeds), pinned by `tests/test_kgx_export.py` and described in `docs/KGX_EXPORT.md`.
- `reports/semantic_review_20260921/validate_review.py` asserts the same projection for the reviewed bundle `output/mim-kgx-710-full`, and `README.md`/`DECISIONS.md` in that directory state it as the reviewed contract.

To close: switch both to `biolink:broad_match` (relation `skos:broadMatch`), drop or rename the `hierarchy` projection, update `docs/KGX_EXPORT.md`, and rebuild/re-validate the review bundle so `supported-graph` stays green. Whether the reviewed release keeps its current `subclass_of` edges or is re-cut is a release decision.

Related: #245, #390, kg-microbe reader change (mediadive parent-edge emission).
title: KGX exporter and 2026-09-21 review bundle still project skos:broadMatch as biolink:subclass_of (#245 ruling)
