3. **Rename in the other direction** — conform filenames to the existing subjects,
   preserving acronym case, and resolve #236 as option 1 or 2.

My recommendation is 1 for #298 (it is the only option that publishes nothing new)
and then 3 as its own PR once #236 is decided, since that is the direction that
preserves both identifier stability and readable acronyms.

Related: #236, #293.
title: 62 published MIM CURIEs were silently case-mangled with no alias trail

body:
`tests/test_check_chebi_currency.py::test_kgmicrobe_default_is_a_sibling_not_a_hardcoded_home`
fails on this machine, on `main`, unrelated to any working change (confirmed by
stashing).

```
assert "/Users/" not in str(mod.default_kgm_chebi())
E  AssertionError: assert '/Users/' not in
   '/Users/marcin/Documents/VIMSS/ontology/KG-Hub/KG-Microbe/kg-microbe/data/raw/chebi.owl.gz'
```

The intent is right — the default once named one developer's home directory,
making the currency check a permanent silent no-op for everyone else — but the
assertion tests the wrong thing. It rejects the substring `/Users/` anywhere in
the resolved path, and `default_kgm_chebi()` now correctly resolves a *sibling*
of the repo. On any macOS checkout under `/Users/<name>/...` the correct answer
contains `/Users/` and the test fails.

So it passes only where the repo is not under `/Users` — CI on Linux — and fails
for every macOS developer, which is the population the check exists to protect.

The property actually wanted is that the default is *derived from the repo
location* rather than hardcoded. Something like asserting the path is relative to
the repo root:

```python
assert mod.default_kgm_chebi().is_relative_to(REPO_ROOT.parent)
```

or that it does not contain a username that isn't in the repo path already.

Low priority — it is a test-only defect and the underlying fix it guards is
correct — but it means the local suite is never green on macOS, which trains
people to ignore a red result.
title: test_kgmicrobe_default_is_a_sibling fails whenever the repo lives under /Users

body:
The Edison sweep surfaced the same CAS (13408-09-8) on records that turn out to
be four spellings of one substance:

| identifier | preferred_term | status | ontology_id |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cas:13408-09-8` | `Na2glycerophosphate•5H2O` | MAPPED | CHEBI:15978 |
| `UNMAPPED_0101` | `Na2Glycerophosphate•5H2O` | UNMAPPED | — |
| `UNMAPPED_0081` | `Na2Glycerophosphate.5H2O` | UNMAPPED | — |
| `UNMAPPED_0465` | `Na2 beta-glycerol PO4 x 5 H2O` | UNMAPPED | — |

The mapped record and `UNMAPPED_0101` differ **by the case of a single letter**
(`glycerophosphate` vs `Glycerophosphate`). `UNMAPPED_0081` differs from
`UNMAPPED_0101` only in `.` vs `•`.

The mapped record was grounded during this sweep, per MAPPING_SEMANTICS Section 3
— `cas:` identifier plus `skos:narrowMatch` to CHEBI:15978 plus the Rule B1
registry row. The three unmapped siblings did not move, so the same substance is
now both mapped and unmapped depending on which spelling a medium happens to use.

Also worth noting: `Beta-Glycerophosphate disodium salt hydrate` is separately
mapped as `cas:154804-51-0` -> CHEBI:17270, so there may be a fifth member with
an unspecified hydration state.

No gate catches this. `qc-duplicate-ids` compares identifiers, and these have
four distinct ones; `reconcile_sssom.py` sees no drift because unmapped records
are not expected to publish rows.

Two things to decide, and I don't think they should be decided together:

1. **Are these duplicates?** Almost certainly yes for the three `5H2O` spellings.
   `Na2 beta-glycerol PO4 x 5 H2O` reads the same but is a looser paraphrase, so
   it deserves a separate look.
2. **Should they be merged onto `cas:13408-09-8`, or should the mapped record be
   reconsidered?** The reports hedge on the CAS itself: 13408-09-8 is linked to
   β-glycerophosphate but the retrieved sources "do not explicitly confirm that
   this CAS is the exact disodium pentahydrate form rather than a less-specific
   parent/supplier entry", and a second report says the evidence "does not fully
   establish that CAS 13408-09-8 always denotes a rigorously fixed 5-hydrate
   material". Merging three records onto that identifier propagates a hedge to
   four records instead of one.

Nothing applied. CAS enrichment on the two candidates was deliberately withheld
pending this, and the refusals are recorded in
`scripts/apply_edison_cas_enrichment.py`.

The case-only difference is the same drift as #293 and #236, appearing here as
duplicate records rather than as subject/file mismatch.
title: Four records for disodium β-glycerophosphate pentahydrate; one mapped, three not

body:
167 records now carry a `curation_history` entry citing
`research/ingredients/<slug>-edison-literature.md`. `.gitignore` line 60 ignores
`research/` wholesale, and NEXT_TASKS.md documents that as deliberate.

The consequence: a curator on a fresh clone cannot open any report a curation
event cites. Before this sweep it did not matter, because nothing in the curated
collections referenced those paths — all 160 such citations were introduced by
this work.

Mitigated for now (PR on `curation/edison-unmapped-sweep`): each note quotes the
report's bolded verdict and lists the CURIEs it discusses inline, and labels the
path a local artifact rather than presenting it as a repo file. So the note
stands on its own; what is lost is the evidence *behind* the verdict — the
citations, the retrieved passages, the candidate table with its reasons.

That loss is not hypothetical. Five CAS numbers were rejected during this sweep
purely on wording found in candidate tables ("Do not add CAS 9014-63-5...", "Do
not assign CAS 9004-34-6 without supplier documentation"). Anyone re-deriving
those decisions from the repo alone cannot see what they rest on.

Options:

1. **Commit the reports.** ~304 files, roughly 6 MB of markdown. Auditable
   forever, and diffable when a record is re-researched. Cost is repo weight and
   a large one-time diff.
2. **Commit only the reports a curation event cites** (167 now). Keeps the
   ignore rule for exploratory runs while making cited evidence real.
3. **Extract a short evidence block per record into the YAML** — verdict,
   candidate table, citation keys — and keep all markdown ignored. Heaviest to
   build, but puts the evidence where the decision is.
4. **Leave as-is** and treat the inline quote as sufficient.

Option 2 looks like the best ratio to me: it makes exactly the cited files
auditable, which is the actual defect, and leaves the 137 uncited reports out.

Related: #236 (subject/file identity), #293 (subject/file case drift).
title: Edison identity reports are gitignored, so cited provenance is unauditable

body:
The Edison literature sweep surfaced two records whose reports identify a
confident ontology term while explicitly refusing to assert an identity mapping:

| record | term | report's words |
|---|---|---|
| `Calf brains` | `UBERON:0000955` *brain* | "high-confidence anatomical-source annotation" but "do **not** assert `skos:exactMatch` or `skos:closeMatch`" |
| `Cow manure` | `ENVO:00003031` *animal manure* | recommends retaining UNMAPPED |

Both terms resolve correctly against the local builds, and both prefixes are
already in `promote_resolved_unmapped.py`'s `ONTOLOGY_DB`.

The reports forbid `exactMatch` and `closeMatch` — the two predicates that
license node substitution. They do not mention `skos:narrowMatch`, which is
exactly the predicate that says the subject is *narrower than* the object
without claiming they are interchangeable, and which MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md
Section 3 already uses for hydrates (`NaH2PO4*H2O` narrowMatch the anhydrous
`CHEBI:37585`).

So the question is a policy one, not a lookup one: **is Section 3's
identifier + narrowMatch + Rule B1 registry row pattern meant only for
hydrate/salt variants of a parent compound, or does it also cover
source-qualified materials** — calf brains as a narrower thing than brain, cow
manure than animal manure, larchwood xylan than xylan?

Arguments each way:

- **For extending it.** These records would gain a real, correct, non-substituting
  edge into UBERON/ENVO, which is more than the current UNMAPPED conveys. The
  narrowMatch semantics are literally true.
- **Against.** "Calf brains" as a medium ingredient is a *preparation*, and
  narrowMatch on a preparation-to-anatomy axis is a different relation from
  narrowMatch on a hydrate-to-anhydrous axis. Conflating them makes the
  predicate mean two things, and kg-microbe consumers cannot tell which.
  UBERON:0000955 as an *anatomical source* — which is what the report actually
  recommends — is arguably a schema slot, not an SSSOM row.

Nothing was applied; the records stay UNMAPPED and the CURIEs are recorded in
their curation history. Raising this because the same question governs a
recurring class of records (extracts, tissue preparations, source-qualified
polymers), and deciding it once is better than deciding it per record.

Blocked on a curator's call; see also #236 on subject/file identity.
title: Does the Section 3 narrowMatch pattern extend to source-material records?

body:
Found when the curie-normalizer test started failing with `UNKNOWN_SUBJECT` after a bulk promotion.

## The mismatch

`export_individual_records.FilenameIndex` **never renames** an existing per-record file — that is deliberate, so paths stay stable. But `promote_resolved_unmapped.py` **recomputes** the SSSOM subject from `preferred_term` via `sanitize_filename` on every promotion.

So the two disagree whenever the on-disk stem predates the current naming rule:

```
file on disk:     data/ingredients/mapped/Na2glycerophosphate5h2o.yaml
SSSOM subject:    MIM:Na2glycerophosphate5H2O          <- recomputed, differs by case
```

`CurieNormalizer.resolve()` checks the subject against the known record set, so a recomputed subject that no file matches returns `UNKNOWN_SUBJECT` — and `test_curie_normalizer.py::test_equivalent_term_picks_highest_ranked_exact_match` fails on it.

## Scale

This session's stock-solution minting took the count of SSSOM subjects with no matching file stem from **9 → 75**. All 66 new ones were case-only differences of exactly this kind. I realigned them to their actual stems in the #114 curation branch, returning the count to the 9 pre-existing cases documented in PR #285 — but **the tool will reintroduce them on the next bulk promotion**.

## The fix already exists elsewhere

`promote_microbedecoder_reviewed.py` gets this right, and says so in its docstring:

> Synthesises an SSSOM row (subject `MIM:<existing file stem>` **from the manifest so the export never renames it** …)

`promote_resolved_unmapped.py` should resolve the subject the same way — look up the record's existing file stem, and only fall back to `sanitize_filename` when the record has no file yet (a genuinely new promotion).

## Why it matters beyond the test

`MIM:` expands to `data/ingredients/mapped/` in the SSSOM `curie_map`, so a subject that resolves to no file is a broken address for any consumer that follows it. #236 is the open question about whether `MIM:` slugs *should* be paths at all — but regardless of how that is settled, the tool should not be **generating** new mismatches, and `check_sssom_subject_files.py` (added in #285) now makes the count visible either way.

Related: #236, #285, #114.
title: promote_resolved_unmapped recomputes the SSSOM subject instead of using the existing file stem (#236 at scale)

body:
Hit twice now, in #114 and again applying Edison research.

`scripts/merge_unmapped_into_mapped.py` folds an UNMAPPED record into a MAPPED one as a `RAW_TEXT` synonym. It refuses when the source carries anything a synonym cannot represent:

```
'Na2Glycerophosphate.5H2O': source carries data a synonym cannot represent
  (ingredient_type, occurrence_statistics(1/1), synonyms(1 beyond the self-reference));
  merge it by hand or extend this script
```

The refusal is **right in principle** — silently dropping occurrences or an `ingredient_type` would lose real data, and it is what caught the `MES buffer` (`STOCK_SOLUTION`) vs `MES` (`SINGLE_INGREDIENT`) distinction in #114, which was a genuine semantic difference worth stopping for.

But it now blocks the ordinary case too. Two spelling variants of one substance —

```
Na2glycerophosphate•5H2O    (grounded to cas:13408-09-8 from Edison research)
Na2Glycerophosphate.5H2O    punctuation variant
Na2Glycerophosphate•5H2O    capitalisation variant
```

— cannot be merged, because each carries `occurrence_statistics(1/1)` and an `ingredient_type`. Those are exactly the fields `merge_mapped_records.py` already knows how to transfer: it **sums** occurrences and unions role facets, and #196 taught it to carry `source_occurrences` per source as well.

So the capability exists; it just lives in the wrong script. The asymmetry is:

| | occurrences | ingredient_type | source_id |
|---|---|---|---|
| `merge_mapped_records` | summed | — | carried to history |
| `merge_unmapped_into_mapped` | **refuses** | **refuses** | carried to history |

Suggested: reuse `merge_mapped_records.transfer_occurrences()` (extracted in #196 precisely so it could be shared) and allow the merge when the source and target `ingredient_type` **agree** — keeping the refusal only when they differ, which is the `MES buffer` case the check exists for.

Until then, variant-label cleanup on unmapped records needs a hand-edit, which is what #267 was filed about.

Related: #114, #196, #267, #218.
title: merge_unmapped_into_mapped refuses any source carrying occurrences or ingredient_type — the common case

body:
Found finishing #114's non-chemical disposition.

The UNMAPPED residual contained **96 records typed `STOCK_SOLUTION`** — named multi-component lab preparations (`Wolfe's vitamin mix`, `Wolfe's mineral mix`, trace-metal and amino-acid mixes). None has an ontology term and none could: a preparation is not a substance. Searching CHEBI, NCIT, MeSH, FOODON and ENVO by label and synonym returned a hit for **2 of 96, and both were false** — `PBS` → `NCIT:C122728` *'TSPO wt Allele'* (a gene allele) and `Trace minerals` → an M-prefixed MeSH concept id rather than a D/C descriptor.

I minted `kgmicrobe.ingredient:` identifiers for the **61 that occur in at least one medium**, following the convention 12 existing mapped `STOCK_SOLUTION` records already use (`FALLBACK_REGISTRY`, no parent — a multi-component mix does not narrow to a single compound).

**I deliberately left the other 35**, which have `total_occurrences: 0`. The reasoning was that an identifier for a preparation nothing uses is not worth the published row.

That is a judgement, not an obvious call, and it leaves the population half-done. Worth deciding explicitly:

- **Finish them** — consistency, and a zero-occurrence record today may be used tomorrow; the marginal cost is 35 rows.
- **Leave them** — the SSSOM stays proportional to what is actually used, and zero-occurrence records are the ones most likely to be import noise or duplicates that should be merged rather than minted.
- **Triage first** — check whether any of the 35 are spelling variants of the 61 already minted (e.g. `Mc_general_salts` vs `Mc_general_salts_SO4free` are genuinely different, but others may not be). That would make some of them merges rather than mints, which is a better outcome than either option above.

I would lean on the third: the zero-occurrence tail is exactly where duplicate/variant labels accumulate, and minting them would fix that population in place rather than deduplicating it.

Related: #114, #218 (duplicate identifiers), #226.
title: 35 zero-occurrence STOCK_SOLUTION records left unminted — decide whether the population should be finished

body:
Found doing #114's PubChem `cas_rn` audit.

Six records carried an **EC / EINECS** registry number in `chemical_properties.cas_rn`. The two formats are distinguishable by shape alone:

```
CAS-RN   NNNNNNN-NN-N   (2–7 digits, 2 digits, 1 check digit)   110-16-7
EC/EINECS  NNN-NNN-N    (3-3-1)                                 203-742-5
```

Five of the six came from `data_source: PubChem API` — the same `fetch_cas_rn_from_pubchem` path that produced Beef extract's `103-47-9` (=CHES) in #114. PubChem records carry both identifiers, and the lookup evidently grabbed the wrong one for these.

They are corrected in the branch for #114 (`Arabinose`, `BaCl2`, `Fucose`, `Galactose`, `Maleic acid`, `Na2EDTA·2H2O`), but **nothing prevents the next import from reintroducing them**:

- the LinkML schema types `cas_rn` as a plain string with no pattern;
- `validate-strict` therefore accepts any string;
- and the id↔label gate does not look at `chemical_properties` at all.

Suggested, cheapest first:

1. **Add a `pattern` to `cas_rn` in the schema** — `^\d{2,7}-\d{2}-\d$`. That alone would have rejected all six at write time, and `save_yaml(validate=True)` already runs on every writer, so it costs nothing to enforce.
2. Optionally validate the **check digit** (the last digit is a mod-10 weighted sum of the others), which catches transpositions that pass the shape test.
3. Consider an `ec_number` field, since the EC numbers were *correct information in the wrong field* — worth keeping rather than discarding.

### Worth knowing before writing the check

The same audit found **146 disagreements** between a record's `cas_rn` and its CHEBI term's CAS dbxref, and only these 6 are defects. The other 140 are legitimate:

- **71 salt/hydrate forms** — the CAS correctly describes the record while the term is the anhydrous or free parent (the #218/#242 shape);
- **57** differ only by stereochemistry (record `Arginine` carrying L-arginine's CAS on the stereo-unspecified parent);
- **12** are spelling variants of the same substance.

So a check that simply flags "cas_rn disagrees with the term's dbxref" would be **~96% false positives**. Format validation is the part that pays; semantic cross-checking is not worth gating on.

Related: #114, #218, #242.
title: Validate cas_rn format on write — EC/EINECS numbers are being stored as CAS-RNs

body:
Found while fixing #273 (PR #278).

#278 teaches `reground_mapped_record.py` the Section 3 move — a record takes a `cas:`/`kgmicrobe.compound:` identifier plus a `narrowMatch` to the nearest ontology parent, with the Rule B1 registry sibling row. But that script only operates on records that are already **MAPPED**.

The complementary path is still closed. `promote_resolved_unmapped.py`'s own docstring says:

> exact/close need no Rule B1 registry sibling; narrow/broad are refused here

and its `--quality` choices are `EXACT_MATCH | SYNONYM_MATCH | CLOSE_MATCH`. So an **UNMAPPED** record whose correct answer is "no ontology term denotes this; mint an identifier and narrowMatch the parent" has nowhere to go in one step.

That is not hypothetical — it is the shape of the #213 salt/hydrate bucket, all of which is UNMAPPED today:

| record | occurrences | parent CHEBI has | salt CHEBI lacks |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Esculin Ferric Citrate` | 164 | — | the ferric citrate complex |
| `Potassium 5-ketogluconate` | 47 | `CHEBI:58143` 5-dehydro-D-gluconate | the potassium salt |
| `Potassium 5-dehydro-D-gluconate` | 38 | `CHEBI:58143` | the potassium salt |
| `Potassium 2-dehydro-D-gluconate` | 8 | `CHEBI:16808` 2-dehydro-D-gluconate | the potassium salt |
| `Maltose Hydrate` | 8 | `CHEBI:17306` maltose | the hydrate |

Grounding any of these `exactMatch` to the parent asserts the salt **is** its parent — the conflation #242 and #263 removed. So the honest options today are a two-step (promote to the parent as CLOSE, then re-ground onto a mint with #278) which briefly publishes a mapping the repo considers wrong, or a hand-edit, which is what #267 was filed about.

Suggested: extend `promote_resolved_unmapped.py` with the same `--to <mint> --parent <ontology term>` pair #278 adds, reusing its Rule B1 row emission so there is one implementation of the Section 3 shape rather than two.

Related: #273, #278, #213, #267, #239.
title: promote_resolved_unmapped.py refuses narrow/broad, so an UNMAPPED record cannot go straight to a registry mint

body:
Found when CI failed on PR #275 (#213).

`scripts/promote_resolved_unmapped.py` advertises itself as doing the migration "end to end", and it does regenerate per-record files and the `docs/data/` CSVs — its output even says *"Regenerating per-record files + docs ..."* and it self-runs `reconcile_sssom` and `validate_sssom_invariants`. But it never invokes the browser export:

```
$ grep -c "export-browser\|browser_export" scripts/promote_resolved_unmapped.py
0
```

So after 11 promotions, `docs/data/ingredients.json` was still the pre-promotion file, and `check_flat_export_coverage.py` failed the `qc` job:

```
ERROR: docs/data/ does not match what its producer generates — it is stale:
  ingredients.json           regenerate with `just export-browser`  (browser_export.py, reads data/ingredients/)
```

The check did its job — this is not a silent-corruption report — but the failure mode is unpleasant: the tool prints `Done.` and a green-looking self-verification, so a curator reasonably believes the migration is complete, and only discovers otherwise after pushing. Every promotion needs a manual `just export-browser` that nothing tells you about.

Two ways to close it:
1. Chain `browser_export.py` in the same regeneration step as the CSVs (preferred — it is the same class of artifact and reads the same tree).
2. If chaining is unwanted (it is the slowest export), make the tool's closing "Now run:" line name `just export-browser` explicitly. It currently names only `just validate-products` and `just validate-strict`.

Worth checking the sibling writers for the same omission — `merge_unmapped_into_mapped.py` and `merge_mapped_records.py` both end with a "next:" line that *does* name `just export-browser`, so this looks like an inconsistency in `promote_resolved_unmapped.py` specifically rather than a repo-wide convention.

Related: #213, #275.
title: promote_resolved_unmapped.py regenerates docs/data CSVs but not the browser export, leaving ingredients.json stale

body:
Found while working #208.

`scripts/reground_mapped_record.py` validates the destination against the local ontology adapter and refuses anything it cannot resolve:

```
$ reground_mapped_record.py --identifier CHEBI:33697 \
    --to kgmicrobe.compound:ribonucleic_acid_from_torula_yeast_type_vi ...
kgmicrobe.compound:ribonucleic_acid_from_torula_yeast_type_vi has no rdfs:label in chebi.db — absent or wrong id
```

That check is right for ontology destinations, but it makes the tool unable to express the **MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md Section 3** move — "no exact ontology term exists, so take a registry identifier (`cas:` / `kgmicrobe.compound:`) plus a `narrowMatch` to the nearest parent". 248 records already hold `cas:` identifiers in exactly that shape, so the destination class is well established; there is just no tool that can *move an existing mapped record into it*.

## What it blocks

The #208 RNA split. `Ribonucleic acid from torula yeast type VI` — a specific commercial preparation — currently holds `CHEBI:33697 "ribonucleic acid"` at **EXACT_MATCH**. That over-claims (Type VI torula-yeast RNA is not the generic class) and it **occupies the CURIE that the label which genuinely IS generic RNA should hold**: residual `UNMAPPED_0842 "RNA"` (microbedecoder, occurrence 1).

The correct end state is:
- Torula product → `kgmicrobe.compound:ribonucleic_acid_from_torula_yeast_type_vi`, `narrowMatch` → CHEBI:33697, plus the Rule B1 registry row;
- `RNA` → promoted onto the freed CHEBI:33697.

The second step is exactly what `reground_mapped_record.py`'s docstring advertises ("the freed CURIE becomes available, which is usually the point"), but the first step cannot be run.

**Not worked around.** Hand-editing is what #267 was filed about — it is how PR #266 minted two duplicate identifiers. #208's actual instruction is "generic RNA must **not** merge onto the specific Torula-yeast product record", and that is satisfied: no merge was performed. The record simply stays unmapped until the tool can do the split safely.

Suggested: allow a registry-prefixed `--to` (validated against the known registry prefixes rather than an ontology adapter), require `--parent`/`--quality NARROW_MATCH` when the destination is a mint, and emit the Rule B1 registry row — the logic `anchor_cas_hydrate_records.py` already has for records that arrive with a `cas:` identifier.

Related: #208, #267, #239, #245.
title: reground_mapped_record.py cannot move a record onto a registry mint, which blocks the #208 RNA split

body:
Found while auditing the microbedecoder thread for #213.

The local branch `feat/microbedecoder-residual-grounding` (worktree at `MediaIngredientMech-residual`) is **PR #201, which is closed**, and it now sits **26 commits behind `main`**. Most of its content has landed by other routes — the 386-promotion, the review manifest, and both residual TSVs (`microbedecoder_residual_grounded.tsv`, `microbedecoder_residual_locant_fixed.tsv`) are all on `main`, and #214 explicitly applied "the 9 residual merges and 55 NEEDS_EXPERT flags PR #201 never landed".

```
scripts/promote_microbedecoder_residual.py   (169 lines) — absent from main
```

That is the promotion path for the *residual* groundings, i.e. the tooling most directly relevant to working down #213's ~583 remaining labels. Its sibling `scripts/promote_microbedecoder_reviewed.py` did land and has since been substantially reworked (#203 / PR #269 — specificity gate, verdict writeback, real timestamps), so the residual script as written on that branch is **not** a drop-in: it predates those fixes and would reintroduce the tautological-approval shape if run as-is.

2. Rebase its intent onto current `main`, reusing `promote_microbedecoder_reviewed.py`'s specificity gate rather than its own approval check.
3. Then delete the branch and its worktree.

Flagging rather than acting: the branch and worktree belong to a separate work thread and I did not create them, so removing them is the owner's call.

body:
Found reviewing PR #269 (#203). This is the "wider exposure" half of #203, which #269 deliberately does not close.

#269 adds a specificity gate to the promotion path, but it only evaluates rows still at `PENDING`. Manifest PENDING is now **0** — so the gate will never see the rows that were promoted under the old tautological check. Running the new rule over the full 403-row manifest flags **12**, of which **11 are already `APPROVED` and published**:

| subject | object | direct subclasses |
|---|---|---|
| Bile Acid | CHEBI:3098 | 415 |
| Lactone | CHEBI:25000 | 164 |
| Cephalosporin | CHEBI:23066 | 111 |
| Hopanoid | CHEBI:51963 | 93 |
| Purines | CHEBI:26401 | 92 |
| Macrolide Antibiotic | CHEBI:25105 | 68 |
| Amino Acid | CHEBI:33709 | 57 |
| Beta-D-galactoside | CHEBI:28034 | 57 |
| Carotenoid | CHEBI:23044 | 17 (+7 more specific labels) |
| Sterol | CHEBI:15889 | 17 (+6) |
| Polymyxin | CHEBI:59062 | 11 (+16) |

(The 12th, `Sulfonamide` → CHEBI:35358, is already `HELD_WRONG_SENSE` with its SSSOM row withdrawn — that one was caught by hand in #195.)

**This is not automatically a defect list.** As #203 says, most of these MIM subjects are themselves kg-microbe *traits*, so a class↔class `exactMatch` is often the right call — `Macrolide Antibiotic` → *macrolide antibiotic* looks entirely correct. The problem is that **nothing distinguished the cases**: they were approved by a check that could not say no, and `skos:exactMatch` licenses node substitution for every one of them.

Worth a curator pass to convert each into a decision:
- **Correct as-is** (trait ↔ class) → record the verdict so it is a decision, not an accident.
- **Wrong sense** → the `Sulfonamide` treatment: hold and withdraw the SSSOM row.
- **Too broad but not wrong** → consider `skos:broadMatch`, which does not license substitution.

Two specific oddities from #203 that belong in the same pass, where one drug got opposite treatment in two records: `Netilmycin` → CHEBI:7528 promoted while `Netilmicin` → CHEBI:748901 was demoted; same shape for `Cyclodextrin` / `Gamma-cyclodextrin` and `Polymyxin` / `Polymyxin B`.

Reproduce the list with:
```
python scripts/promote_microbedecoder_reviewed.py   # gate logic; see _specificity_alarm
```

Related: #203, #269, #195, #213.
title: 11 already-published class-level skos:exactMatch rows predate the specificity gate and were never reviewed

body:
Found reviewing PR #266 (#263).

All four records re-grounded in #263 had `molecular_formula` / `inchi` / `smiles` (and one `pubchem_cid`) written onto them by `AUTO_BACKFILL_CHEBI_CHEMISTRY`, copied from the CHEBI term the record pointed at. When that term is wrong, the backfill silently manufactures wrong chemistry that looks curated.

`Casamino acids` shows the worst of it. It is a casein hydrolysate — an undefined mixture — and was correctly typed `UNDEFINED_MIXTURE` by a rule matching the name. Then:

1. The record was grounded to CHEBI:78020 *heptacosanoate* (wrong).
2. `AUTO_BACKFILL_CHEBI_CHEMISTRY` wrote heptacosanoate's `C27H53O2` / InChI / SMILES onto it.
3. `auto_classify_ingredient_type` saw populated chemical structure and **re-typed the record `SINGLE_INGREDIENT`**, overwriting the correct classification — its own history says *"chemical structure populated (molecular_formula)"*.

So one wrong id cascaded into wrong structure and a wrong record type, each step looking like a legitimate automated curation entry in `curation_history`. Nothing flagged the contradiction between `ingredient_type=UNDEFINED_MIXTURE` and "has a single exact molecular formula".

Worth considering:
- **Record provenance on backfilled fields.** If `molecular_formula` carried "derived from `<curie>`", re-grounding could invalidate it automatically instead of relying on a curator to notice. (#138 is the same shape: stale derived columns outranking corrections.)
- **Do not let a derived field drive a classification.** `auto_classify_ingredient_type` promoting `UNDEFINED_MIXTURE` → `SINGLE_INGREDIENT` on the strength of a backfilled formula lets a grounding error rewrite the record's identity.
- **Flag the contradiction.** A name matching a known complex/mixture pattern *and* a single exact formula is a signal worth surfacing.

PR #266 drops the poisoned fields on the four affected records rather than recomputing them, but does not address the mechanism — any future wrong grounding will do this again.

Related: #263, #266, #138, #237.
title: AUTO_BACKFILL_CHEBI_CHEMISTRY propagates a wrong grounding into structure fields and can flip ingredient_type

body:
Found reviewing PR #266 (#263).

The repo has `scripts/reground_mapped_record.py`, whose own help says it *"moves a mapped record to a different term"* and that it **refuses when the destination CURIE is already held**. That refusal is precisely the safety check the #263 work needed.

I re-grounded four records by hand-editing the YAML instead, and duly minted two identifiers that were already held (`CHEBI:66870`, `FOODON:03315719`). `just qc-duplicate-ids` caught it — so the net is fine — but the failure came *after* the edit, the collection re-sync, the product re-export, and the SSSOM reconcile had all been run on bad state, and unwinding that cost more than the edit itself.

Nothing points a curator at the tool at the moment they need it:

- `MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md` describes the mapping *semantics* but names no script for changing an existing grounding.
- The `map-media-ingredients` and `merge-ingredients` skills cover mapping new records and merging, not re-grounding a wrong one.
- `just --list` has no re-ground recipe, so the script is invisible unless you already know it exists (`merge_mapped_records.py` at least gets referenced from the duplicate-gate failure text).

Suggestions, cheapest first:
1. Add the re-ground script to the `qc-duplicate-ids` failure message, next to the existing `--write-baseline` hint — that is exactly where someone who just made this mistake is looking.
2. Add a `just reground` recipe so it appears in `just --list`.
3. Cross-reference it from `MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md` and the `map-media-ingredients` skill.

Related: #263, #266, #224, #218.

body:
Surfaced by pointing the plausibility gate at the curator label (#261). These are **not** naming-convention noise — each is a record asserting a CHEBI id for an unrelated molecule, verified against live `sqlite:obo:chebi`.

| record | asserted id | what the id actually is | what the ingredient is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data/ingredients/mapped/Casamino_Acids.yaml` | CHEBI:78020 | **heptacosanoate** (C27 fatty acid anion) | acid-hydrolysed casein digest — a peptide/amino-acid mixture |
| `data/ingredients/mapped/Na2s2o4.yaml` | CHEBI:61278 | **scutellarin** (a flavone glucuronide) | sodium dithionite, Na₂S₂O₄ — a reducing agent |
| `data/ingredients/mapped/Sodium_Succinate_Dibasic.yaml` | CHEBI:150903 | a trisaccharide-type glycoside (`(2S,3S,4R,5S,6S)-2-[…]oxane-3,4,5-triol`) | disodium succinate |
| `data/ingredients/mapped/Tomatidine_Hydrochloride.yaml` | CHEBI:93130 | `1-methyl-3-[…]-1,3,5-triazinane-2,4,6-trione` | tomatidine HCl, a steroidal alkaloid |

`Casamino acids → heptacosanoate` and `Na2S2O4 → scutellarin` are the starkest: nothing about either pair is chemically close, and both are common media ingredients, so the wrong id propagates into every export and downstream KG edge.

## Also worth a look (different failure class)

`Fructooligosaccharides (FOS)` → CHEBI:28645 **beta-D-fructofuranose**. Not an unrelated molecule, but a **granularity** error: a single monosaccharide standing in for an oligosaccharide mixture. Closer to the #237/#216 `DEFINED_MEDIUM` discussion than to the four above.

## Scope note

The gate reported 61 `IMPLAUSIBLE_LABEL` in total. **Most of the rest look like correct groundings** the lexical heuristic cannot see — `2-Furfuraldehyde` → *furfural*, `Irgasan` → *triclosan*, `Sodium 2-mercaptoethanesulfonate` → *Mesna*, `Soy peptone` → *vegetable protein, hydrolyzed* (the very example the validator's own comment cites as a legitimate no-shared-word case). So the 61 is a **triage queue, not a defect count**, which is exactly why #261 holds this surface at `severity: warn` rather than flipping it to `error`.

These four, though, are confirmed and should be re-grounded.

Related: #261, #114.
title: Four verified wrong CHEBI groundings the no-op plausibility gate was hiding

body:
Found while syncing the #242 hydration verdicts from the hub. Measured, not inferred.

## The gate does nothing today

`conf/id_label_targets.yaml`'s `mapped_csv` target waives `ontology_id` and upgrades the waiver with `label_waiver_mode: plausible`, gating the pair `[ontology_id, ontology_label]`. Running the plausibility classifier over all 1902 CHEBI rows of `docs/data/mapped_ingredients.csv`:

| gated column | result |
|---|---|
| `ontology_label` (**what is gated today**) | **OK_ID_ONLY 1902** — nothing else, at all |
| `preferred_term` (the curator label) | OK_ID_ONLY 1806 · IMPLAUSIBLE_LABEL 50 · **HYDRATE_ON_ANHYDROUS_TERM 39** · LABEL_SUBSCRIPTS_LOST 3 · **HYDRATION_STATE_MISMATCH 2** · **ANHYDROUS_ON_HYDRATE_TERM 2** |

Every gated row short-circuits at `_plausibility_verdict`'s first line — `normalize(label) in accepted` — because the label being checked **is** the term's own canonical label. The formula comparison never runs. `IMPLAUSIBLE_LABEL: 0` was never evidence of clean data; it is the gate not doing anything.

## The config's stated premise is stale

The `PRODUCT DECISION (item 3c)` comment says `ontology_label` surfaces the CURATOR-INTENDED label and names `CHEBI:86158 "CaCl2 x 2 H2O"` as its example. The export no longer does that:

```
identifier=CHEBI:86158  preferred_term='CaCl2 x 2 H2O'  ontology_label='calcium chloride dihydrate'
identifier=CHEBI:86158  preferred_term='CaCl22H2O'      ontology_label='calcium chloride dihydrate'
```

The curator label moved to `preferred_term`; `ontology_label` is now the OBO canonical form (792 of 1902 CHEBI rows differ between the two columns). So the gate built to police curator labels is pointed at a column that by construction can never fail it.

## Consequence for #242

The three hydration verdicts are correct and now vendored in, but **cannot fire in MIM** until the gate reads the curator column. The 39 + 2 + 2 findings above are real records — e.g. `CaCl2 x 7 H2O` on CHEBI:3312 *calcium dichloride* (anhydrous), `CoCl2 x 2/4/6 H2O` all on CHEBI:35696 *cobalt dichloride* — the same population `just report-hydrate-grounding` (#240) measures independently.

## Why this is not a one-line fix

`plausibility_severity: error`, so `IMPLAUSIBLE_LABEL` is an **error** verdict. Simply adding `[ontology_id, preferred_term]` to `pairs` turns 50 rows into enforce failures and breaks `just validate-products` immediately. Sequencing needs to be deliberate:

1. Add the pair with `plausibility_severity: warn` (or per-target severity) so the population is visible without breaking CI.
2. Triage the 50 IMPLAUSIBLE_LABEL — some will be genuine mis-groundings, some need `exceptions` rows with a documented reason.
3. Work the 43 hydration findings via MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md Section 3 (hydrate term, or `cas:` mint + narrowMatch).
4. Only then consider restoring error severity.
5. Fix the stale `PRODUCT DECISION` comment either way — it documents behaviour the export stopped having.

Related: #242, #240, #260, #218.
title: The plausibility gate is a no-op: it checks ontology_label (the OBO canonical label), not the curator label

body:
Found while reviewing PR #255 (closes #254).

\`water_multiplicity\` returns any integer it finds. The corpus contains a corrupt synonym \`MgCl2  x 76 H2O\` (almost certainly \`7\`/\`6\` concatenated), and it parses to \`76\`:

\`\`\`
>>> water_multiplicity('MgCl2 x 76 H2O')  -> '76'
\`\`\`

The #254 report then presents \`76\` as a legitimate distinct hydration state (see \`reports/hydrate_synonyms.tsv\`, CHEBI:6636), mixing a data-entry corruption in with real hydration-state collapses. No mineral hydrate reaches the 70s.

Options: cap plausible multiplicities (e.g. treat > ~20 as unspecified/malformed and route to a separate "malformed hydrate notation" bucket rather than counting it as a state), so the collapse signal stays clean. Low priority — it surfaces a real data issue, just under the wrong heading.
