body:
Found while reviewing PR #255 (closes #254).

\`_DIGIT_WATER\` in \`src/mediaingredientmech/curation/hydrate_guard.py\` accepts these separators before a digit multiplier:

\`\`\`
[x × · • ・ ⋅ ∙ . whitespace]
\`\`\`

but **not** the ASCII hyphen \`-\`. Hyphen-separated hydrate labels are present in the corpus:

\`\`\`
ZnSO4-7H2O
CuCl2-2H2O
Na2MoO4-2H2O
\`\`\`

All three parse to \`None\` ("unspecified") today:

\`\`\`
>>> water_multiplicity('ZnSO4-7H2O')  -> None
>>> water_multiplicity('CuCl2-2H2O')  -> None
\`\`\`

Consequence: a \`ZnSO4-7H2O\` synonym sitting on a record labelled e.g. \`ZnSO4 x 6 H2O\` is a genuine hydration-state collapse that the #254 detector silently skips. The direction is safe (false-negative, never a false mismatch), but the miss is real because these strings actually occur.

Fix: add \`-\` (and consider the Unicode minus U+2212) to the separator class, with a pinned test case. Guard against false positives from names like \`omega-3\` — the regex already requires \`(\d+)\s*H2\s*O\` contiguous, so \`-3 fatty acid ... H2O\` will not match.
title: water_multiplicity misses hyphen-separated hydrates that exist in the data

body:
Split out of #251 / PR #253, where a first attempt at detecting this shipped 96 findings that were almost all false.

## The population

A record whose `preferred_term` is a hydrate can still carry synonyms naming a **different** hydration state:

```
CHEBI:32599  "MgSO4·7H2O"     synonym: MgSO4 x 6 H2O
CHEBI:75832  "FeSO4 x 5 H2O"  synonyms naming the 6- and 7-hydrate
CHEBI:35696  "CoCl2 x 2 H2O"  8 differing forms
```

That is the same MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md Section 3 collapse as #251's anhydrous case — different substances folded into one record — but it is **invisible to every current check**, including #253's new bucket. Those records land in `OK_HYDRATE_TERM`, i.e. reported clean, because their own label *is* a hydrate.

Roughly 30 records look affected on a crude scan, but see below before trusting that number.

## Why #253 did not ship the detection

It needs the water multiplicity, and parsing that reliably is harder than it looks:

- **Formula digits sit adjacent to the separator.** `AlCl3.6H2O` — a naive `\d+(?:\.\d+)?\s*H2O` captures `3.6`, reading the aluminium subscript as part of the multiplier.
- **`hexahydrate` and `6 H2O` are the same state.** Comparing raw tokens flagged them as different; the word forms must normalise to numbers (`hemi`→0.5 … `dodeca`→12).
- **Some labels are genuinely ambiguous.** `CaCl22H2O` is CaCl₂·2H₂O written without a separator, but nothing in the string says whether the trailing `2` is the subscript or the multiplier.
- **Unspecified hydrates must not read as monohydrate.** A bare `hydrate` or `x n H2O` says nothing; treating it as 1 invents mismatches against records that genuinely say 6.

A first version of the detector hit all four and reported **96 records**, of which the sample checked were overwhelmingly just respellings of the same state. Shipping that would have been the #237 classifier mistake again — laundering a guess into a machine-readable verdict.

## Suggested approach

Write the multiplicity parser as its own tested unit before wiring it into a report: normalise multiplier words to numbers, require a separator (or string start) before a digit multiplier, and return "unspecified" rather than a number when the label does not say. Pin `AlCl3.6H2O`, `CaCl22H2O`, `MgSO4 x n H2O`, `hexahydrate` vs `6 H2O`, and `Al2(SO4)3 x 18 H2O` as cases. Only then add the bucket.

Related: #251, #253, #218, #225.
title: Records carrying a synonym of a different hydration state are invisible

body:
Found reviewing #250.

`report_hydrate_grounding.py` scans `preferred_term` only. The hydrate notation this corpus uses most exotically lives in **synonyms**, where the report cannot see it:

| separator | occurrences in synonyms | in preferred_term |
|---|---|---|
| `・` U+30FB | 74 | 0 |
| `⋅` U+22C5 | 29 | 0 |
| `∙` U+2219 | 18 | 0 |
| `×` U+00D7 | 13 | 0 |

**18 mapped records carry a hydrate-notated synonym while their `preferred_term` is the anhydrous form**, for example:

```
CHEBI:3312   "CaCl2"       synonym: CaCl2 × 2 H2O
CHEBI:35696  "CoCl2"       synonym: CoCl2 × 6H2O
CHEBI:17561  "L-Cysteine"  synonym: Cysteine-HCl∙H2O
```

That is the #218 identity collapse **after** a merge: the hydrate was folded into the anhydrous record as a synonym rather than given its own identifier. MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md Section 3 says a hydration state is a distinct substance, so a hydrate label should not be a synonym of the anhydrous term — it should be its own record with a hydrate-specific term or its own `cas:` id.

## Why the report misses it

Both loops in `report_hydrate_grounding.py` key on `preferred_term`. Since #229 publishes synonyms, these labels *do* resolve from `docs/data/all_ingredients.csv` — to the anhydrous parent, which is exactly the wrong answer and is invisible to every current check:

- `qc-duplicate-ids` sees one identifier, one record — no duplicate.
- `qc-flat-coverage` sees the label published — coverage satisfied.
- `report-hydrate-grounding` never looks at synonyms.

## Suggested fix

Add a third bucket to the report: mapped records whose `preferred_term` is not a hydrate but which carry a hydrate-notated synonym. Then decide per record whether to split the synonym out into its own record (Section 3) or, where the synonym is merely a spelling of the same hydration state the record already represents, leave it.

Worth checking against the 15 merges in #226 and the 9 in #214 — some of these may be merges that should not have happened, in which case they need the same treatment `merge-ingredients`' Scenario 3 now describes.

Related: #250, #247, #218, #225, #229.
title: Hydrate notation hidden in synonyms is invisible to every hydrate check

body:
Found reviewing #248, which claimed two records were the only ones whose primary key resolves to nothing. It is off by six.

Six records carry a CHEBI identifier that **does not exist in ChEBI**, with `ontology_mapping: null`:

| record | identifier |
|---|---|
| `unmapped/Lysostaphin.yaml` | `CHEBI:753395` |
| `unmapped/Carbomycin.yaml` | `CHEBI:756054` |
| `unmapped/Netilmicin.yaml` | `CHEBI:748901` |
| `unmapped/Colistin_Sulfate.yaml` | `CHEBI:759883` |
| `unmapped/Polymyxin_B.yaml` | `CHEBI:759086` |
| `unmapped/Gentamicin.yaml` | `CHEBI:759884` |

All six are above the `CHEBI: 300000` ceiling in `conf/id_label_targets.yaml`, which is the "foreign identifier wearing an OBO prefix" signature #170 describes.

## How they got here

Created **2026-08-04** by `microbedecoder-import-review`. When the id came back `ID_OUT_OF_RANGE` the importer stripped `ontology_mapping` — correctly, since the term could not be verified — but **left the unverifiable CURIE as the record's `identifier`**. In MIM the identifier *is* the ontology CURIE, so the record now asserts an identity it cannot support.

This reproduced #170's defect one day before #248 tried to fix #170.

## Why they should be `UNMAPPED_NNNN`

The repo's own convention (`manage-identifiers` skill) is that an unmapped record carries an `UNMAPPED_NNNN` placeholder; the ontology CURIE is only the identifier once the mapping is real. These six are `mapping_status: UNMAPPED` with `ontology_mapping: null` — by that rule they should each hold a placeholder, with the claimed CHEBI id preserved in `notes`/`curation_history` so the eventual re-check can find it.

## Interaction with #207 and #210

Six of the antibiotics #207 tracks are blocked on a semsql build that would make these ids resolvable, and #210/#197 argue the 300000 ceiling is itself wrong. If the ceiling is the bug and these CURIEs are genuine recent ChEBI terms, the fix is to raise the ceiling rather than re-key the records. **That should be settled first** — re-keying six records and then discovering the ids were valid all along would be worse than leaving them.

So: decide #210 before acting here, and treat this issue as the record that the six exist and are currently unresolvable either way.

Related: #170, #207, #210, #197, #248.
title: Six UNMAPPED records carry a CHEBI identifier that does not exist

body:
Raised in review of #246.

#246 makes the automated curation path **refuse** to file a hydrate label onto a non-hydrate term. That is right — it stops #218/#225 recurring. But it creates a queue with no consumer.

Measured against the current curated set, roughly **60 currently-mapped hydrate records** sit on a term the guard now calls a non-hydrate. Going forward the automated path will refuse that whole class, and by this repo's own convention (MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md Section 3, applied in #244) the correct answer for most of them is:

> its own `cas:<hydrate CAS>` identifier, a `narrowMatch` to the parent, and the Rule B1 registry row

**No automated path can mint that.** `promote_resolved_unmapped.py` only takes CHEBI; `anchor_cas_hydrate_records.py` (#244) is plan-driven and assumes the record already has a `cas:` identifier. So a refused record is left `UNMAPPED`, appears in the batch report as skipped, and then nothing picks it up.

## What is missing

1. **A worklist.** `just report-hydrate-grounding` (#238) reports records already mapped; it does not report records the guard *refused*. The refusals emit a `refused_hydrate_on_non_hydrate_term` decision row in the batch CSV, but that is per-run and not aggregated.
2. **A minting path.** Something that takes a refused record plus its hydrate CAS and produces the Section 3 shape — essentially `anchor_cas_hydrate_records.py` generalised to records that do *not* yet have a `cas:` identifier, including looking the CAS up.

## Why it matters now rather than later

Before #246 these records were silently mis-mapped, which is worse. But "refused and untracked" is only better if something eventually tracks them — otherwise the hydrate residual grows invisibly instead of visibly, and the next person measures coverage, sees it fall, and has no explanation.

Suggested: extend `report_hydrate_grounding.py` with a REFUSED bucket sourced from the curated set (records whose label is a hydrate and whose status is UNMAPPED), so the worklist exists before the minting tool does.

Related: #246, #243, #239, #244, #218.
title: Records the hydrate guard refuses are stranded — nothing routes them to cas: minting

body:
Raised in review of #244; not a defect of that PR, which follows existing precedent.

MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md Section 1 is explicit that `skos:narrowMatch` means *"MIM:X is a kind-of Y"* and that **consumers MUST emit it as `biolink:subclass_of` / `rdfs:subClassOf`**. Section 3 step 2 then mandates `narrowMatch` from a salt or hydrate to its parent compound.

For a hydrate that is defensible — a heptahydrate arguably *is* a kind of the compound. For a **salt** it is not:

    EDTA tetrasodium tetrahydrate salt  --subclass_of-->  ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid

is false in ChEBI's own model. ChEBI relates salts to their parent acids with `has part` and `is conjugate base of`, **not** `is_a`. A downstream consumer obeying Section 1 will emit a subclass edge that the source ontology contradicts.

This is not new with #244 — **all 111 existing `cas:`+CHEBI records** use this pattern, and #244 is consistent with them. But the precedent has never been examined, and Section 3 has now written it down as policy, which makes it worth settling.

## Options

1. **Accept it** and document the deviation in Section 1 — say plainly that MIM's `narrowMatch` is "more specific than", not strict subsumption, and tell consumers not to emit a subclass edge for salt/hydrate rows.
2. **Use `closeMatch`** for salts, which Section 1 already defines as informational and non-substitutable. Cost: it carries no directional signal, and Rule B1's registry requirement is keyed on narrow/broadMatch, so those records would lose their registry row obligation.
3. **A new predicate** for the salt-of / hydrate-of relation. Most faithful, most work, and needs kg-microbe to understand it.

(1) is probably right, but it should be a stated decision rather than an unexamined default — the whole point of Section 3.

Related: #244, #237, #239.
title: narrowMatch for salts asserts a subclass relation ChEBI itself does not model

body:
Split out of #238 / PR #240, which fixed the *documentation* entry points only.

#240 corrected the skills and `/ground-or-propose-ingredient` so a curator reading them no longer grounds a hydrate onto its anhydrous parent. The **code** still does it:

- `src/mediaingredientmech/utils/chemical_normalizer.py:20-27,90-105` strips hydrates
- `scripts/llm_curate_unmapped.py:274-305` calls `accept_mapping(record, candidate, quality=…)` on the *normalized* candidate, then files the original as a `HYDRATE_FORM` synonym
- `scripts/batch_curate_unmapped.py:386-400` does the same

So #240's framing — "the next grounding sweep would have recreated the families" — is only true of the **manual** path. An automated run still produces exactly the bucket `just report-hydrate-grounding` measures (53 records today).

## Suggested fix

Normalization should stay — stripping is how you find the family. What must change is the acceptance step: after finding the family, search for the hydration state actually present before accepting the parent, and if no specific term exists, route to the `cas:`/mint path of MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md Section 3 rather than accepting the anhydrous term at `EXACT_MATCH`.

A cheaper interim guard: have those two scripts refuse to accept a mapping when the record's label carries hydrate notation and the candidate term's formula has no water — the same test `report_hydrate_grounding.py` uses — and emit the record for manual routing instead.

Related: #238, #240, #218, #225.
title: The automated curation path still implements strip-then-map

body:
Split out of #238 / PR #240.

`scripts/validate_id_label_correspondence.py` and `tests/test_id_label_plausibility.py` are on `check_vendored_sync.sh`'s **byte-identical** list, so the verdict cannot be added in this repo — it must land in `CultureBotAI/CultureMech` first, then `scripts/.vendored_canon_ref` gets bumped here. #240 tried to edit them directly and failed `vendored-sync`.

## It needs redesign, not just relocation

The obvious change — split `HYDRATE_RELAXED` out of `OK_ID_ONLY` into a warning — is **half wrong**. `chem_formula.compare_formulas` returns `HYDRATE_RELAXED` whenever the non-H/O *skeleton* matches and the full counts don't. That is **symmetric**:

| label | term | what it really is |
|---|---|---|
| `NiCl2 x 6 H2O` | CHEBI:34887 nickel dichloride | hydrate on an anhydrous term ✅ the case we want |
| `MgSO4` | CHEBI:31795 magnesium sulfate **heptahydrate** | **anhydrous label on a hydrate term** |
| `MnSO4 x 4 H2O` | CHEBI:131523 manganese(II) sulfate **hexa**hydrate | **wrong hydration state** |

A single verdict named `HYDRATE_ON_ANHYDROUS_TERM` whose detail reads *"label has waters of hydration that X lacks"* asserts the opposite of the facts for the last two, and prescribes the wrong remedy — Section 3's answer for those is a *different term*, not a `cas:` mint.

## Suggested design

Three verdicts, distinguished by comparing the water count on each side:

- `HYDRATE_ON_ANHYDROUS_TERM` — label has water, term has none
- `ANHYDROUS_ON_HYDRATE_TERM` — term has water, label has none
- `HYDRATION_STATE_MISMATCH` — both have water, different amounts

Each needs its own remediation text. All three should start in `_WARN_VERDICTS`, and all three need adding to the exception allow-list (`validate_id_label_correspondence.py:868-871` currently permits waivers only for `MISMATCH` / `ID_NOT_FOUND` / `IMPLAUSIBLE_LABEL` / `LABEL_SUBSCRIPTS_LOST`, so a curator would have no escape hatch) and to the summary loop at `:885-903`, which is hardcoded — a verdict missing from it is invisible to `just validate-products` and only recoverable via `just report-label-drift`.

Meanwhile `just report-hydrate-grounding` (#240) measures the population without touching vendored code.

Related: #238, #240, #218.
title: Land HYDRATE_ON_ANHYDROUS_TERM in the CultureMech hub — and redesign it first

body:
Found reviewing #237.

`MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md` Section 3 step 2 says a substance with no exact ontology term takes `cas:<its own CAS>` as its identifier, `narrowMatch` to the nearest ontology parent, **plus** the Rule B1 registry row.

Measured over `mappings/ingredient_mappings.sssom.tsv`:

- **34** hydrate-labelled subjects are fully compliant — `cas:` exactMatch + parent narrow/broadMatch + `kgmicrobe.*` registry row. These are the precedent Section 3 was written from.
- **22** more `cas:`-identified hydrate records have **no parent row and no registry row at all**: `Stachyose Hydrate`, `Maltotriose Hydrate`, `L-Rhamnose Monohydrate`, `EDTA tetrasodium tetrahydrate salt`, and others.

Those 22 became non-compliant with the convention the moment it landed. They are a backlog, not counter-examples — the identifier is right, the anchoring rows are missing.

## Why it is not urgent but should not be forgotten

Rule B1 is strict-by-default and makes CI fail on a *missing registry row for a subject that asserts narrowMatch*. These records assert no narrowMatch, so they slip through: they are invisible to the rule rather than violating it. That is the same shape as a check that looks healthiest when it has stopped working.

## Suggested fix

Add the parent narrowMatch + registry row for each, which is mechanical once the parent term is identified. Then consider whether Rule B1 (or a new rule) should also flag a `cas:`-identified record that anchors to no ontology parent at all — that is the invariant that would have caught these.

Related: #237, #218.
title: 22 cas: hydrate records lack the parent and registry rows Section 3 now requires

body:
Found reviewing #237. The convention landed but nothing that *produces* the data knows about it.

`MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md` Section 3 now says a hydrate takes its own identifier and narrowMatches the anhydrous parent. These still say the opposite:

| file | what it teaches |
|---|---|
| `.claude/skills/map-media-ingredients/SKILL.md:49` and `reference/examples-and-troubleshooting.md:9-31` | hydrate stripping, using literally the example Section 3 calls the bug: `MgSO4•7H2O` → strip → `CHEBI:32599`, quality `EXACT_MATCH` |
| `.claude/commands/ground-or-propose-ingredient.md:54-55` | "`FeSO4`, `FeSO4 x 7 H2O` and `iron(II) sulfate heptahydrate` are one compound; ground the anhydrous parent once and carry the hydrate as a `HYDRATE_FORM` synonym" |
| `scripts/validate_id_label_correspondence.py:409` | treats `HYDRATE_RELAXED` as a **PASS** |

So the next grounding sweep will keep creating exactly the 32 families #218 tracks, and the id↔label gate will keep approving them. Section 3 is unenforced policy until these move.

## Suggested fix

1. Rewrite the hydrate guidance in both skill files and the `/ground-or-propose-ingredient` command to the Section 3 decision procedure.
2. Decide what `HYDRATE_RELAXED` should do — under Section 3 a hydrate label against an anhydrous term is a finding, not a pass. Changing it to a warning first (report-then-enforce, as `id-label-correspondence` recommends) would show the true size before it blocks CI.
3. `check_instruction_refs.py` already catches instruction files naming recipes that do not exist (#185); it cannot catch instruction files teaching a superseded policy. Worth a note in the skill files pointing at MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md as the authority, so drift is at least visible.

Related: #237, #218, #225.
title: Curation entry points still teach the hydrate anti-pattern Section 3 forbids

body:
Found in review of #234.

The SSSOM `curie_map` expands `MIM:` to `.../data/ingredients/mapped/`, so `MIM:<slug>` is meant to address the per-record file. But `export_individual_records.FilenameIndex` **deliberately never renames an existing file** — it preserves the original stem so per-record paths stay stable.

So when a record's `preferred_term` changes, the SSSOM subject slug changes and the file stem does not:

    SSSOM subject: MIM:2-phenylethylamine
    file on disk:  data/ingredients/mapped/Phenethylamine_Hydrochloride.yaml

Measured on #234's branch: SSSOM subjects with no matching file stem went **7 → 8** (7 pre-existing, 1 added by that PR's relabel).

Nothing currently checks this. `reconcile_sssom.py` validates GAP/ORPHAN/STALE on `ontology_id` and never looks at the subject slug, which is why #234's "reconcile 0" reassurance did not cover it.

## Options

1. Teach `export_individual_records` to rename when `preferred_term` changes, and accept that per-record paths are not permanently stable.
2. Accept that `MIM:` slugs are opaque identifiers rather than file paths, and say so in the curie_map documentation — then the mismatch is not a defect.
3. Add a check that every `MIM:` subject resolves to a file, and fix the 7 pre-existing cases.

(2) is probably right — stable per-record paths are worth more than slug/path agreement — but it should be a stated decision, since today the curie_map implies (1).

Related: #234, #209.
title: Relabelling a record leaves its MIM: SSSOM subject pointing at a filename that no longer matches

body:
Raised in review of #234 and worth recording rather than waving off.

MIM's record now named `2-phenylethylamine` (CHEBI:18397) carries:

    cas_rn: 64-04-0
    data_source: CultureBotHT compounds_to_cas.csv

`64-04-0` is phenethylamine, the **free base**, and is ChEBI's own xref for CHEBI:18397. But the record's original `preferred_term` was **"Phenethylamine Hydrochloride"**. So CultureBotHT paired a hydrochloride catalogue name with a free-base CAS.

Two readings, and the record cannot distinguish them:

1. **The name was wrong** — the ingredient really is the free base, someone typed a salt name. #234 took this reading and renamed the record, because ChEBI has no phenethylamine hydrochloride term (the only `C8H11N.HCl` is CHEBI:191064, *N*-methylbenzylamine hydrochloride) and every other datum on the record is the free base.
2. **The CAS lookup was wrong** — the ingredient really is the hydrochloride (CAS 156-28-5) and CultureBotHT's name→CAS step dropped the salt. In that case the record should be a hydrate/salt-style grounding, not a rename.

#234 chose (1) and the stakes are low — the record has **0 occurrences**, so no medium depends on it. But the same `compounds_to_cas.csv` source feeds other records, and if its name→CAS step silently drops salt forms then other salt-named records may carry free-base CAS numbers.

## Worth checking

Scan records whose `chemical_properties.data_source` is `CultureBotHT compounds_to_cas.csv` for a `preferred_term` containing a salt/hydrate word (hydrochloride, sulfate, sodium salt, …) whose `cas_rn` resolves to the parent instead. That tells you whether this is one bad row or a systematic step.

Related: #234, #228, #218.
title: CHEBI:18397's cas 64-04-0 came from a salt catalogue name — verify the pairing

body:
Found reviewing #231.

`docs/data/ingredients.json` is the browser/Pages artifact, written by `scripts/browser_export.py` (via `just export-browser`). It is **committed and deployed**, and it is the artifact that *did* carry merged raw labels correctly while the CSV exports dropped them (#229).

Two gaps:

1. **It is stale.** 2876 records against 2877 in the curated collections — `TAPSO` is missing. Somebody regenerated the `export_lists.py` artifacts without `export-browser`, or vice versa.
2. **The new `qc-flat-coverage` gate does not cover it.** #231's freshness check regenerates and diffs the six `export_lists.py` outputs (all/mapped/unmapped × csv/json). `ingredients.json` comes from a different script and is excluded.

So the one artifact that was already doing the right thing is the one with no gate on it.

## Why it was left out of #231

`browser_export.py` may pull dependencies beyond stdlib + PyYAML, and `qc-flat-coverage.yaml` is deliberately a pip-install-plus-one-command job so it runs standalone rather than behind `just qc` (which needs OAK and the claw checkout, and never runs in CI — the lesson from #224). Adding it needs a check that the CI job stays cheap.

## Suggested fix

Extend the freshness check to regenerate `ingredients.json` too, or fold `export-browser` into whatever regenerates `docs/data/`, then commit the refreshed artifact. Worth doing together with #217's observation that `export_lists.py` was reachable from no recipe at all — the underlying pattern is that `docs/data/` has several producers and no single "regenerate everything published" entry point.

Related: #231, #229, #217.
title: docs/data/ingredients.json is stale and not covered by the freshness gate

body:
Found reviewing #231, which introduces the ambiguity by publishing synonyms.

Before #231, `docs/data/*.csv` carried only `preferred_term`, and **preferred_terms are unique** (verified: zero duplicates). So the CSV supported an unambiguous `{label: identifier}` join. Publishing synonyms makes that join order-dependent for **87 labels**.

The sharp cases are where **one record's `preferred_term` is another record's synonym** — a consumer's answer depends purely on row order:

| label | holders |
|---|---|
| `Vitamin B12` | CHEBI:176843 (preferred) / CHEBI:17439 (synonym) / UNMAPPED_0005 (synonym) |
| `Mannitol` | CHEBI:29864 (preferred) / CHEBI:16899 (synonym) |
| `Tryptophan` | CHEBI:27897 (preferred) / CHEBI:16828 (synonym) |
| `Citrate` | CHEBI:16947 (preferred) / CHEBI:30769 (synonym) |
| `Sulfur` | CHEBI:26833 (preferred) / CHEBI:17909 (synonym) |
| `Putrescine` | CHEBI:17148 (preferred) / cas:333-93-7 (synonym) |

…and ~12 more of that shape.

Some of these are the #218 family in another guise — `Citrate`/`Citric acid`, `Sulfur`, `Mannitol` are the same substance under two CHEBI ids, i.e. the inverse defect of #225. Others are legitimately shared synonyms where two distinct terms both accept a loose common name.

#231 does **not** treat this as a failure — a synonym legitimately can be shared, and failing the build on it would block the fix. The gate prints it as a note.

## What to decide

1. Which of the 87 are the #225/#218 inverse defect (one substance, two ids) and should be merged, versus genuinely-shared loose names.
2. For the genuine ones, whether the published surface should carry a precedence signal so a consumer can resolve deterministically — e.g. a `match_type` column distinguishing preferred_term from synonym, so `Vitamin B12` → CHEBI:176843 is the documented answer.

Until (2), consumers joining on the `synonyms` column should prefer a row whose `preferred_term` equals the query.

Related: #231, #229, #218, #225.
title: 87 published labels resolve to more than one identifier, including 18 preferred_term-vs-synonym collisions

body:
Noticed reviewing #227 (which added the third). Pre-existing; #227 did not cause it and the new mapping is correct.

Current state:

| record | identifier | ChEBI label |
|---|---|---|
| `Arabitol` | CHEBI:18403 | **L-arabinitol** |
| `Arabinitol` | CHEBI:22605 | **arabinitol** (stereo-unspecified parent) |
| `D-arabitol` | CHEBI:18333 | **D-arabinitol** |

`D-arabitol → CHEBI:18333` (added in #227) is right, and this is **not** the #225 inverse defect — the three CURIEs are genuinely distinct ChEBI terms.

The problem is `Arabitol`. Unqualified "arabitol" is a `hasRelatedSynonym` of **CHEBI:22605** (the stereo-unspecified parent), not of the L-form. Grounding it to CHEBI:18403 `L-arabinitol` asserts a stereochemistry the source label does not carry — and D-arabitol, not L-, is the biologically common one in microbial media (it is a standard Biolog carbon source).

So a medium listing plain "arabitol" is currently recorded as the L-enantiomer on no evidence.

## Why it is not a one-line fix

Retargeting `Arabitol` → CHEBI:22605 collides with the existing `Arabinitol` record, which already holds that id — two records, one CURIE, which `just qc-duplicate-ids` (#224) rejects. So it becomes a merge of `Arabitol` into `Arabinitol`, i.e. #226 territory (two MAPPED records, needing occurrence/role/SSSOM reconciliation).

Also worth checking whether MIM has other unqualified-vs-stereospecific pairs grounded the same way; `\`audit_duplicate_identifiers.py\`` will not catch these because the identifiers differ.

Related: #227, #226, #224.
title: Arabitol / Arabinitol / D-arabitol are three records across three stereochemical senses

body:
Found reviewing #227. Applies to #214's 9 merges as well, and the new `merge_unmapped_into_mapped.py` guarantees it repeats.

## The regression

A merge deletes the UNMAPPED record and adds its raw label as a `RAW_TEXT` synonym on the target. By design it adds **no SSSOM row** — SSSOM subjects are `preferred_term`s of MAPPED records, never synonyms (`reconcile_sssom.py:74-82`), so adding one would be reported ORPHAN.

But `docs/data/{all,mapped,unmapped}_ingredients.csv` have **no synonyms column**:

    identifier,ontology_id,preferred_term,mapping_status,ontology_label,ontology_source,mapping_quality,total_occurrences,media_count

So after a merge the raw label appears in **no flat artifact at all**. Only `docs/data/ingredients.json` (which has `synonyms`/`searchable`) and the YAML retain it.

## Failure scenario

A kg-microbe consumer joining raw ingredient strings against `docs/data/all_ingredients.csv` or `mappings/ingredient_mappings.sssom.tsv`:

- **before** #227: `D-lactate` → `UNMAPPED_0654` — resolves to "known ingredient, not yet grounded"
- **after**: `D-lactate` → **nothing**

Record-level coverage went *up* (the label is now grounded to CHEBI:16004) while flat-surface coverage went *down*. That is the opposite of the intended effect, and it is invisible to every current gate: reconcile is GAP/ORPHAN/STALE 0, roundtrip is clean, qc-duplicate-ids is clean.

Affected so far: 5 labels from #227 (`3-hydroxy 2-butanone`, `D-lactate`, `Iso-butanol`, `N-acetyl-neuraminic Acid`, `Trimethyleneglycol`) and 9 from #214 (`2-dichloropropane`, `1% Sodium Chloride`, `Peptones`, …).

## Options

1. **Add a synonyms column to `export_lists.py`** — smallest change, keeps SSSOM semantics intact, makes the CSVs self-sufficient for string resolution.
2. **Emit a synonym-subject SSSOM row** with a distinct predicate — richer, but needs `reconcile_sssom.py` and the invariant validator taught about non-preferred_term subjects, and a decision on the right predicate.
3. Accept it and document that raw-string resolution must go through `ingredients.json`.

Option 1 looks right. Whichever is chosen, a check that every `RAW_TEXT` synonym is resolvable from at least one published flat artifact would stop this recurring.

Related: #227, #214, #220.
title: Merging a raw label into an existing record removes it from every flat export and from SSSOM

body:
Found applying the Edison residual research in #227, which had to hold two groundings back because of this.

## The records

| record `identifier` | `preferred_term` | `ontology_label` | quality |
|---|---|---|---|
| CHEBI:18397 | **Phenethylamine Hydrochloride** | 2-phenylethylamine | `EXACT_MATCH` |
| CHEBI:64243 | **Sodium glutamate monohydrate** | monosodium L-glutamate | `EXACT_MATCH` |

In both the record names a **salt** or a **hydrate**, and the id is the anhydrous free form. Neither is an exact match:

- Phenethylamine hydrochloride is C8H11N·HCl; CHEBI:18397 is the free base C8H11N.
- Sodium glutamate monohydrate is C5H8NNaO4·H2O; CHEBI:64243 is the anhydrous salt. Different formula weight — the thing a medium recipe depends on, same class of problem as the hydrate families in #218/#225.

Verified against the local `chebi.db`: **CHEBI has no term** for `phenethylamine hydrochloride`, `2-phenylethylamine hydrochloride`, `sodium glutamate monohydrate` or `monosodium L-glutamate monohydrate`. So there is no drop-in correct id.

## Why it blocks work

Edison deep research over the microbedecoder residual resolved two unmapped labels to these exact ids:

- `Beta-phenylethylamine` → CHEBI:18397
- `Sodium L-glutamate` → CHEBI:64243

Both incoming labels are the **free base / unspecified-hydrate form** — i.e. each is a *better* match for the id than the record currently holding it. So the normal dispositions both fail:

- **Promote** → two records would hold one CURIE, which `just qc-duplicate-ids` (#224) now rejects.
- **Merge** into the existing record → files the free base as a synonym of a record labelled "Hydrochloride", compounding the original error.

#227 therefore held both back rather than guess.

## What needs deciding

For each pair, which record should own the CURIE, and what does the other become? Options: downgrade the salt/hydrate record to `CLOSE_MATCH` on the same id (blocked — one CURIE, one record), mint a `kgmicrobe.compound` term for the salt/hydrate, or map it to a non-CHEBI scheme that does have the salt.

This is the same shape as the 32 `HYDRATE_FAMILY_UNREVIEWED` rows in `mappings/duplicate_identifier_baseline.tsv` and should probably be settled with the same convention rather than case by case.

Related: #227, #218, #224, #225.
title: Two salt/hydrate records are mapped to the anhydrous free form as EXACT_MATCH, and block incoming better matches

body:
Follow-up to #218 / #224. #224 built the detection and triage; this is the execution.

`mappings/duplicate_identifier_baseline.tsv` now marks **15 groups `SAFE_MERGE`** — verified by reading the records, not inferred:

- pure spelling variants — `Glycerol`/`glycerol`, `Glycyl-glycine`/`Glycylglycine`, `Sea water`/`Seawater`, the two poly(L-lysine) spellings
- redundant stereo descriptors — `D-Sucrose`/`Sucrose`, `Glutathione`/`L-Glutathione`
- `X` vs `X (role annotation)` from the communitymech import — `Acetate (carbon source)`, `Ammonium chloride (nitrogen source)`, `Sodium nitrate (nitrogen source)`, `Sodium metasilicate (silicate for diatom frustules)`
- salt-name variants — `Ampicillin sodium salt`/`Na-ampicillin`, `Calcium D-Pantothenate`/`Calcium pantothenate`
- `Bacto X` vs `Bacto X (Difco)` — MICRO:0000113, MICRO:0000114
- CHEBI:16991 `Deoxyribonucleic acid from herring sperm`/`Fish-Sperm DNA` — one reagent

Precedent exists: CHEBI:63005 already carries a synonym sourced `merged_from_duplicate_mim_record`.

## Why this needs new tooling

No current script implements record-merge semantics. `promote_resolved_unmapped.py` promotes; `apply_microbedecoder_residual_merges.py` (#214) folds an **UNMAPPED** record into a mapped one, which is a different case — both records here are MAPPED and each may carry:

1. **occurrence_statistics** — `Glycerol` has 208/54, `glycerol` has 6/6. Summing `total_occurrences` is right; summing `media_count` over-counts if a medium lists both spellings. Needs a decision.
2. **role facets** — both `Glycerol` records carry roles; `Glycyl-glycine` has roles and `Glycylglycine` does not. Union, or keep the survivor's?
3. **SSSOM rows** — subjects are keyed on `preferred_term` of MAPPED records, so deleting the loser **orphans its row**. Both `MIM:Glycyl-glycine` and `MIM:Glycylglycine` currently exist; one must be removed or `reconcile_sssom` reports ORPHAN.
4. **survivor choice** — sometimes the record matching the canonical ontology_label has *fewer* occurrences (ENVO:00002149: `Sea water` matches the label but `Seawater` holds the occurrences and the SSSOM row).

Also relevant: the `merge-ingredients` skill documents marking the source `REJECTED` as a tombstone (#220), which #214 did not do. Worth settling once and applying to both paths.

Whatever is built should be dry-run-first, and afterwards the baseline must be refreshed (`--write-baseline`) since `qc-duplicate-ids` now fails on GONE entries by design.
title: Execute the 15 SAFE_MERGE duplicate-identifier groups (needs role/occurrence/SSSOM merge semantics)

body:
Found reviewing #224, which added detection for this.

#218 covers the forward defect — two records sharing one identifier. This is the **inverse**: one substance under two identifiers. `scripts/audit_duplicate_identifiers.py` now reports it (folding preferred_terms on case/punctuation and looking for names that map to more than one CURIE), but deliberately does not gate it, because some collisions are legitimate.

These are not legitimate:

| folded name | identifiers |
|---|---|
| `MgSO4·7H2O` / `MgSO47H2O` | **CHEBI:32599** and **CHEBI:31795** |
| `FeSO4 x 7 H2O` / `FeSO4 x 7H2O` | **CHEBI:75836** and **CHEBI:75832** |
| `MgCl2 x 6 H2O` / `MgCl2x 6 H2O` | **CHEBI:86345** and **CHEBI:6636** |
| `Glucose` / `glucose` | CHEBI:17234 and CHEBI:42758 |
| `Maltose` / `maltose` | CHEBI:17306 and CHEBI:18167 |

## Why this blocks the #218 hydrate work

`CHEBI:75832`, `CHEBI:6636`, `CHEBI:31795`, `CHEBI:86345` and `CHEBI:32599` are **all rows in `mappings/duplicate_identifier_baseline.tsv`**, dispositioned `HYDRATE_FAMILY_UNREVIEWED`.

So the same heptahydrate simultaneously:
- sits inside a multi-member family that still needs splitting onto distinct hydrate terms, **and**
- already exists under a second CHEBI id elsewhere in the collection.

Whoever executes "give each hydrate its own term" will collide with an id that is already in use for that hydrate, or mint a third. The two defects have to be worked together, and the hydrate families cannot be triaged in isolation.

## Suggested approach

Resolve the cross-identifier collisions **first** — decide the canonical CHEBI id per (salt, hydration state) — then split the families onto that settled set. The glucose/maltose pairs are a separate question (CHEBI:17234 glucose vs CHEBI:42758 aldehydo-D-glucose are genuinely different terms; whether both should be in use for media ingredients is a curation call).

`just qc-duplicate-ids` prints the current collision list on every run.
title: One substance under two CHEBI ids: the hydrate split has already been done inconsistently

body:
Follow-up to #168 (closed by #216).

#216 took the low-risk path: it sharpened the `DEFINED_MEDIUM` description to say the value denotes **record granularity** (a complete named medium), not the microbiology term of art "chemically defined medium". That removes the immediate docs hazard but leaves the **enum name** itself still reading as "chemically defined" to anyone who doesn't open the description.

The honest fix is a rename (e.g. `NAMED_MEDIUM` / `COMPLETE_MEDIUM` / `MEDIUM_FORMULATION`), but it is **cross-Mech**:
- CultureMech imports MIM's enums, so the token must change in lockstep (coordinate via culturebotai-claw / the vendored-schema path `mech_shared.yaml` if the enum lives there, or a synchronized rename if it is MIM-owned).
- 53 MIM records currently carry `DEFINED_MEDIUM`, and kg-microbe consumes the value — a rename needs a data migration + a consumer heads-up.

Decision needed: is the description-only clarification sufficient long-term, or do we schedule the coordinated rename? Not blocking; parked so it is not lost when #168 closes.
title: Consider renaming IngredientTypeEnum.DEFINED_MEDIUM (cross-Mech) — description clarified in #216

body:
Found reviewing #214.

`MappingStatusEnum` (`src/mediaingredientmech/schema/mediaingredientmech.yaml:597-612`) distinguishes:

- `NEEDS_EXPERT` — *"Requires expert domain knowledge"*
- `AMBIGUOUS` — *"Multiple possible interpretations"*
- `REJECTED` — *"Determined to be invalid or duplicate"*

`AMBIGUOUS` currently has **zero instances** across the repo.

#214 flags four parse-noise records `NEEDS_EXPERT`, but the recorded reason for one of them is literally the definition of `AMBIGUOUS`:

> `2-tetrachloroethane` — reachable from both 1,1,1,2- (CHEBI:34024) and 1,1,2,2-tetrachloroethane (CHEBI:36026); no unique reconstruction

No amount of domain expertise recovers information that is not in the string — the locant was destroyed by a CSV comma-split upstream. That is "multiple possible interpretations", not "needs an expert".

The other three (`0129 (2`, `4-Diamino-6`, `4-diol`) are irrecoverable fragments of labels that were split mid-name; arguably `REJECTED` ("invalid"), since the string is not an ingredient name at all.

I kept `NEEDS_EXPERT` in #214 to match what closed PR #201 recorded, rather than silently diverge from the reviewed manifest — but the status is doing double duty and the distinction the schema draws is being lost.

## Why it matters

These statuses are the queue discipline: `NEEDS_EXPERT` implies *route to a human who knows the domain*, `AMBIGUOUS` implies *the label itself is under-determined — go back to the source*, `REJECTED` implies *stop looking*. Collapsing them means the residual can't be triaged by status, and an enum with no instances is effectively dead.

## Suggested fix

Decide whether `AMBIGUOUS` is real. If yes, move `2-tetrachloroethane` to it and `0129 (2` / `4-Diamino-6` / `4-diol` to `REJECTED`, and say in the schema description when each applies. If no, drop it from the enum so it stops looking like an available option.

The upstream fix for all four is #204-adjacent: the microbedecoder import splits labels on commas, which is what produced them.
title: AMBIGUOUS has zero instances repo-wide; parse-noise records are filed NEEDS_EXPERT instead

body:
Found reviewing #214.

The repo's own documented merge procedure — `.claude/skills/merge-ingredients/reference/matching-strategies.md:54-56` — is *"Mark source as REJECTED … Preserves audit trail"*, and the schema has `REJECTED: "Determined to be invalid or duplicate"` for exactly this. Two REJECTED tombstones already live in the mapped collection, so the pattern is in use.

`scripts/apply_microbedecoder_residual_merges.py` instead removes the source record outright. Synonyms and `preferred_term` are carried onto the target and `occurrence_statistics` were `0/0`, but the `notes` field is not — and that is where the upstream key lives:

    notes: Imported from microbedecoder (source_id=kgmicrobe.trait:2_dichloropropane)

Compare two records from the *same* `microbedecoder_residual_locant_fixed.tsv` batch after #211 and #214:

- `CHEBI:27789` (UNMAPPED_0722, **promoted**) → `notes: Imported from microbedecoder (source_id=kgmicrobe.trait:2_dichloroethane)`
- `CHEBI:142468` (UNMAPPED_0784, **merged**) → `notes: None`

So `kgmicrobe.trait:2_dichloropropane → CHEBI:142468` now exists nowhere in the data, while 826 other records carry their `kgmicrobe.trait` source_id. Same for `2_trichloroethane`, `1_sodium_chloride`, `1_sodium_lactate`, and the five re-routed in #214's second commit. MIM publishes to kg-microbe, so the trait id is the join key back to the source.

Related asymmetry, worth a decision rather than a fix: promoted records get an SSSOM row keyed on `preferred_term`, merged ones get none (SSSOM subjects are never synonyms — `reconcile_sssom.py:74-82`). A consumer resolving raw microbedecoder labels through the SSSOM resolves `2-dichloroethane` and silently misses `2-dichloropropane`. Defensible — the target is already mapped — but it means four rows of one manifest batch got two different treatments.

## Suggested fix

Either carry the source `notes`/source_id onto the merge target (e.g. as an additional evidence item or appended note), or tombstone as REJECTED per the documented procedure instead of deleting. Then make the merge helper and the skill doc agree, since they currently don't.
title: Merging deletes the source record instead of tombstoning it, dropping its kgmicrobe.trait source_id

body:
Found reviewing #214.

`justfile:367-368`:

    gen-docs:
        gen-doc --directory docs ...

`gen-doc` is invoked **bare**, not under `uv run`, so it resolves to whatever is on PATH rather than the pinned dependency:

- `which gen-doc` → `/opt/homebrew/Caskroom/miniforge/base/bin/gen-doc`, `gen-doc --version` → **1.10.0**
- `pyproject.toml:30` pins `linkml>=1.7.0,<1.10`; `uv.lock` resolves **1.9.3**

So the recipe runs a version the project explicitly excludes.

## Effect

Running `just build-docs` (which calls `gen-docs`) rewrote ~200 files under `docs/`, about 5,000 lines, as pure template restructuring — `* Range: X` became `### Type and Range` tables, `## Type Properties` blocks appeared — with **no schema change**. See `docs/Boolean.md`, `docs/mapping_status.md`.

Two consequences:

1. Any curation PR that regenerates docs carries 5,000 lines of unrelated diff, burying the real change. #214's first pass was 258 files / 28.6k lines for a 64-record curation change; dropping `gen-docs` took it to 88 files.
2. It ping-pongs. The next person who runs it under the pinned 1.9.3 reverts all of it, and back again — with the committed state depending on whose PATH won.

Every other recipe that runs Python tooling uses `uv run`; this one is the outlier.

## Suggested fix

    gen-docs:
        uv run --extra dev gen-doc --directory docs ...

then regenerate once, in its own commit, so the churn lands separately from curation work. Worth grepping the justfile for other bare tool invocations at the same time.
title: just gen-docs runs gen-doc outside the lockfile, rewriting ~200 schema pages with template churn

body:
Found reviewing #214, which had to work around it.

`data/curated/mapped_ingredients.yaml` holds more than one MAPPED record for the same identifier:

| identifier | records |
|---|---|
| `MICRO:0000178` | `preferred_term: Bacto peptone` **and** `preferred_term: Peptone` |

and the same ingredient under two different identifier schemes:

| ingredient | records |
|---|---|
| glycogen | `CHEBI:28087` (`Glycogen`) **and** `cas:9005-79-2` |

In MIM the record `identifier` **is** the ontology mapping CURIE, so two records with one CURIE are two records claiming to be the same term. The CHEBI/cas pair is the dual-identifier case `review-ingredients` is meant to catch.

## Why it bites

Any tool that indexes records by identifier — the obvious `{r['identifier']: r for r in ...}` — silently keeps whichever record comes last. #214 merges raw labels into existing mapped records, so a last-wins lookup would have attached `Peptones` and `Peptone (0.01 %` to whichever peptone record happened to sort last, with a `curation_history` entry asserting the merge was deliberate. It now resolves targets by CURIE **and** `preferred_term` and raises on ambiguity, but that is a guard around the defect, not a fix.

`reconcile_sssom.py` keys SSSOM subjects off `preferred_term` of MAPPED records, so a duplicated CURIE also means two SSSOM subjects pointing at one object.

## Suggested fix

Merge each pair with the `merge-ingredients` procedure — keep the ontology-backed record (`CHEBI:28087`, and one of the two peptone records), fold the other's synonyms and occurrence statistics in, tombstone the loser. Then add a `qc` assertion that no identifier appears twice across the mapped collection; that invariant is cheap and nothing currently checks it.
title: Two mapped records share MICRO:0000178, and glycogen is mapped twice (CHEBI:28087 and cas:9005-79-2)

body:
Found reviewing #214.

`scripts/export_lists.py` regenerates the six published backlog artifacts under `docs/data/`:

- `all_ingredients.{csv,json,md}`
- `mapped_ingredients.{csv,json,md}`
- `unmapped_ingredients.{csv,json,md}`

It is referenced by **no** justfile recipe, no GitHub workflow, and no documented procedure. `build-docs` is `gen-docs export-browser` (justfile:364) — `gen-docs` writes the LinkML *schema* pages and `export-browser` writes only `docs/data/ingredients.json`. So the six list artifacts are refreshed only when a curator happens to remember to run the script by hand.

## Failure

In the first pass of #214 I ran `just export-individual && just build-docs`, which is the documented path, and still shipped `docs/data/unmapped_ingredients.csv` containing rows for four records the same commit had deleted:

    UNMAPPED_0721,,1% Sodium Chloride,UNMAPPED,,,,0,0
    UNMAPPED_0784,...

…plus 60 records listed as `UNMAPPED` after being moved to `NEEDS_EXPERT`. `docs/data/ingredients.json` *was* regenerated, so files in the same directory contradicted each other.

This is the same failure shape as #148/#169: a generated artifact with no wired-up producer looks maintained and isn't. `docs/data/unmapped_ingredients.csv` is the human-facing triage list, so a stale copy sends a curator to work records that no longer exist.

Independent evidence it drifts: `docs/data/ingredients.json` on `main` held 2,340 records (MAPPED 1860 / UNMAPPED 477) while the curated YAML held 2,886 — it had been stale since a dedicated "Regenerate docs/" commit, i.e. this has already happened at least once and was fixed by hand.

## Suggested fix

Fold `export_lists.py` into `build-docs`, and add a `qc` check that regenerating `docs/data/` produces no diff — the same freshness assertion `qc-roundtrip` makes for `data/curated` vs `data/ingredients`. A generated file that CI never re-derives will drift again.
title: export_lists.py is invoked from no recipe, so docs/data/ goes stale silently

body:
The residual of #197, still live after #205 restored the 11 records and #199 added the currency check. Both of those treated symptoms; the ceiling that produced them is unchanged.

## The number is wrong for CHEBI, and only for CHEBI

`conf/id_label_targets.yaml`:

```yaml
max_accession:
  CHEBI: 300000
  FOODON: 4000000
  UBERON: 9000000
  ENVO: 9000000
  NCIT: 900000
```

CHEBI's is an order of magnitude below every sibling, and it is below CHEBI's own real range: the local `chebi.db` reaches accession **747618**, and ChEBI keeps minting above that. So the ceiling does not describe CHEBI's accession space — it describes a guess that was already stale when it was written.

## What it actually does

The verdict is correct in structure. `validate_id_label_correspondence.py:492-496` only reaches the ceiling when the id did **not** resolve, so a locally-resolving high accession passes; the ceiling is a tie-breaker on ids that already failed. The heuristic's genuine purpose is real — it separates a PubChem CID wearing a `CHEBI:` prefix (8 digits) from a retired accession.

But at 300000, a valid ChEBI term that merely postdates the local build lands in the same bucket as a foreign identifier, and gets told so in those words: *"a foreign identifier wearing an OBO prefix."* That wording is what invited the destructive response in #193 — 17 real terms demoted, 11 of which resolved locally the whole time.

The six still held (`CHEBI:756054`, `759883`, `759884`, `753395`, `748901`, `759086`) are in exactly that state today: real per OLS4, unresolvable locally, above 300000, therefore reported as foreign identifiers.

## The fix does not weaken anything

Raise the CHEBI ceiling to `999999`, above ChEBI's real 6-digit range and below the 8 digits PubChem reaches.

Both `ID_NOT_FOUND` and `ID_OUT_OF_RANGE` are already **fatal** (`scripts/validate_id_label_correspondence.py:131`, and the comment at 743-744 says `ID_OUT_OF_RANGE` "is a strictly better diagnosis of an id that already failed as `ID_NOT_FOUND`"). So nothing that fails today starts passing. The only thing that changes is which of two fatal verdicts a curator sees — and therefore whether the tool tells them "this identifier is fake, delete it" or "this identifier did not resolve here."

Checked against the counter-example #197 raised: `CHEBI:867561` (from #170) is genuinely bogus and returns NOT FOUND from OLS4. At 999999 it reports `ID_NOT_FOUND` rather than `ID_OUT_OF_RANGE` — still caught, still fatal, just no longer accused of being a PubChem CID, which it also is not.

## Tasks

- [ ] Raise `CHEBI` to `999999` in `conf/id_label_targets.yaml`, with a comment recording that the number tracks *PubChem's* digit count, not a guess at ChEBI's ceiling — so the next person knows what would justify changing it.
- [ ] Re-run `just validate-products` and confirm the six held records move from `ID_OUT_OF_RANGE` to `ID_NOT_FOUND` and remain fatal.
- [ ] Soften the `ID_OUT_OF_RANGE` message so it states the evidence ("did not resolve, and the accession is above CHEBI's range") rather than the conclusion ("a foreign identifier"). The conclusion is an inference, and #193 shows what happens when a curator acts on it as though it were a finding.
- [ ] Add a regression test pinning that a resolvable above-ceiling id passes and an unresolvable 8-digit one still reports `ID_OUT_OF_RANGE`.

Note this file is vendored byte-identical across the four Mech repos — `conf/id_label_targets.yaml` may not be, but confirm before editing, and if the script needs touching it goes through `CultureBotAI/CultureMech` first.

Related: #197, #198, #200, #205, #207, #170.
title: The CHEBI accession ceiling is 300000 while CHEBI reaches 747618 — valid terms get called foreign identifiers

body:
Follow-up from the review of #199 (PR #199, `scripts/check_chebi_currency.py`).

`refresh_would_help()` decides whether re-downloading the semsql ChEBI build
would change anything by comparing the published artifact's `Content-Length`
against the local `.gz`. Equal size ⇒ same build ⇒ refresh is a no-op.

That inference is a proxy, not a proof. It cannot distinguish two builds that
happen to compress to the same length, and it reports "a refresh WOULD change
the build" for any rebuild of the *same* release whose bytes shifted.

It is deliberately the safe direction — a false "would help" costs one 760 MB
download, whereas a false "would not help" would leave someone stuck behind with
no prompt to act. And it is the strongest signal available without downloading
the artifact, which is the whole cost the check exists to avoid.

**What would actually settle it:** the semsql publisher exposes no version
endpoint we currently read. Options, roughly in order of effort:

- Range-request the first N kB of `chebi.db.gz` and read `owl:versionInfo` out of
  the decompressed prefix — gzip is streamable, so this is likely a few hundred
  kB rather than 760 MB. Needs checking that S3 honours `Range` here and that
  the `statements` row lands early enough in the file.
- Compare `ETag`/`Last-Modified` against a recorded value from the last refresh,
  which detects *change* precisely without identifying the release.

Not urgent: the current behaviour is correct in the state that actually obtains
(published == local == 252), and wrong only in the cheap direction.
title: check-chebi-currency infers 'a refresh would help' from byte size, not release

body:
Found reviewing #195 before merge.

`scripts/promote_microbedecoder_reviewed.py` promotes `PENDING_REVIEW` groundings to `MAPPED` and publishes their SSSOM rows. Its entire approval criterion is:

```python
lbl = ad[prefix].label(oid)
if lbl is None: skipped...
if lbl.strip().lower() != mrow["ontology_label"].strip().lower(): skipped...
```

It checks that the id resolves and that its canonical label equals **the label the import already stored for that id** — and that label came from the same OLS lookup that produced the grounding. **The check closes on itself.**

Measured: across all 386 rows, `normalize(subject_label) == normalize(object_label)` for **386/386**. Re-running the script in dry-run against the pre-promotion tree gives `to promote (verified): 386, skipped: 0`. A gate with a 100% pass rate on the exact population it was written for isn't a review — it re-derives the identity that created the mapping, so it would approve any wrong grounding whose id resolves, which is every `ols-label-exact` grounding by construction.

## It is not hypothetical — one wrong grounding got through

`MIM:Sulfonamide → CHEBI:35358` was approved. `CHEBI:35358 "sulfonamide"` is the **structural functional-group** class with **2976 direct subclasses**, spanning diuretics and herbicides. The record's provenance is `kgmicrobe.trait:sulfonamide` — an antibiotic-resistance trait — so the intended target is `CHEBI:87228 "sulfonamide antibiotic"` (24 subclasses).

Since `skos:exactMatch` licenses node substitution, publishing it would let kg-microbe collapse every sulfonamide-resistance edge onto the functional-group node, making furosemide a sibling of sulfamethoxazole under an asserted identity. Held at `PENDING_REVIEW` in #195 with its SSSOM row withdrawn.

## The wider exposure

The same batch publishes `skos:exactMatch` to other class-level terms, uniformly and without anyone deciding: `CHEBI:3098` bile acid (415 subclasses), `CHEBI:25000` lactone (164), `CHEBI:23066` cephalosporin (111), `CHEBI:26401` purines (92), `CHEBI:33709` amino acid (57), plus cytochrome, Collagen, Fibrin, cyclodextrin, carrageenan.

In fairness, most of those MIM subjects are themselves kg-microbe *traits*, so class↔class `exactMatch` is often right. The problem is that nothing distinguished the cases — sulfonamide is where the uniform default was wrong, and no mechanism would have caught a second one.

Related oddity for a curator: `Netilmycin → CHEBI:7528` was promoted while `Netilmicin → CHEBI:748901` was demoted — one drug, two records, opposite treatment. Same shape for `Cyclodextrin`/`Gamma-cyclodextrin` and `Polymyxin`/`Polymyxin B`.

## Suggested

1. A homonym/specificity check: flag any object whose direct-subclass count exceeds a threshold, or whose label is a strict prefix of a sibling's (`X` vs `X antibiotic`), for human verdict rather than auto-approval.
2. `FAILED_ROUNDTRIP` is documented in the script's docstring but never written anywhere — the one failure mode the manifest exists to record is the one it cannot record. Implement it or drop it from the docs.
3. The script stamps `--date` as `T00:00:00`, producing history entries dated *before* the record was created. Use a real timestamp.
title: promote_microbedecoder_reviewed.py's approval check is tautological — it re-runs the lookup that created the mapping

body:
Found while grounding the microbedecoder UNMAPPED residual (the free normalized/fuzzy pass on `feat/microbedecoder-residual-grounding`).

The #193 import demoted 17 auto-groundings to `UNMAPPED` as "SUSPECT_ID_OUT_OF_RANGE" — CHEBI ids above the `conf/id_label_targets.yaml` `max_accession: CHEBI: 300000` ceiling. On inspection, **11 of the 17 are valid, current CHEBI terms that resolve in the local `chebi.db`** and were demoted purely for their accession number:

`CHEBI:338412` (-)-anisomycin · `CHEBI:474053` cefazolin · `CHEBI:478164` cefepime · `CHEBI:472657` cefixime · `CHEBI:355510` cefotiam · `CHEBI:404903` ertapenem · `CHEBI:471744` imipenem · `CHEBI:495056` gamma-cyclodextrin · `CHEBI:747004/747005` 1-chloropropane/1-chlorobutane · `CHEBI:546840` 4-nitrophenyl alpha-D-galactoside

## Root cause

Two different range rules disagree:

- **The id↔label gate** (`scripts/validate_id_label_correspondence.py`) only returns `ID_OUT_OF_RANGE` when the id **does not resolve** AND is above the ceiling (the ceiling is a tie-breaker for *unresolvable* ids — "a PubChem CID wearing a CHEBI prefix"). A locally-resolving above-ceiling id passes as `OK_CANONICAL`. Correct.
- **The import's demotion logic** applied the ceiling as a *hard cap* regardless of resolution, so it demoted resolvable terms the gate would have accepted.

The local `chebi.db` reaches accession **747618**; modern CHEBI legitimately issues ids far above 300000. The ceiling number cannot by itself distinguish a real `CHEBI:759086` from a foreign CID — resolution is the real test, which is exactly what the gate already does.

## Done in the grounding branch
Re-promoted the 11 to MAPPED (all `EXACT_MATCH`, id↔label gate green). No config change was needed because the gate already accepts them.

## Suggested fix (import path)
Align the importer's demotion with the gate: demote on **(above ceiling AND unresolvable)**, not on the ceiling alone. Otherwise every future import re-demotes valid high-accession CHEBI terms.

## Still genuinely blocked (separate, not fixed here)
6 ids exceed local coverage (>747618) — valid & current in OLS but absent from the local `chebi.db`, so they cannot pass the local gate until the db is refreshed: `CHEBI:756054` carbomycin · `CHEBI:759883` colistin sulfate · `CHEBI:759884` gentamicin · `CHEBI:753395` lysostaphin · `CHEBI:748901` netilmicin · `CHEBI:759086` polymyxin B. Triage TSV: `mappings/microbedecoder_demoted_antibiotics_triage.tsv`. These stay demoted pending a `chebi.db` refresh (or an OLS fallback in the gate).
title: microbedecoder import over-demoted 11 valid CHEBI antibiotics via a stale 300000 accession ceiling

body:
Cleanup owed from #193, caused by #197.

During the microbedecoder onboarding I demoted 17 auto-grounded records from `MAPPED` to `UNMAPPED`, recording a `DEMOTED_TO_UNMAPPED` event on each that says the id is "the signature of a foreign identifier wearing an OBO prefix".

**That reason is false.** All 17 ids are real, non-obsolete ChEBI terms (verified against live OLS4 — see #197). They failed only because the local ChEBI build is stale and the `CHEBI: 300000` ceiling then reclassified the non-resolution.

## What needs undoing

For each of the 17: restore `ontology_mapping` (the id and label are preserved in the `DEMOTED_TO_UNMAPPED` history entry and in the record `identifier`), set `mapping_status` back to `PENDING_REVIEW` so they rejoin the review cohort rather than jumping straight to `MAPPED`, and append a correcting event — the existing one must stay, since curation history is append-only and the erroneous reasoning is part of the record.

Affected: cefazolin, cefepime, cefixime, cefotiam, ertapenem, imipenem, gentamicin, netilmicin, polymyxin B, colistin sulfate, carbomycin, anisomycin, lysostaphin, 1-chlorobutane, 1-chloropropane, 4-nitrophenyl α-D-galactoside, gamma-cyclodextrin.

## Blocked on #197

Restoring them before the adapter/ceiling is fixed just makes `just validate-products` fail again — the gate will re-reject the same 17. Sequence: #197 first, then this.

## Two related corrections

- These 17 are **not "all antibiotics"**, a claim I repeated in #192, #193's commit message and PR body, and a history record. It is 12 of 17 — 1-chlorobutane, 1-chloropropane, 4-nitrophenyl α-D-galactoside and γ-cyclodextrin are not antibiotics, and lysostaphin is a bacteriolytic endopeptidase. Anyone using that summary to prioritise review would mis-batch them.
- The 17 also still carry the rejected CHEBI CURIE as their record `identifier` — the only 17 of 626 records in `unmapped/` not using an `UNMAPPED_NNNN` placeholder. If #197 resolves in favour of the ids being valid, the identifiers are correct as-is and nothing further is needed; if not, they need re-minting.

A corrected manifest marking these 17 `DEMOTED_IN_ERROR_RESTORE` with the OLS evidence exists but is not committed — #194 still carries the superseded `SUSPECT_ID_OUT_OF_RANGE` labelling.
title: Restore the 17 microbedecoder records I demoted on a false positive

body:
`conf/id_label_targets.yaml` sets `max_accession: CHEBI: 300000`. The validator treats an id that **does not resolve locally AND sits above the ceiling** as "a foreign identifier wearing an OBO prefix".

During the microbedecoder onboarding (#193) that rule rejected 17 groundings as `ID_OUT_OF_RANGE`, and I acted on it — demoting all 17 to `UNMAPPED`. **That was wrong.**

## Verified against live OLS4

All 17 are **real, non-obsolete ChEBI terms with exactly the labels claimed**:

| id | label |
|---|---|
| `CHEBI:474053` | cefazolin |
| `CHEBI:759883` | colistin sulfate |
| `CHEBI:747005` | 1-chlorobutane |
| `CHEBI:495056` | gamma-cyclodextrin |
| …and 13 more | cefepime, cefixime, cefotiam, ertapenem, imipenem, gentamicin, netilmicin, polymyxin B, carbomycin, anisomycin, lysostaphin, 1-chloropropane, 4-nitrophenyl α-D-galactoside |

They fail only because the **local ChEBI sqlite build is stale** and cannot resolve them, and the ceiling then reclassifies the non-resolution as "foreign identifier".

## The heuristic is not worthless

Checked the same way, #170's `CHEBI:867561` (Sodium L-lactate's identifier) returns **NOT FOUND** from OLS4 — genuinely bogus, correctly caught. So the rule catches real problems; it just cannot distinguish "invalid id" from "valid id my local ontology copy predates".

## Why this matters beyond 17 records

ChEBI keeps minting accessions above 300000. As-is, this gate will reject **every future grounding to a recent ChEBI term**, and the failure presents as "foreign identifier" — which invites exactly the destructive response I took.

## Options

1. **Refresh the local ChEBI adapter** — addresses the root cause; the ceiling then only fires on ids that genuinely don't exist anywhere.
2. **Fall back to OLS4 before declaring ID_OUT_OF_RANGE** — a non-resolving id above the ceiling gets one live lookup before being called foreign. Slower, but it is the check that would have prevented this.
3. Raise the ceiling — cheapest, but it weakens the one signal that correctly caught #170.

(1) or (2). Related: #170, #193, #195.
title: The CHEBI accession ceiling mis-rejects valid recent terms — 17 false positives, verified against live OLS4

body:
Found during the #192 review (see PR #195) of the microbedecoder auto-groundings.

All 386 microbedecoder-derived records (now promoted to MAPPED) carry:

```yaml
occurrence_statistics:
  total_occurrences: 0
  media_count: 0
```

But the source `unmapped_labels.tsv` carried real occurrence counts — e.g. `esculin` 3569, `D-glucose` 3377, `indole` 6005 — which is exactly the signal the onboarding assessment used to rank the 1,023 candidates.

## Is this a bug or correct-by-definition?

Defensible either way, which is why this is a flag, not a fix in #195:

- **Correct-by-definition:** MIM's `occurrence_statistics` counts **CultureMech media recipes** containing the ingredient. These labels come from BacDive traits / Bergey substrates, not media recipes, so `media_count: 0` is accurate and there is no CultureMech occurrence to record.
- **Signal loss:** even so, `total_occurrences: 0` discards the microbedecoder graph-occurrence entirely. Anything downstream that weights ingredients by prevalence now sees 386 zero-weight entries, and the abundance ranking that made this source worth onboarding is not retained anywhere in the record.

## Options for the maintainer

1. Leave as-is (occurrence = CultureMech-media-only, by definition).
2. Have `import_ingredients.py` carry the microbedecoder `occurrences` into a distinct field (e.g. a source-scoped `source_occurrences` or an evidence note) so the prevalence signal survives without overloading `media_count`.

No action taken in #195 — that PR only reviews and promotes the groundings.
title: microbedecoder-imported records carry total_occurrences: 0 — source occurrence signal is dropped

body:
Outstanding curation from the microbedecoder onboarding (kg-microbe `data/transformed/microbedecoder/unmapped_labels.tsv`).

The import auto-grounded 403 labels via `ols-label-exact-chebi` / `-ncit`. Rather than publish those on automated label matching alone, they are held at **`mapping_status: PENDING_REVIEW`** — the schema's own "Suggested mapping awaiting review". `reconcile_sssom.py` only publishes `MAPPED` records, so they are structurally barred from the published SSSOM until a reviewer flips the status.

- **386** at `PENDING_REVIEW` awaiting review
- **17** already rejected by the blocking id↔label gate and demoted to `UNMAPPED` (see below)
- Manifest: `reports/microbedecoder_auto_mapped_review.tsv` — one row per record with `ontology_id`, `ontology_label`, resolver method, and a `review_verdict` column

## Why this is not a rubber stamp

The gate rejected **17 of 403 (4%)** outright: CHEBI accessions above the 300000 ceiling in `conf/id_label_targets.yaml` that do not resolve in the local ChEBI adapter — `CHEBI:759086` (polymyxin B), `CHEBI:756054` (carbomycin), `CHEBI:759883` (colistin sulfate), `CHEBI:759884` (gentamicin), `CHEBI:753395` (lysostaphin), `CHEBI:748901` (netilmicin), and 11 more. **All antibiotics**, which suggests a systematic resolver problem on that class rather than scattered bad luck — worth checking whether the remaining antibiotic groundings in the 386 share it.

That is the same signature as this repo's earlier incidents: a PubChem CID wearing a `CHEBI:` prefix, and `CHEBI:86457` standing in for "MnCl·4H₂O".

## Suggested approach

`review-ingredients` over the manifest, prioritising:

1. The antibiotic rows, given 100% of the rejected ids were antibiotics.
2. Rows whose `ontology_label` differs from `preferred_term` by more than case — an exact-label match that needed normalising is where a homonym slips through.
3. Everything else in bulk.

Flip reviewed records to `MAPPED`, then `python scripts/reconcile_sssom.py --apply --date <YYYY-MM-DD>` publishes only those.

Blocked on nothing. Depends on #191 only in the sense that any further import should not be run until the write-back is fixed.
title: Review the 386 PENDING_REVIEW microbedecoder auto-groundings before they reach the SSSOM

body:
Found while onboarding the kg-microbe `microbedecoder` source.

`culturebotai-claw/scripts/import_ingredients.py` writes new ingredient YAMLs to `MIM_INGREDIENTS/{mapped,unmapped}/` and **never touches `data/curated/`**:

```python
MIM_INGREDIENTS = Path(".../MediaIngredientMech/data/ingredients")
MAPPED_DIR   = MIM_INGREDIENTS / "mapped"
UNMAPPED_DIR = MIM_INGREDIENTS / "unmapped"
```

Since `just export-individual` projects the collection **over** the per-record tree, the next export reverts everything an import created. That is exactly the mechanism that silently reverted 55 curation events (#148), and exactly the defect #171 fixed for `apply_role_research_results.py` — except this one sits in **the primary intake path for every new ingredient in the repo**.

## Reproduced, not theorised

Applying the microbedecoder source created 634 records, and then:

```
$ just qc-roundtrip
✗ Round-trip integrity check failed   (exit 1)
```

`just sync-curated` closed it. But nothing in the import path tells you to run it — I only knew because #167 added the gate that catches it.

## Why it went unnoticed until now

Before #167 there was no round-trip gate, so an import would desync the two surfaces silently and the next export would quietly undo it. Every historical import has had this shape; the damage was invisible because nobody ran a full export afterwards.

## Suggested fix

Mirror #178: have the importer call the write-back itself after a successful `--apply`, so a run leaves the tree consistent. In MIM terms that is `aggregate_records.py --output-dir data/curated` followed by `export_individual_records.py`, i.e. what `just sync-curated` does.

The importer lives in **culturebotai-claw**, so the code change is there; filing here because this is where the damage lands and where the tracking lives (same arrangement as #138).

## Related, found alongside

`MIM_INGREDIENTS` was a hardcoded absolute path, so an import always wrote into whatever branch the primary MediaIngredientMech checkout had out — which, when the work lives on a worktree branch, is the wrong one and lands 634 files invisibly in someone else's working tree. I added a `MIM_INGREDIENTS_DIR` environment override on claw branch `feat/microbedecoder-ingredient-source`; that half is done but unmerged.
title: claw's import_ingredients.py writes only per-record, never data/curated — the #171 defect in the primary intake path

body:
Found by the new instruction-reference check (#185).

`.claude/skills/merge-ingredients/SKILL.md` step 4 says:

> **Document flagged records** in `data/curation/flagged_duplicates.yaml` (chebi_id, record indices, reason, reviewer, resolution).

Neither `data/curation/` nor that file exists, and `git log` shows no trace of either. So an agent that merges records and dutifully "documents the flagged ones" writes to a path nothing reads, or creates a one-off directory outside every existing convention.

## Why this needs a decision rather than a path fix

The repo has since grown two surfaces that plausibly own this:

- **`history/`** (added #163) — append-only provenance, one record per session per target, scaffolded with `just new-history`. Built for exactly "which model changed what, why, under which issue".
- **`discussions:`** on the record itself — the `Discussion` supertype with `kind: CURATION_TODO` / `OPEN_QUESTION`, already carried by 8 records.

A flagged-but-unresolved duplicate is arguably a `Discussion(kind=OPEN_QUESTION)` on the surviving record, which would make it visible in the discussions browser and the knowledge-gap scan rather than sitting in a file nobody reads. But that's a curation-workflow call, not a docs fix.

## Live relevance

This isn't hypothetical: there are **61 duplicate identifier primary keys across 86 mapped records** (tracked in `NEXT_TASKS.md`), and working them will produce exactly these flags — some are clean merges, some are distinct compounds sharing an imprecise CAS, at least one is a narrowMatch judgment. Whoever picks that up needs a real place to record the "flagged, not merged" cases.

Suppressed inline with `<!-- refcheck: ignore -->` so the check stays green; remove that marker as part of the fix.
title: merge-ingredients skill directs flagged duplicates to data/curation/, which does not exist
